A1 given answer

parts.label: b

parts.label: a

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 2x − 1 to find the exact value of ∫₁⁵ x/√(2x − 1) dx.
parts.working: B1 x = (u+1)/2, dx = ½ du, limits u = 1 to 9; M1 integrand becomes ¼(u^{½} + u^{−½}); A1 ¼[(2/3)u^{3/2} + 2u^{½}]; M1 limits; A1 ¼(24 − 8/3) = 16/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 1 + x³ to find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x²(1 + x³)⁴ dx.
parts.working: M1 du = 3x² dx; A1 ⅓∫u⁴ du with limits 1 and 2; M1 (1/15)[u⁵]₁²; A1 31/15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = sin x to find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/2} cos x/(1 + sin x)² dx.
parts.working: M1 du = cos x dx, limits 0 and 1; A1 ∫₀¹(1 + u)⁻² du; M1 [−(1 + u)⁻¹]₀¹; A1 −½ + 1 = ½.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = √x to find the exact value of ∫₁⁴ e^{√x}/√x dx.
parts.working: M1 dx = 2u du, limits 1 and 2; A1 ∫₁² 2eᵘ du; M1 2[eᵘ]₁²; A1 2e² − 2e.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = x − 2 to find the exact value of ∫₂³ x(x − 2)⁵ dx.
parts.working: M1 x = u + 2, limits 0 and 1; A1 ∫₀¹(u⁶ + 2u⁵) du; M1 [u⁷/7 + u⁶/3]₀¹; A1 10/21.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 1 + x² to show that ∫₀^{√3} x³/√(1 + x²) dx = 4/3.
parts.working: B1 du = 2x dx and x² = u − 1; B1 limits 1 and 4; M1 integrand ½(u − 1)u^{−½} = ½(u^{½} − u^{−½}); A1 ½[(2/3)u^{3/2} − 2u^{½}]; M1 limits; A1 ½(4/3 + 4/3) = 4/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution x = tan θ to show that ∫₀¹ 1/(1 + x²)² dx = ∫₀^{π/4} cos²θ dθ.
parts.working: M1 dx = sec²θ dθ; A1 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ so integrand becomes sec²θ/sec⁴θ = cos²θ; A1 limits 0 and π/4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀¹ 1/(1 + x²)² dx.
parts.working: M1 cos²θ = ½(1 + cos 2θ); M1 ½[θ + ½ sin 2θ]; A1 π/8 + ¼.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 1 + ln x to find the exact value of ∫₁^e √(1 + ln x)/x dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = eˣ + 1 to show that ∫₀^{ln 3} e^{2x}/(eˣ + 1) dx = 2 − ln 2.
parts.working: M1 du = eˣ dx and eˣ = u − 1; A1 integral becomes ∫(u − 1)/u du; B1 limits 2 and 4; M1 [u − ln u]₂⁴; A1 2 − ln 4 + ln 2 = 2 − ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: By writing sin³x = (1 − cos²x) sin x and using the substitution u = cos x, find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/3} sin³x dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution x = 2 sin θ to find the exact value of ∫₀¹ 1/(4 − x²)^{3/2} dx.
parts.working: B1 dx = 2cos θ dθ; M1 (4 − 4sin²θ)^{3/2} = 8cos³θ; A1 integrand ¼ sec²θ; B1 limits 0 and π/6; M1 integrate to ¼ tan θ; A1 ¼ × 1/√3 = √3/12.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution x = 3 sin θ to find the exact value of ∫₀^{3/2} √(9 − x²) dx.
parts.working: M1 dx = 3 cos θ dθ, √(9 − 9 sin²θ) = 3 cos θ; A1 ∫9 cos²θ dθ; B1 limits 0 and π/6; M1 (9/2)[θ + ½ sin 2θ]; A1 (9/2)(π/6 + √3/4); A1 3π/4 + 9√3/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = √(x + 1) to find the exact value of ∫₀³ x/(1 + √(x + 1)) dx.
parts.working: M1 x = u² − 1, dx = 2u du; B1 limits 1 and 2; M1 (u² − 1)/(1 + u) = u − 1; A1 ∫₁² 2u(u − 1) du; M1 2[u³/3 − u²/2]₁²; A1 5/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = tan x to find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/4} tan²x sec⁴x dx.
parts.working: M1 du = sec²x dx; M1 sec²x = 1 + u²; A1 ∫₀¹ u²(1 + u²) du; M1 [u³/3 + u⁵/5]; A1 8/15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 2 + cos x to show that ∫₀^{π/2} sin 2x/(2 + cos x) dx = 2 − 4 ln(3/2).
parts.working: M1 sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x; M1 du = −sin x dx, cos x = u − 2; A1 ∫₂³ 2(u − 2)/u du (limits reversed with sign); M1 2[u − 2 ln u]₂³; A1 2(1 − 2 ln 3 + 2 ln 2); A1 2 − 4 ln(3/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where the line y = x + 3 meets the curve y = x² − 2x + 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the line and the curve.
parts.working: M1 ∫₀³ ((x + 3) − (x² − 2x + 3)) dx; A1 integrand 3x − x²; M1 [3x²/2 − x³/3]₀³; A1 27/2 − 9 = 9/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 6 − x² meets the line y = 2 at the points P and Q. Find the x-coordinates of P and Q.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curve and the line.
parts.working: M1 ∫(4 − x²) dx; M1 [4x − x³/3] from −2 to 2; A1 32/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where the line y = 10 − x meets the curve y = x² − 2x + 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the line and the curve.
parts.working: M1 ∫(6 + x − x²) dx; M1 limits −2 and 3; A1 125/6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x³ and the line y = 4x meet at the origin and at the point A in the first quadrant. Find the coordinates of A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed between the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curve y = √x and the line y = ½x.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 4√x and the line y = x meet at the origin O and at the point A. Find the coordinates of A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the curves y = 4/x² and y = 5 − x² meet where x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0, and hence find the x-coordinates of their points of intersection for x > 0.
parts.working: M1 4 = 5x² − x⁴; A1 equation; A1 (x² − 1)(x² − 4) = 0 → x = 1, 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the two curves for x > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curves y = x² − 2x and y = 6x − x².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = x² + 1 at the point (2, 5).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the curve, the tangent and the y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region bounded by the curves y = eˣ and y = e^{−x} and the line x = ln 3.
parts.working: B1 the curves meet at x = 0; M1 ∫₀^{ln 3}(eˣ − e^{−x}) dx; A1 [eˣ + e^{−x}]; M1 (3 + ⅓) − (1 + 1); A1 4/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 4 − x² passes through P(1, 3). Find the equation of the normal to the curve at P.
parts.working: B1 dy/dx = −2x = −2 at P; M1 normal gradient ½; A1 y − 3 = ½(x − 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The normal meets the curve again at Q. Find the x-coordinate of Q.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve and the normal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line x + y = 10 meets the curve y = 9/x at the points A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region enclosed between the line and the curve, giving your answer in the form p − q ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = kx, where 0 < k < 4, meets the curve y = 4x − x² at the origin and at the point P. Find the x-coordinate of P in terms of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the area enclosed between the line and the curve is (4 − k)³/6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given that this area is 9/2, find k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the first two points where the curves y = sin x and y = cos x meet for x > 0.
parts.working: M1 tan x = 1; A1 both values.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region enclosed between the two curves between these points.
parts.working: M1 ∫(sin x − cos x) dx (sin x above); A1 [−cos x − sin x]; M1 limits: (√2/2 + √2/2) − (−√2/2 − √2/2); A1 2√2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 2x^{3/2} and the line y = 8x meet at the origin and at the point A. Find the coordinates of A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ (4x + 2)/(x² + x + 1) dx, giving your answer as a single logarithm.
parts.working: M1 recognise 4x + 2 = 2 × d/dx(x² + x + 1); A1 2 ln(x² + x + 1); A1 2 ln 3 − 2 ln 1 = ln 9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 3/(2x + 5) dx, for x > −5/2.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(ax + b) dx = (1/a) ln(ax + b) with a = 2; A1 (3/2) ln(2x + 5) + c (ln|2x + 5| accepted).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀² 3/(2x + 5) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: (3/2) ln 9 − (3/2) ln 5; A1 (3/2) ln(9/5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (6x − 1)/(3x² − x + 2) dx.
parts.working: B1 6x − 1 is the derivative of 3x² − x + 2; M1 ∫ f′(x)/f(x) dx = ln f(x) + c; A1 ln(3x² − x + 2) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ (6x − 1)/(3x² − x + 2) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 [ln(3x² − x + 2)]₀¹ = ln 4 − ln 2; A1 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁^e (2 + 1/x) dx, giving your answer in an exact form.
parts.working: B1 integral 2x + ln x; M1 limits (2e + ln e) − (2 + ln 1); A1 2e − 1 (ln e = 1, ln 1 = 0).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 5/(1 − 2x) dx, for x < ½.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(b − ax) dx = −(1/a) ln(b − ax) with a = 2, b = 1; A1 −(5/2) ln(1 − 2x) + c (check: differentiating gives 5/(1 − 2x)).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (2x + 5)/(x + 1) can be written as 2 + 3/(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀² (2x + 5)/(x + 1) dx.
parts.working: M1 integrate to 2x + 3 ln(x + 1); A1; A1 (4 + 3 ln 3) − 0 = 4 + 3 ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (x² + 3x + 4)/(x + 1) can be written as x + 2 + 2/(x + 1).
parts.working: M1 divide, or write x² + 3x + 4 = (x + 1)(x + 2) + 2; A1 result shown with remainder 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀³ (x² + 3x + 4)/(x + 1) dx, giving your answer in the form p + q ln 2, where p and q are rational.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has gradient dy/dx = (2x + 3)/(x² + 3x) for x > 0, and passes through the point (1, 0). Find y in terms of x.
parts.answer: y = ln(x² + 3x) − ln 4, i.e. y = ln((x² + 3x)/4)
parts.working: M1 the numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so y = ln(x² + 3x) + c; M1 substitute (1, 0): ln 4 + c = 0; A1 c = −ln 4; A1 y = ln((x² + 3x)/4).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinate of the point on this curve where y = ln 2, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln((x² + 3x)/4) = ln 2 gives x² + 3x = 8; M1 solve x² + 3x − 8 = 0 and take the positive root (−3 + √41)/2; A1 x = 1.70.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ eˣ/(1 + eˣ) dx.
parts.working: B1 the numerator eˣ is the derivative of the denominator 1 + eˣ; A1 ln(1 + eˣ) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀^{ln 3} eˣ/(1 + eˣ) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: ln(1 + e^{ln 3}) − ln(1 + e⁰) = ln 4 − ln 2; A1 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₁^k 2/(x + 1) dx = ln 8, where k > 1, find the exact value of k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (x³ + 2x)/(x⁴ + 4x² + 3) dx, for all real x.
parts.working: B1 the denominator f = x⁴ + 4x² + 3 has f′ = 4x³ + 8x = 4(x³ + 2x); M1 ∫ f′/(4f) dx = ¼ ln f; A1 ¼ ln(x⁴ + 4x² + 3) + c (f > 0 for all x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ (x³ + 2x)/(x⁴ + 4x² + 3) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 ¼[ln(x⁴ + 4x² + 3)]₀¹ = ¼(ln 8 − ln 3); A1 ¼ ln(8/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ dx/(x ln x) for x > 1.
parts.working: B1 the denominator x ln x is the product of ln x and its derivative 1/x, so the integrand is f′(x)/f(x) with f(x) = ln x; M1 ∫ f′/f dx = ln f + c; A1 ln(ln x) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫_e^{e²} dx/(x ln x), giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 [ln(ln x)] from e to e² = ln 2 − ln 1; A1 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (2x³ + 3x² + 1)/(x² + x) = 2x + 1 + 1/x − 2/(x + 1) for x > 0.
parts.answer: 2x³ + 3x² + 1 = (x² + x)(2x + 1) + (1 − x), and (1 − x)/(x(x + 1)) = 1/x − 2/(x + 1), so the result is shown.
parts.working: M1 long division gives quotient 2x + 1 and remainder 1 − x; M1 partial fractions of (1 − x)/(x(x + 1)) with coefficient 1 (x = 0) and −2 (x = −1); A1 full result shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₁³ (2x³ + 3x² + 1)/(x² + x) dx, giving your answer in the form p + ln(q/r), where p, q and r are integers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₀^k (2x − 6)/(x² − 6x + 10) dx = ln(k² − 6k + 10) − ln 10 for k > 0.
parts.answer: The numerator 2x − 6 is the derivative of x² − 6x + 10, which is positive for all x, so the integral is [ln(x² − 6x + 10)]₀^k = ln(k² − 6k + 10) − ln 10 (shown).
parts.working: M1 numerator is the derivative of the denominator; A1 limits give the result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the two values of k for which ∫₀^k (2x − 6)/(x² − 6x + 10) dx = ln ½.
parts.working: M1 ln(k² − 6k + 10) − ln 10 = ln ½, so k² − 6k + 10 = 5; M1 k² − 6k + 5 = 0, so (k − 1)(k − 5) = 0; A1 k = 1 or k = 5 (both positive).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ dx/(x(2 + ln x)) for x > e⁻².
parts.working: B1 the denominator f(x) = 2 + ln x has f′(x) = 1/x, so the integrand is f′/f; M1 ∫ f′/f dx = ln f + c; A1 ln(2 + ln x) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₁^e dx/(x(2 + ln x)), giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 [ln(2 + ln x)] from 1 to e = ln 3 − ln 2; A1 ln(3/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (e^{2x} + 3e^{−x}) dx.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₀^{ln 2} (e^{2x} + 3e^{−x}) dx = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (2e^{3x} − e^{−x}) dx.
parts.working: M1 ∫ e^{ax} dx = (1/a)e^{ax} used with a = 3 and a = −1; A1 (2/3)e^{3x} + e^{−x} + c.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀^{ln 2} e^{2x} dx, giving your answer as an exact number.
parts.working: B1 integral ½e^{2x}; M1 ½(e^{2 ln 2} − e⁰) = ½(4 − 1); A1 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k e^{x/2} dx = 6, find the exact value of k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ e^{−2x} dx.
parts.working: B1 antiderivative −½e^{−2x}; M1 (−½e⁻²) − (−½); A1 ½(1 − e⁻²).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has gradient dy/dx = 4e^{2x} − 3 and passes through (0, 5). Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 2e^{2x} − 3x + c; M1 use (0, 5): 2 + c = 5; A1 c = 3, so y = 2e^{2x} − 3x + 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = ln 2, giving your answer in the form p − q ln 2, with p and q integers.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = ln 2: 2e^{2 ln 2} − 3 ln 2 + 3 = 8 − 3 ln 2 + 3; A1 11 − 3 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀^{ln 2} (eˣ + e^{−x})² dx, giving your answer in the form p + q ln 2, where p and q are rational.
parts.working: M1 expand: e^{2x} + 2 + e^{−2x}; M1 integrate: ½e^{2x} + 2x − ½e^{−2x}; A1 value at ln 2 is 2 + 2 ln 2 − 1/8; A1 value at 0 is 0, so the answer is 15/8 + 2 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₀¹ (eˣ − e^{−x}) dx = (e − 1)²/e.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative eˣ + e^{−x}; M1 (e + e⁻¹) − (1 + 1); A1 e − 2 + 1/e, and (e − 1)²/e = (e² − 2e + 1)/e = e − 2 + 1/e.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of a for which ∫₀^a 3e^{−3x} dx = 0.95, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k 4e^{2x} dx = 10, find the exact value of k.
parts.working: M1 integrate to 2e^{2x}; M1 2e^{2k} − 2 = 10; A1 e^{2k} = 6, k = ½ ln 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ (eˣ + 1)² dx.
parts.working: M1 expand e^{2x} + 2eˣ + 1; A1 ½e^{2x} + 2eˣ + x; M1 limits; A1 (½e² + 2e + 1) − (½ + 2) = ½e² + 2e − 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that e^{2x}/(eˣ + 1) = eˣ − eˣ/(eˣ + 1).
parts.answer: eˣ(eˣ + 1) − eˣ = e^{2x}, so the identity is shown.
parts.working: M1 put the right side over the common denominator eˣ + 1: (eˣ(eˣ + 1) − eˣ)/(eˣ + 1); A1 numerator is e^{2x}, shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^{ln 4} e^{2x}/(eˣ + 1) dx.
parts.working: B1 ∫eˣ dx = eˣ; M1 ∫ eˣ/(eˣ + 1) dx = ln(eˣ + 1), since the numerator is the derivative of the denominator; M1 [eˣ − ln(eˣ + 1)] from 0 to ln 4 = (4 − ln 5) − (1 − ln 2); A1 3 − ln(5/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x e^{x²} dx.
parts.working: B1 x e^{x²} is ½ times the derivative of e^{x²}; M1 ½[e^{x²}] from 0 to 1; A1 ½(e − 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function f satisfies f″(x) = 6e^{2x} − 4e^{−x}, with f′(0) = 1. Find f′(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given also that f(0) = 2, find f(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of f(ln 2).
parts.working: M1 substitute x = ln 2, using e^{2 ln 2} = 4 and e^{−ln 2} = ½: 6 − 2 − 6 ln 2 + 9/2; A1 17/2 − 6 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀^{ln 3} eˣ/(1 + e^{2x}) dx.
parts.working: M1 substitute u = eˣ (du = eˣ dx, limits 1 to 3): ∫₁³ du/(1 + u²); A1 [arctan u] from 1 to 3; M1 arctan 3 − arctan 1; A1 arctan 3 − π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (eˣ − 1)² eˣ = e^{3x} − 2e^{2x} + eˣ.
parts.working: M1 expand the square and multiply by eˣ; A1 result shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀^{ln 2} (eˣ − 1)² eˣ dx exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁⁴ (3√x − 2/x²) dx.
parts.working: M1 increase powers: 2x^{3/2} + 2x^{−1}; A1 each term correct (A1 A1 if separate); M1 limits (16 + ½) − (2 + 2); A1 12.5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁³ (4x − 1/x²) dx, giving your answer as an exact fraction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² (x² − 2x − 3) dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁² 6(3x − 2)² dx.
parts.working: M1 integrate using the chain rule: (2/3)(3x − 2)³; M1 limits (2/3)(4³) − (2/3)(1³); A1 42.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₁^a (2x + 1) dx = 12, where a > 1, find a correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 integral = [x² + x] from 1 to a = a² + a − 2; M1 a² + a − 2 = 12, so a² + a − 14 = 0; A1 a = (−1 + √57)/2 = 3.27.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k (6x² − 4x) dx = 14, where k > 0, find k correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 integral = [2x³ − 2x²] from 0 to k = 2k³ − 2k²; M1 2k³ − 2k² = 14, so k³ − k² − 7 = 0; M1 sign change of 2k³ − 2k² − 14 between 2.305 and 2.315 (or iteration); A1 k = 2.31.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀¹ x(1 − x)⁴ dx.
parts.working: M1 expand: x − 4x² + 6x³ − 4x⁴ + x⁵ (or substitute u = 1 − x); M1 integrate term by term; A1 ½ − 4/3 + 3/2 − 4/5 + 1/6; A1 1/30.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁⁴ (√x + 4/x²) dx, giving your answer as an exact fraction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (x + 1)²/x² = 1 + 2/x + 1/x².
parts.working: B1 expand the numerator and divide each term by x².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₁² (x + 1)²/x² dx = 3/2 + 2 ln 2.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative x + 2 ln x − 1/x; M1 limits (2 + 2 ln 2 − ½) − (1 + 0 − 1); A1 3/2 + 2 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 4/(2x + 1)³ dx.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of the improper integral ∫₁^∞ 4/(2x + 1)³ dx, explaining how the upper limit is dealt with.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫_a^{a+2} (4x − 3) dx = 20, find the value of a.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative 2x² − 3x; M1 limits: 2(a + 2)² − 3(a + 2) − (2a² − 3a) = 8a + 2; M1 8a + 2 = 20; A1 a = 9/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function f(x) = ax² + bx, where a and b are constants, satisfies ∫₀² f(x) dx = 10 and ∫₀¹ f(x) dx = 2. Find a and b.
parts.working: M1 ∫₀² f = 8a/3 + 2b = 10; M1 ∫₀¹ f = a/3 + b/2 = 2; M1 eliminate b (b = 4 − 2a/3) to get 4a/3 + 8 = 10; A1 a = 3/2; A1 b = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₁² (x − 2/x)² dx = 1/3.
parts.working: M1 expand: x² − 4 + 4/x²; M1 integrate: x³/3 − 4x − 4/x; A1 limits (8/3 − 8 − 2) − (1/3 − 4 − 4); A1 = 1/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₁^p (3x² − 2px) dx = 9, where p > 1, find p.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative x³ − px²; M1 limits (p³ − p·p²) − (1 − p) = p − 1; M1 p − 1 = 9; A1 p = 10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² |x² − 1| dx.
parts.working: B1 x² − 1 ≤ 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and ≥ 0 for 1 ≤ x ≤ 2, so split the integral at x = 1; M1 ∫₀¹ (1 − x²) dx = 2/3; M1 ∫₁² (x² − 1) dx = (8/3 − 2) − (1/3 − 1) = 4/3; A1 total 2/3 + 4/3 = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = 2x + 1, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid, then give it correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀² (2x + 1)² dx; M1 integrate: π[(2x + 1)³/6] from 0 to 2; A1 π(125 − 1)/6 = 62π/3 ≈ 64.9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = √x, for 1 ≤ x ≤ 4, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₁⁴ y² dx = π∫₁⁴ x dx; M1 π[x²/2] from 1 to 4; A1 π(8 − ½) = 15π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = 3x, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis, forming a solid. Find its exact volume.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀² (3x)² dx = 9π∫₀² x² dx; M1 9π[x³/3] from 0 to 2 = 24π; A1 24π (a cone of radius 6 and height 2: ⅓π·6²·2 = 24π).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = √(4 − x²), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀² (4 − x²) dx; M1 π[4x − x³/3] from 0 to 2; A1 π(8 − 8/3) = 16π/3 (half of a sphere of radius 2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the curve y = √(x + 1), the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 3 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀³ (x + 1) dx; A1 π[x²/2 + x]; M1 limits; A1 π(9/2 + 3) = 15π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by y = eˣ, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 1 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume, and give it to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀¹ (eˣ)² dx = π∫₀¹ e^{2x} dx; M1 π[½e^{2x}] from 0 to 1; A1 π(e² − 1)/2; A1 ≈ 10.0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = 4 − x² and the x-axis is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 the curve meets the x-axis at x = ±2, so V = π∫₋₂² (4 − x²)² dx; M1 = 2π∫₀² (16 − 8x² + x⁴) dx by symmetry; M1 2π[16x − 8x³/3 + x⁵/5] from 0 to 2; A1 2π(256/15) = 512π/15 ≈ 107.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by y = 1/(x + 1), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the line y = kx, the x-axis, and the line x = 3, where k > 0, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. The volume of the solid is 36π. Find k.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀³ k²x² dx = πk²[x³/3] from 0 to 3 = 9πk²; M1 9πk² = 36π; A1 k² = 4; A1 k = 2 (k > 0).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = 5 meets the curve y = x² + 1 at the points A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The region enclosed between the curve and the line is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫_{−2}^{2} (5² − (x² + 1)²) dx; M1 expand (x² + 1)² = x⁴ + 2x² + 1; A1 integrand 24 − 2x² − x⁴; A1 [24x − 2x³/3 − x⁵/5]; M1 limits (or 2 × from 0 to 2); A1 2π(48 − 16/3 − 32/5) = 1088π/15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curves y = √x and y = x², for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 washer method: V = π∫₀¹ ((√x)² − (x²)²) dx; M1 the curves meet at x = 0 and x = 1, and √x is the upper curve on this interval; M1 integrand x − x⁴; A1 π[x²/2 − x⁵/5] from 0 to 1; A1 π(½ − ⅕) = 3π/10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the curve y = x², the y-axis, and the line y = 4, with x ≥ 0, is rotated through 360° about the y-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 for this region x = √y, so x² = y and V = π∫₀⁴ x² dy; M1 = π∫₀⁴ y dy = π[y²/2] from 0 to 4; A1 π(8) = 8π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express sin²x in terms of cos 2x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The region between the curve y = sin x, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = π is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Hence show that the volume of the solid is π²/2.
parts.answer: V = π∫₀^π sin²x dx = π²/2 (≈ 4.93), shown
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀^π sin²x dx; M1 = (π/2)∫₀^π (1 − cos 2x) dx; A1 (π/2)[x − ½ sin 2x] from 0 to π = (π/2)π; A1 V = π²/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = 4 − x² (above) and the line y = 2 − x (below), for −1 ≤ x ≤ 2, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 meeting points: 4 − x² = 2 − x gives x² − x − 2 = 0, so x = −1 and x = 2; M1 V = π∫₋₁² [(4 − x²)² − (2 − x)²] dx; M1 integrand 12 + 4x − 9x² + x⁴; A1 [12x + 2x² − 3x³ + x⁵/5] from −1 to 2 = 21.6; A1 V = 108π/5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by y = 1/√x, the x-axis, and the lines x = 1 and x = k, where k > 1, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Show that the volume is π ln k.
parts.answer: V = π∫₁^k (1/x) dx = π[ln x] from 1 to k = π ln k (shown).
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₁^k (x^{−1/2})² dx = π∫₁^k x⁻¹ dx; M1 π[ln x] from 1 to k = π(ln k − 0); A1 V = π ln k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of k for which the volume is 2π.
parts.working: M1 π ln k = 2π, so ln k = 2; A1 k = e².

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x³ − 6x² + 8x crosses the x-axis at O, A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area of the regions enclosed between the curve and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 4.
parts.working: M1 integrate to x⁴/4 − 2x³ + 4x²; A1 ∫₀² = 4; A1 ∫₂⁴ = −4 (region below the axis); A1 total area 4 + 4 = 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the line y = 2x + 3, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 4.
parts.working: M1 the line is above the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, so area = ∫₀⁴ (2x + 3) dx; M1 [x² + 3x] from 0 to 4 = 16 + 12; A1 28.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 6/(x + 2) is drawn for x ≥ 1. Find the exact area bounded by the curve, the x-axis, and the lines x = 1 and x = 4.
parts.working: M1 ∫₁⁴ 6/(x + 2) dx = [6 ln(x + 2)] from 1 to 4; M1 6(ln 6 − ln 3); A1 6 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region between the curve y = 4 − x², the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: M1 the curve is above the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2; M1 ∫₀² (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3] from 0 to 2; A1 8 − 8/3 = 16/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x² − 5x + 4 crosses the x-axis at x = 1 and x = 4. Find the area of the region between the curve and the x-axis for 1 ≤ x ≤ 4.
parts.working: B1 for 1 < x < 4 the curve is below the x-axis, so area = −∫₁⁴ y dx; M1 ∫₁⁴ (x² − 5x + 4) dx = [x³/3 − 5x²/2 + 4x] from 1 to 4; A1 the integral is −9/2; A1 area = 9/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the curve y = 9/(x + 1)², the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: M1 integrate to −9/(x + 1); M1 limits −3 − (−9); A1 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line x = k divides this region into two parts of equal area. Find k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the curve y = 2e^{−x/2}, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 4 has area A. Find A in the form p(1 − e⁻²), where p is an integer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area bounded by the curve y = 1/√(3x + 1), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the curve y = x³ − 4x can be written as y = x(x − 2)(x + 2), and state the x-coordinates where it meets the x-axis for −2 ≤ x ≤ 2.
parts.answer: y = x(x − 2)(x + 2); the curve meets the x-axis at x = −2, 0 and 2.
parts.working: B1 x³ − 4x = x(x² − 4) = x(x − 2)(x + 2); B1 the roots are −2, 0 and 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area of the regions between the curve and the x-axis for −2 ≤ x ≤ 2.
parts.working: B1 for −2 ≤ x ≤ 0 the curve is above the axis: ∫₋₂⁰ (x³ − 4x) dx = 0 − (4 − 8) = 4; M1 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 the curve is below the axis: ∫₀² (x³ − 4x) dx = 4 − 8 = −4, so that area is 4; M1 add the two areas; A1 total 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area under the curve y = k/(x + 1) from x = 0 to x = 3 is ln 8. Find the value of k.
parts.working: M1 area = k[ln(x + 1)] from 0 to 3 = k ln 4; M1 k ln 4 = ln 8; A1 k = ln 8/ln 4; A1 k = 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x(x − 2)² is drawn for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 (it touches the x-axis at x = 2). Find the area between the curve and the x-axis.
parts.working: M1 y ≥ 0 on [0, 2], so area = ∫₀² x(x − 2)² dx; M1 = ∫₀² (x³ − 4x² + 4x) dx; A1 [x⁴/4 − 4x³/3 + 2x²] from 0 to 2 = 4 − 32/3 + 8; A1 4/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area bounded by the curve y = 2x/(x + 1)², the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = x³ − 3x² = x²(x − 3), and state the sign of y for −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.
parts.answer: y = x²(x − 3). For −1 ≤ x < 3 with x ≠ 0, x² > 0 and x − 3 < 0, so y < 0; y = 0 only at x = 0 (touching) and at x = 3.
parts.working: B1 factorise x³ − 3x² = x²(x − 3); B1 x² ≥ 0 and x − 3 < 0 on the interval, so y ≤ 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area between the curve and the x-axis for −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.
parts.working: B1 y ≤ 0 on the whole interval, so area = −∫₋₁³ y dx; M1 ∫(x³ − 3x²) dx = [x⁴/4 − x³]; M1 value at 3 is −27/4 and at −1 is 5/4, so the integral is −27/4 − 5/4 = −8; A1 area = 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area bounded by the curve y = 3x²/(x³ + 4), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: B1 the numerator 3x² is the derivative of x³ + 4, which is positive; M1 ∫₀² = [ln(x³ + 4)] from 0 to 2; A1 ln 12 − ln 4; A1 ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area bounded by the curve y = 1/(x² + 4), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: M1 ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) arctan(x/a) with a = 2; M1 ½[arctan(x/2)] from 0 to 2; A1 ½(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 3/((x + 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ 3/((x + 1)(x + 2)) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln(x + 1) − 3 ln(x + 2); M1 limits (3 ln 2 − 3 ln 3) − (0 − 3 ln 2); A1 6 ln 2 − 3 ln 3 = 3 ln(4/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (5x + 1)/(x² − 1) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₂³ (5x + 1)/(x² − 1) dx, giving your answer in the form p ln 2 − q ln 3, with p and q integers.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln(x − 1) + 2 ln(x + 1); M1 limits (3 ln 2 + 2 ln 4) − (3 ln 1 + 2 ln 3); A1 7 ln 2 − 2 ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.working: M1 combine the right side over (x − 2)(x + 2); A1 numerator (x + 2) − (x − 2) = 4, so the result is shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₃⁵ 1/(x² − 4) dx = ¼ ln(15/7).
parts.working: M1 integrate: ¼[ln(x − 2) − ln(x + 2)]; M1 limits ¼[(ln 3 − ln 7) − (ln 1 − ln 5)]; A1 ¼ ln(15/7).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x + 3)/(x(x + 1)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₁² (2x + 3)/(x(x + 1)) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln x − ln(x + 1); M1 limits (3 ln 2 − ln 3) − (0 − ln 2); A1 4 ln 2 − ln 3 = ln(16/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 5/((x − 1)(x + 4)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₂⁴ 5/((x − 1)(x + 4)) dx, giving your answer as a single logarithm.
parts.working: M1 ln(x − 1) − ln(x + 4); M1 limits (ln 3 − ln 8) − (ln 1 − ln 6); A1 ln(18/8) = ln(9/4).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + 4)/(x² − x − 2) in the form A + B/(x − 2) + C/(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₃⁴ (x² + 4)/(x² − x − 2) dx, giving your answer in the form 1 + p ln 2 − q ln 5, where p and q are rational.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (5x + k)/((x + 1)(x − 3)) ≡ A/(x + 1) + 2/(x − 3) for all x other than −1 and 3, find the values of the constants k and A.
parts.working: M1 multiply through: 5x + k = A(x − 3) + 2(x + 1); M1 x = 3 gives 15 + k = 8, so k = −7; M1 x = −1 gives −5 + k = −4A, so A = 3; A1 k = −7 and A = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ (5x − 7)/((x + 1)(x − 3)) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln(x + 1) + 2 ln|x − 3|; M1 limits: at 1, 2 ln 2 and at 0, 2 ln 3 (|x − 3| = 2 and 3); A1 3 ln 2 + 2 ln 2 − 2 ln 3 = ln(32/9).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x + 4)/(x²(x − 2)) in the form A/x + B/x² + C/(x − 2).
parts.working: M1 B: multiply by x² and set x = 0: B = 4/(0 − 2) = −2; M1 C: set x = 2 in (x + 4)/x²: C = 6/4 = 3/2; M1 compare coefficients (large x gives A + C = 0), so A = −3/2; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₃⁴ (x + 4)/(x²(x − 2)) dx = (3/2) ln(3/2) − 1/6.
parts.working: M1 integrate: −(3/2) ln x + 2/x + (3/2) ln(x − 2); M1 use limits 3 and 4; A1 (3/2)(ln 3 − ln 2) + (½ − ⅔) = (3/2) ln(3/2) − 1/6.

parts.label: a
parts.working: M1 combine the right side over (x + 1)(x + 3); A1 numerator 2(x + 3) − 2(x + 1) = 4, so the identity is shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k 4/((x + 1)(x + 3)) dx = ln 4, find the value of k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x² + 3)/(x²(x + 1)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: B1 form A/x + B/x² + C/(x + 1); M1 2x² + 3 = Ax(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + Cx²; A1 B = 3, C = 5; A1 A = −3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₁² (2x² + 3)/(x²(x + 1)) dx = 3/2 + 5 ln 3 − 8 ln 2.
parts.working: M1 integrate: −3 ln x − 3/x + 5 ln(x + 1); A1 (follow through); M1 limits: (−3 ln 2 − 3/2 + 5 ln 3) − (−3 + 5 ln 2); A1 3/2 + 5 ln 3 − 8 ln 2; A1 fully correct log work.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express x/((x + 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₀¹ x/((x + 1)(x + 2)) dx = ln(9/8).
parts.working: M1 integrate: −ln(x + 1) + 2 ln(x + 2); M1 limits (−ln 2 + 2 ln 3) − (0 + 2 ln 2); A1 2 ln 3 − 3 ln 2 = ln(9/8).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 1/((x − 1)²(x + 1)) in the form A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 1)² + C/(x + 1).
parts.working: M1 B = 1/(x + 1) at x = 1 gives B = ½; M1 C = 1/(x − 1)² at x = −1 gives C = ¼; M1 x = 0 gives −A + B + C = 1, so A = −¼; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₂³ 1/((x − 1)²(x + 1)) dx, giving your answer exactly in the form p + q ln(2/3).
parts.working: M1 integrate: −¼ ln(x − 1) − ½(x − 1)⁻¹ + ¼ ln(x + 1); M1 value at 3 is ¼ ln 2 − ¼ and at 2 is −½ + ¼ ln 3; A1 difference ¼ + ¼ ln(2/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 1/(x(x² + 1)) in the form A/x + Bx/(x² + 1).
parts.working: M1 A = 1 (multiply by x and set x = 0); M1 A(x² + 1) + Bx² = 1 gives A + B = 0, so B = −1; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₁^{√3} 1/(x(x² + 1)) dx = ½ ln(3/2).
parts.working: M1 integrate: ln x − ½ ln(x² + 1); M1 limits: (½ ln 3 − ½ ln 4) − (0 − ½ ln 2); A1 ½ ln 3 − ln 2 + ½ ln 2; A1 ½ ln(3/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 1/(4 − x²) in partial fractions.
parts.working: M1 set up A/(2 − x) + B/(2 + x) with A(2 + x) + B(2 − x) = 1; M1 x = 2 gives A = ¼ and x = −2 gives B = ¼; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ dx/(4 − x²), giving your answer in the form ¼ ln k.
parts.working: M1 integrate: ¼[ln(2 + x) − ln(2 − x)] from 0 to 1 = ¼ ln 3 − 0; A1 ¼ ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x² + 3x − 1)/(x³ − x) in partial fractions, given that x³ − x = x(x − 1)(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₂³ (2x² + 3x − 1)/(x³ − x) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: ln x + 2 ln(x − 1) − ln(x + 1); M1 limits (ln 3 + 2 ln 2 − ln 4) − (ln 2 + 0 − ln 3); A1 2 ln 3 − ln 2; A1 ln(9/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 1/(x² + 9) dx.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(x² + a²) dx = (1/a) arctan(x/a) with a = 3; A1 (1/3) arctan(x/3) + c.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² 4/(x² + 4) dx, giving your answer in exact form.
parts.working: B1 ∫ 4/(x² + 4) dx = 4 × ½ arctan(x/2) = 2 arctan(x/2); M1 2(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² 2x/(x² + 5) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: B1 the numerator 2x is the derivative of x² + 5, so the antiderivative is ln(x² + 5); M1 ln 9 − ln 5; A1 ln(9/5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₋₁¹ 1/(x² + 2x + 5) dx.
parts.working: M1 complete the square: x² + 2x + 5 = (x + 1)² + 4; M1 ∫ 1/((x + 1)² + 2²) dx = ½ arctan((x + 1)/2); M1 ½[arctan 1 − arctan 0]; A1 π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀^{½} 3/(4x² + 1) dx, giving your answer in terms of π.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(4x² + 1) dx = ¼ × 2 arctan(2x) = ½ arctan(2x), so ∫ 3/(4x² + 1) dx = (3/2) arctan(2x); M1 (3/2)(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 3π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (x + 1)/(x² + 4) dx.
parts.working: B1 split: (x + 1)/(x² + 4) = x/(x² + 4) + 1/(x² + 4); M1 x/(x² + 4) gives ½ ln(x² + 4) and 1/(x² + 4) gives ½ arctan(x/2); A1 result + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀² (x + 1)/(x² + 4) dx, giving your answer in the form ½ ln 2 + π/8.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: ½ ln 8 − ½ ln 4 + ½(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 ½ ln 2 + π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (2x − 3)/(x² − 2x + 5) dx.
parts.working: M1 write 2x − 3 = (2x − 2) − 1; M1 the first part gives ln(x² − 2x + 5); M1 complete the square: x² − 2x + 5 = (x − 1)² + 4, so ∫ 1/((x − 1)² + 4) dx = ½ arctan((x − 1)/2); A1 result + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₁³ (2x − 3)/(x² − 2x + 5) dx, giving your answer exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cosec θ − 2 sin θ = 1 for 0° < θ < 360°.
parts.working: M1 multiply by sin θ: 1 − 2 sin²θ = sin θ; M1 2 sin²θ + sin θ − 1 = 0 so (2 sin θ − 1)(sin θ + 1) = 0; A1 sin θ = ½ gives 30° and 150°, sin θ = −1 gives 270°; A1 all three answers

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation sec x = 2 + tan x for 0° ≤ x < 360°, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place. (Note that sec x and tan x are undefined at x = 90° and 270°.)
parts.working: M1 multiply by cos x (cos x ≠ 0): 1 = 2 cos x + sin x; M1 write as √5 sin(x + 63.4°) = 1; M1 x + 63.4° = 26.6° or 153.4°; A1 x = −36.9° (i.e. 323.1°) or x = 90°; A1 x = 90° is rejected because sec 90° is undefined, so x = 323.1°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cot² x + 3 cosec x = 3 for 0° ≤ x < 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: M1 use cot²x = cosec²x − 1 so cosec²x + 3 cosec x − 4 = 0; M1 (cosec x − 1)(cosec x + 4) = 0; A1 cosec x = 1 gives x = 90°; A1 sin x = −¼ gives x = 194.5° and 345.5°; A1 all three answers

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Show that 1/(1 + cos x) + 1/(1 − cos x) ≡ 2 cosec² x. (b) Hence solve 2 cosec² x = 6 for 0° < x < 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.answer: (a) the sum is (1 − cos x + 1 + cos x)/(1 − cos²x) = 2/sin²x = 2 cosec²x. (b) x = 35.3°, 144.7°, 215.3°, 324.7°
parts.working: (a) M1 combine over (1 + cos x)(1 − cos x); A1 = 2/sin²x. (b) M1 sin²x = 1/3; M1 sin x = ±1/√3; A1 x = 35.3° and 144.7°; A1 x = 215.3° and 324.7°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove that cosec 2θ + cot 2θ ≡ cot θ.
parts.working:
M1 (1 + cos 2θ)/sin 2θ
M1 2 cos² θ/(2 sin θ cos θ)
A1 cot θ

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve cosec 4x + cot 4x = 3 for 0° < x < 180°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity cosec x − sin x ≡ cos x cot x. (b) Hence solve cosec x − sin x = 2 cos x for 0° ≤ x < 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.answer: (a) cosec x − sin x = (1 − sin²x)/sin x = cos²x/sin x = cos x cot x. (b) x = 26.6°, 90°, 206.6°, 270°
parts.working: (a) M1 write both terms over sin x; A1 1 − sin²x = cos²x so the expression equals cos x cot x. (b) M1 cos x cot x = 2 cos x, so cos x(cot x − 2) = 0; M1 cos x = 0 gives x = 90° and 270°; M1 cot x = 2 gives x = 26.6° and 206.6°; A1 all four answers

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3 tan x − cot x = 2 for 0° < x < 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: M1 write cot x = 1/tan x and let t = tan x: 3t − 1/t = 2, so 3t² − 2t − 1 = 0; M1 (3t + 1)(t − 1) = 0; A1 t = 1 gives 45° and 225°; A1 t = −⅓ gives 161.6° and 341.6°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation sin 2θ = cos θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
parts.working:
M1 2 sin θ cos θ − cos θ = 0
M1 cos θ(2 sin θ − 1) = 0
A1 90°, 270°
A1 30°, 150°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation sin 2x = sin x for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
parts.working: M1 2 sin x cos x − sin x = 0, so sin x (2 cos x − 1) = 0; M1 sin x = 0 gives 0°, 180°, 360°; M1 cos x = ½ gives 60° and 300°; A1 all five answers

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cos 2x = 4 sin x − 1 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: M1 use cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin²x; M1 2 sin²x + 4 sin x − 2 = 0, so sin²x + 2 sin x − 1 = 0; M1 sin x = −1 + √2 = 0.414; A1 x = 24.5°; A1 x = 155.5°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation sin 2x = 0.6 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 180°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3 cos 2x + 7 cos x + 5 = 0 for 0° < x < 360°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cos 2θ + 3 sin θ = 2 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
parts.working: M1 use cos 2θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ; M1 1 − 2 sin²θ + 3 sin θ = 2, so 2 sin²θ − 3 sin θ + 1 = 0; M1 (2 sin θ − 1)(sin θ − 1) = 0; A1 sin θ = ½ gives 30° and 150°; A1 sin θ = 1 gives 90°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 2 cos 2x + 3 cos x + 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: M1 use cos 2x = 2 cos²x − 1, so 4 cos²x + 3 cos x − 1 = 0; M1 (4 cos x − 1)(cos x + 1) = 0; A1 cos x = ¼ gives 75.5° and 284.5°; A1 cos x = −1 gives 180°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cos 2x = cos x for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
parts.working: M1 2 cos²x − 1 = cos x, so 2 cos²x − cos x − 1 = 0; M1 (2 cos x + 1)(cos x − 1) = 0; A1 cos x = 1 gives 0° and 360°; A1 cos x = −½ gives 120° and 240°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cos 2x + 5 sin x = 3 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
parts.working: M1 use cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin²x; M1 2 sin²x − 5 sin x + 2 = 0; M1 (2 sin x − 1)(sin x − 2) = 0; A1 sin x = ½ gives 30° and 150° (sin x = 2 rejected)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cos 2θ = 3 cos θ − 2 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
parts.working: M1 2 cos²θ − 1 = 3 cos θ − 2, so 2 cos²θ − 3 cos θ + 1 = 0; M1 (2 cos θ − 1)(cos θ − 1) = 0; A1 cos θ = 1 gives 0° and 360°; A1 cos θ = ½ gives 60° and 300°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 2 tan 2θ = 5 tan θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation tan 2x = 3 tan x for 0° ≤ x < 180°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place where necessary.
parts.working: M1 use tan 2x = 2 tan x/(1 − tan²x); M1 2t/(1 − t²) = 3t gives t = 0 or 2 = 3(1 − t²), so t² = 1/3; A1 tan x = 0 gives x = 0°; M1 tan x = ±1/√3 gives x = 30° and 150°; A1 all three answers

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation cos 4θ = 0.5 for 0° ≤ θ < 180°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3 tan 2θ = 4 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Show that the equation 2 cos 2θ = 3 − 4 sin θ can be written as (2 sin θ − 1)² = 0. (b) Hence solve the equation for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°.
parts.answer: (a) 2(1 − 2 sin²θ) = 3 − 4 sin θ gives 4 sin²θ − 4 sin θ + 1 = 0, i.e. (2 sin θ − 1)² = 0. (b) θ = 30°, 150°
parts.working: (a) M1 use cos 2θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ; A1 rearrange to 4 sin²θ − 4 sin θ + 1 = 0 = (2 sin θ − 1)². (b) M1 sin θ = ½ (repeated root); A1 θ = 30°; A1 θ = 150°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity (1 − cos² x)/(sin x cos x) ≡ tan x.
parts.working:
M1 1 − cos² x = sin² x
A1 sin² x/(sin x cos x) = sin x/cos x = tan x

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity (1 + sin θ)/cos θ + cos θ/(1 + sin θ) ≡ 2/cos θ.
parts.answer: LHS = [(1 + sin θ)² + cos² θ]/[cos θ (1 + sin θ)] = (2 + 2 sin θ)/[cos θ (1 + sin θ)] = 2/cos θ = RHS
parts.working: M1 combine the fractions over the common denominator cos θ(1 + sin θ); M1 use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 in the numerator to get 2 + 2 sin θ; A1 cancel (1 + sin θ) to reach 2/cos θ

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity cos⁴ θ − sin⁴ θ ≡ cos 2θ.
parts.answer: cos⁴θ − sin⁴θ = (cos²θ − sin²θ)(cos²θ + sin²θ) = cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ
parts.working: M1 factorise the difference of two squares; A1 use cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 to get cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity 1/(1 − sin x) − 1/(1 + sin x) ≡ 2 tan x/cos x.
parts.answer: LHS = [(1 + sin x) − (1 − sin x)]/[(1 − sin x)(1 + sin x)] = 2 sin x/cos² x = 2 tan x/cos x
parts.working: M1 combine over (1 − sin x)(1 + sin x) = cos²x; A1 numerator 2 sin x; A1 2 sin x/cos² x = 2 tan x/cos x

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Show that sin θ cos θ = tan θ/(1 + tan² θ). (b) Given that tan θ = 2 with θ acute, find the exact value of sin θ cos θ.
parts.answer: (a) divide sin θ cos θ by 1 = sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ: sin θ cos θ = tan θ cos²θ = tan θ/(1 + tan²θ). (b) 2/5
parts.working: (a) M1 1 = cos²θ + sin²θ, so 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; M1 sin θ cos θ = tan θ cos²θ; A1 = tan θ/(1 + tan²θ). (b) A1 2/(1 + 4) = 2/5

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity cos 2x/cos² x ≡ 1 − tan² x. (b) Hence solve 1 − tan² x = 0.6 for 0° ≤ x < 360°, giving your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: (a) M1 cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x; A1 divide by cos²x to get 1 − tan²x. (b) M1 tan²x = 0.4, so tan x = ±√0.4; M1 x = 32.3°, 147.7°, 212.3°, 327.7°; A1 four answers (all correct)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity sin θ/(1 − cos θ) − sin θ/(1 + cos θ) ≡ 2/tan θ.
parts.working:
M1 common denominator 1 − cos² θ
A1 numerator sin θ(1 + cos θ − 1 + cos θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ
M1 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ
A1 2 cos θ/sin θ = 2/tan θ

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve sin θ/(1 − cos θ) − sin θ/(1 + cos θ) = 5 for 0° < θ < 360°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity (sin x + cos x)² ≡ 1 + sin 2x. (b) Hence solve (sin x + cos x)² = 1.5 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity (1 − tan² θ)/(1 + tan² θ) ≡ cos 2θ. (b) Hence solve (1 − tan² θ)/(1 + tan² θ) = 0.5 for 0° < θ < 180°.
parts.answer: (a) multiply top and bottom by cos² θ: (cos²θ − sin²θ)/(cos²θ + sin²θ) = cos 2θ. (b) θ = 30°, 150°
parts.working: (a) M1 multiply by cos² θ; A1 (cos²θ − sin²θ)/1 = cos 2θ. (b) M1 cos 2θ = 0.5, so 2θ = 60° or 300° (0° < 2θ < 360°); A1 θ = 30°, 150°

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity (cosec θ − cot θ)² ≡ (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ).
parts.answer: (cosec θ − cot θ)² = ((1 − cos θ)/sin θ)² = (1 − cos θ)²/(1 − cos²θ) = (1 − cos θ)²/((1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)) = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ)
parts.working: M1 write cosec θ − cot θ = (1 − cos θ)/sin θ; M1 square and use sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ = (1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ); A1 cancel (1 − cos θ); A1 result

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity (1 − cos x)/sin x ≡ sin x/(1 + cos x). (b) Hence solve (1 − cos x)/sin x = 0.5 for 0° < x < 360°.
parts.working: (a) M1 cross-multiply and use sin²x = 1 − cos²x = (1 − cos x)(1 + cos x); A1 identity shown. (b) M1 sin x/(1 + cos x) = 0.5, so tan(x/2) = 0.5; M1 x/2 = 26.57° (within range); A1 x = 53.1° (the solution is unique in 0° < x < 360°, since sin x is negative for 180° < x < 360° making the LHS negative)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prove the identity tan x + 1/tan x ≡ 1/(sin x cos x).
parts.working:
M1 sin x/cos x + cos x/sin x
M1 (sin² x + cos² x)/(sin x cos x)
A1 1/(sin x cos x)

parts.label: b
parts.text: By forming a quadratic equation in tan x, solve tan x + 1/tan x = 4 for 0° < x < 360°, giving exact answers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity tan θ + cot θ ≡ 2 cosec 2θ. (b) Hence solve tan θ + cot θ = 4 for 0° < θ < 180°.
parts.answer: (a) tan θ + cot θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = 2/sin 2θ = 2 cosec 2θ. (b) θ = 15°, 75°
parts.working: (a) M1 combine over sin θ cos θ; M1 sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; A1 2/sin 2θ = 2 cosec 2θ. (b) M1 cosec 2θ = 2, so sin 2θ = 0.5; M1 2θ = 30°, 150°, 390°, 510° in range 0° < 2θ < 360°... so 2θ = 30° or 150° only; A1 θ = 15°, 75°

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity (sec x + tan x)² ≡ (1 + sin x)/(1 − sin x). (b) Hence solve (1 + sin x)/(1 − sin x) = 3 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
parts.answer: (a) (sec x + tan x)² = (1 + sin x)²/cos² x = (1 + sin x)²/[(1 − sin x)(1 + sin x)] = (1 + sin x)/(1 − sin x). (b) x = 30°, 150°
parts.working: (a) M1 write sec x + tan x = (1 + sin x)/cos x; M1 cos²x = (1 − sin x)(1 + sin x); A1 cancel to get (1 + sin x)/(1 − sin x). (b) M1 1 + s = 3(1 − s), so s = 0.5; M1 x = 30°, 150°; A1 both answers

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove the identity cos x/(1 − sin x) ≡ (1 + sin x)/cos x. (b) Hence solve cos x/(1 − sin x) = 3 for 0° ≤ x < 360°, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: (a) M1 cross-multiply: cos²x = (1 − sin x)(1 + sin x); A1 identity shown. (b) M1 (1 + sin x)/cos x = 3, so 1 + sin x = 3 cos x; M1 with 5s² + s − 4 = 0 (using cos²x = 1 − s²), s = 0.8 or s = −1; A1 s = 0.8 gives cos x = 0.6, so x = 53.1° (s = −1 gives cos x = 0, which does not satisfy the original equation)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3 − 2 cos x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. State the range of f.
parts.working:
B1 least value 1 (at x = 0, 2π)
B1 greatest value 5 (at x = π)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the shape of the graph of y = f(x), giving the coordinates of its maximum point and its end-points.
parts.answer: Cosine curve reflected and stretched; max (π, 5); ends (0, 1) and (2π, 1)
parts.working:
B1 one 'hump' shape starting and ending at y = 1
B1 maximum at (π, 5)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Solve the equation f(x) = 4, giving exact answers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by f(x) = 1 + 4 sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. (a) State the range of f, and the coordinates of the maximum point of the graph of y = f(x). (b) Solve the equation f(x) = 3, giving your answers in terms of π.
parts.answer: (a) range −3 ≤ f(x) ≤ 5, maximum point (π/2, 5); (b) x = π/6, 5π/6
parts.working: (a) B1 range [−3, 5] (sin x runs from −1 to 1); B1 maximum point (π/2, 5). (b) M1 4 sin x = 2, so sin x = ½; A1 x = π/6 and 5π/6

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 4 − 2 cos 3x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. (a) State the period of the graph of y = f(x). (b) State the greatest and least values of f(x). (c) Find the x-values, in the range 0 ≤ x ≤ π, at which the greatest value occurs, giving exact answers.
parts.answer: (a) 2π/3; (b) greatest 6, least 2; (c) x = π/3 and x = π
parts.working: (a) B1 period = 2π/3. (b) B1 greatest value 4 + 2 = 6; B1 least value 4 − 2 = 2. (c) M1 cos 3x = −1 so 3x = π, 3π; A1 x = π/3 and π

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function y = cos(x − 2π/3) is defined for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. (a) State the amplitude, the period, and the horizontal translation of the graph of this function compared with y = cos x. (b) Solve cos(x − 2π/3) = 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, giving exact answers.
parts.answer: (a) amplitude 1, period 2π, translation 2π/3 to the right; (b) x = π/6, 7π/6
parts.working: (a) B1 amplitude 1; B1 period 2π; B1 translation of 2π/3 in the positive x direction. (b) M1 x − 2π/3 = ±π/2 (in range −2π/3 ≤ x − 2π/3 ≤ 4π/3); A1 x = π/6 and 7π/6 (only these two)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The graph of y = a sin x + b, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, where a and b are constants with a > 0, has a maximum point at (π/2, 4) and a minimum point at (3π/2, −2). (a) Find a and b. (b) Find the number of solutions of 3 sin x + 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, and give them correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.answer: (a) a = 3, b = 1; (b) two solutions, x = 3.48 and x = 5.94
parts.working: (a) M1 a + b = 4 and −a + b = −2; A1 a = 3, b = 1. (b) B1 3 sin x = −1 so sin x = −1/3, which has two solutions in [0, 2π]; M1 x = π + arcsin(1/3) = 3.48; A1 x = 2π − 0.340 = 5.94 (2 d.p.)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The graph of y = a + b sin x, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, where a and b are constants and b > 0, has a maximum point at (π/2, 7) and a minimum point at (3π/2, −1). Find a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where the graph crosses the x-axis, giving answers correct to 3 decimal places.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the set of values of k for which the equation a + b sin x = k has exactly two solutions for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π.
parts.working:
B1 −1 < k < 7
B1 k ≠ 3 (three solutions 0, π, 2π when k = 3)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The graph of y = a + b cos x, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, where a and b are constants with b > 0, has a maximum point at (0, 9) and a minimum point at (π, 3). (a) Find the values of a and b. (b) Solve the equation a + b cos x = 7.5 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, giving your answers in terms of π.
parts.working: (a) M1 a + b = 9 and a − b = 3; A1 a = 6, b = 3. (b) M1 6 + 3 cos x = 7.5, so cos x = ½; A1 x = π/3 and 5π/3

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = |2 sin x| for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. (a) State the period of f and its range. (b) Find the exact values of x, with 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, for which f(x) = 1.
parts.answer: (a) period π; range 0 ≤ f(x) ≤ 2; (b) x = π/6, 5π/6, 7π/6, 11π/6
parts.working: (a) B1 the modulus reflects the negative part, so the period is π; B1 range 0 to 2. (b) M1 |sin x| = ½; M1 sin x = ±½; A1 x = π/6, 5π/6, 7π/6, 11π/6 (four solutions)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3 + 2 sin(x − π/4) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. (a) Find the greatest value of f(x) and the value of x at which it occurs. (b) Find the least value of f(x) and the value of x at which it occurs. (c) Solve f(x) = 4, giving your answers in terms of π.
parts.working: (a) B1 greatest value 3 + 2 = 5; B1 x − π/4 = π/2 so x = 3π/4. (b) B1 least value 1; B1 x − π/4 = 3π/2 so x = 7π/4. (c) M1 sin(x − π/4) = ½; A1 x − π/4 = π/6 or 5π/6, so x = 5π/12 and 13π/12

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 4 cos x − 1 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. (a) State the range of f. (b) Find the set of values of k for which the equation f(x) = k has exactly two solutions in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π.
parts.working: (a) B1 greatest 4 − 1 = 3 (x = 0 or 2π), least 4·(−1) − 1 = −5 (x = π); A1 range. (b) M1 cos x = (k + 1)/4 has two solutions in [0, 2π] when −1 < (k + 1)/4 ≤ 1 ; A1 −5 < k ≤ 3 (cos x = 1 gives x = 0 and 2π; cos x = −1 gives only x = π)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 1 − 3 sin 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. (a) State the range of f. (b) Solve f(x) = −2, giving the exact value(s) of x.
parts.working: (a) B1 least value 1 − 3 = −2 and greatest 1 + 3 = 4 (since sin 2x runs between −1 and 1); B1 range. (b) M1 3 sin 2x = 3, so sin 2x = 1; M1 2x = π/2 in 0 ≤ 2x ≤ 2π (2x = 5π/2 is outside); A1 x = π/4

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by f(x) = 5 + 2 sin(3x − π/3) for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. (a) State the greatest and least values of f(x). (b) Find the values of x at which f(x) is greatest, in the range 0 ≤ x ≤ π. (c) Find the value of x at which f(x) is least, in the range 0 ≤ x ≤ π.
parts.working: (a) B1 greatest 7, least 3. (b) M1 3x − π/3 = π/2 + 2kπ, so 3x = 5π/6 + 2kπ; A1 x = 5π/18 and 17π/18 (3x ranges over 0 to 3π). (c) M1 3x − π/3 = 3π/2 + 2kπ; A1 x = 11π/18 only (other value is outside the range)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by f(x) = 2 tan(x/2) + 1 for 0 < x < 2π. (a) State the period of f and the value of x in this interval at which the graph has an asymptote. (b) Solve f(x) = 5, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place in degrees.
parts.answer: (a) period 2π; asymptote at x = π; (b) x = 126.9°
parts.working: (a) B1 period of tan(x/2) is 2π; B1 asymptote where x/2 = π/2, so x = π. (b) M1 2 tan(x/2) = 4, so tan(x/2) = 2; M1 x/2 = 63.4°, so x = 126.9° (the other solution x = 486.9° is outside the range)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 2 sec x for 0 ≤ x < 2π. (a) State the equations of the asymptotes of the graph of y = f(x) in this interval. (b) Solve f(x) = 5, giving your answers correct to 2 decimal places in radians.
parts.working: (a) B1 x = π/2; B1 x = 3π/2 (where cos x = 0). (b) M1 2 sec x = 5, so cos x = 0.4; M1 x = arccos 0.4 = 1.159 in the first quadrant and 2π − 1.159 in the fourth quadrant; A1 x = 1.16 and 5.12 (2 d.p.)

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Show that the x-coordinates of the points of intersection of y = sin x and y = cos 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π satisfy 2 sin²x + sin x − 1 = 0. (b) Hence find the exact x-coordinates of the points of intersection.
parts.answer: (a) sin x = 1 − 2 sin²x, so 2 sin²x + sin x − 1 = 0. (b) x = π/6, 5π/6
parts.working: (a) M1 use cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin²x; A1 rearrange to 2 sin²x + sin x − 1 = 0. (b) M1 (2 sin x − 1)(sin x + 1) = 0; M1 sin x = −1 has no solution in 0 ≤ x ≤ π; A1 sin x = ½ gives x = π/6 and 5π/6

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of each of the following, giving each answer in radians. (a) arccos(−½) (b) arctan(√3) (c) arcsin(√2/2)
parts.working: (a) B1 2π/3 (the angle in [0, π] with cosine −½); (b) B1 π/3 (the angle in (−π/2, π/2) with tangent √3); (c) B1 π/4 (the angle in [−π/2, π/2] with sine √2/2)

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Find the exact value of sin(arccos(3/5)). (b) Find the exact value of cos(arcsin(5/13)).
parts.working: (a) M1 let θ = arccos(3/5), so cos θ = 3/5 and sin θ = √(1 − 9/25); A1 4/5. (b) M1 let φ = arcsin(5/13), so sin φ = 5/13 and cos φ = √(1 − 25/169); A1 12/13

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by f(x) = arccos(2x − 1). (a) State the domain of f. (b) State the range of f. (c) Find the exact value of f(0.25).
parts.working: (a) B1 −1 ≤ 2x − 1 ≤ 1 gives 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. (b) B1 range of arccos is [0, π]. (c) M1 f(0.25) = arccos(−½); A1 2π/3

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of each of the following. (a) arcsin(−√3/2) (b) arccos(√3/2) (c) arctan(−1)
parts.working: (a) B1 −π/3 (angle in [−π/2, π/2] with sine −√3/2); (b) B1 π/6 (angle in [0, π] with cosine √3/2); (c) B1 −π/4 (angle in (−π/2, π/2) with tangent −1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 2 − 3 sin x for −π/2 ≤ x ≤ π/2. Find the range of f.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x) and state its domain.
parts.working:
M1 x = 2 − 3 sin y, sin y = (2 − x)/3
A1 f⁻¹(x) = sin⁻¹((2 − x)/3)
B1 domain −1 ≤ x ≤ 5

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of f⁻¹(0.5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by f(x) = 1 + 2 cos x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. (a) State the range of f. (b) Find an expression for f⁻¹(x), and state its domain.
parts.working: (a) B1 f(0) = 3 and f(π) = −1 (cos x runs from 1 to −1), so range [−1, 3]. (b) M1 y = 1 + 2 cos x gives cos x = (y − 1)/2; A1 x = arccos((y − 1)/2); B1 domain of f⁻¹ is the range of f

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by k(x) = 5 sin 2x for −π/4 ≤ x ≤ π/4. (a) State the range of k. (b) Find an expression for k⁻¹(x), and state its domain.
parts.answer: (a) −5 ≤ k(x) ≤ 5; (b) k⁻¹(x) = ½ arcsin(x/5), domain −5 ≤ x ≤ 5
parts.working: (a) B1 2x runs from −π/2 to π/2, so sin 2x runs from −1 to 1 and the range is [−5, 5]. (b) M1 x = 5 sin 2y gives sin 2y = x/5; M1 2y = arcsin(x/5); A1 k⁻¹(x) = ½ arcsin(x/5); B1 domain −5 ≤ x ≤ 5

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Solve the equation arcsin(2x) = π/6, giving the exact value of x. (b) State the domain of the function arcsin(2x).

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Prove that arcsin x + arccos x = π/2 for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1. (b) Hence find arccos(0.6) in radians, correct to 3 decimal places, given that arcsin(0.6) = 0.6435 (correct to 4 decimal places).
parts.working: (a) M1 let α = arcsin x, so −π/2 ≤ α ≤ π/2 and sin α = x; M1 cos(π/2 − α) = sin α = x, with 0 ≤ π/2 − α ≤ π; A1 so arccos x = π/2 − α, giving the result. (b) M1 arccos 0.6 = π/2 − 0.6435; A1 = 0.927

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the exact value of tan(arcsin(3/5) + arccos(5/13)) is −63/16.
parts.working: B1 tan(arcsin(3/5)) = 3/4 (opposite 3, adjacent 4); B1 tan(arccos(5/13)) = 12/5 (opposite 12, adjacent 5); M1 use tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B); M1 substitute; A1 −63/16

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function is defined by g(x) = 1 + 3 tan x for −π/2 < x < π/2. (a) State the range of g. (b) Find g⁻¹(x). (c) Find the exact value of g⁻¹(4).
parts.answer: (a) all real numbers; (b) g⁻¹(x) = arctan((x − 1)/3); (c) π/4
parts.working: (a) B1 tan x takes all real values on (−π/2, π/2), so the range is ℝ. (b) M1 y = 1 + 3 tan x gives tan x = (y − 1)/3; A1 g⁻¹(x) = arctan((x − 1)/3). (c) A1 arctan(1) = π/4

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation arcsin x = arccos x for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, giving the exact value of x.
parts.working: M1 arccos x = π/2 − arcsin x, so arcsin x = π/2 − arcsin x; M1 arcsin x = π/4; A1 x = sin(π/4) = √2/2; A1 check arccos(√2/2) = π/4

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation arctan(2x) + arctan x = π/4, giving the exact value of x, and explain why one of the roots of the resulting quadratic equation is rejected.
parts.working: M1 take tan of both sides: (2x + x)/(1 − 2x²) = 1; M1 3x = 1 − 2x², so 2x² + 3x − 1 = 0; M1 x = (−3 ± √17)/4; A1 both roots, rejected because for the negative root both arctan terms are negative, so their sum is negative and cannot equal π/4; A1 x = (√17 − 3)/4

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 2 arctan(1/3) + arctan(1/7) = π/4.
parts.answer: tan(2 arctan(1/3)) = (2/3)/(1 − 1/9) = 3/4; tan(3/4 + arctan(1/7) combined): (3/4 + 1/7)/(1 − 3/28) = (25/28)/(25/28) = 1; both angles lie in (0, π/2), so the sum lies in (0, π) and equals π/4

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation arccos x = 2 arcsin x for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, giving the exact value of x.
parts.working: M1 let α = arcsin x, so arccos x = π/2 − α (from arcsin x + arccos x = π/2); M1 π/2 − α = 2α, so α = π/6; A1 x = sin(π/6) = ½; A1 check: arccos(½) = π/3 = 2 × π/6

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) is defined by p(x) = 2x³ + ax² − 13x + 6, where a is a constant. It is given that (x − 2) is a factor of p(x). Find the value of a.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence factorise p(x) completely and solve the equation p(x) = 0.
parts.working: Divide by (x − 2) to get 2x² + 5x − 3 M1 A1; = (2x − 1)(x + 3) A1; x = 2, 1/2, −3 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the remainder when x⁴ − 3x³ + 2x − 5 is divided by (x + 2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the remainder when x⁴ − 3x³ + 2x − 5 is divided by (2x − 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial x³ + ax² + bx − 8 has a factor (x + 1), and leaves a remainder of −12 when divided by (x − 2). Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Factorise the polynomial and hence find the exact roots of the equation x³ + ax² + bx − 8 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial f(x) = x³ + 5x² + px − 18, where p is a constant, leaves a remainder of 12 when divided by (x − 2). Find the value of p.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = 2x³ − 3x² + ax − 6 has a factor (x − 2). Find the value of a.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Factorise p(x) completely.
parts.working: Divide 2x³ − 3x² + x − 6 by (x − 2) to get 2x² + x + 3 (M1 for method, A1 for quotient); the quadratic has discriminant 1 − 24 < 0, so it does not factorise further (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = 6x³ + ax² + bx + 2, where a and b are constants, has a factor (2x + 1) and leaves remainder −6 when divided by (x − 1). Find a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence solve the equation 6e³ʸ − 11e²ʸ − 3eʸ + 2 = 0, giving your answers correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = x³ − 4x² + ax + b has a factor (x − 3). When p(x) is divided by (x − 2) the remainder is the same as when p(x) is divided by (x + 2). Find a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − 2).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact roots of p(x) = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = 4x³ + ax² + bx − 3 has factors (2x − 1) and (x + 1). Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the third factor of p(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Solve the equation 4cos³θ + 8cos²θ + cos θ − 3 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
parts.working: cos θ = ½, −1, −3/2 M1; −3/2 has no solutions A1; θ = 60°, 300°, 180° A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial f(x) = x³ + ax² + bx − 6, where a and b are constants, has a factor (x − 1) and leaves a remainder of −12 when divided by (x + 2). Find the values of a and b.
parts.working: f(1) = 0 gives a + b = 5 (M1 A1); f(−2) = −8 + 4a − 2b − 6 = −12 gives 2a − b = 1 (M1); solving gives a = 2 and b = 3 (A1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence factorise f(x) completely.
parts.working: Divide f(x) = x³ + 2x² + 3x − 6 by (x − 1) to get x² + 3x + 6 (M1 A1); the discriminant of x² + 3x + 6 is 9 − 24 < 0, so it does not factorise further

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial q(x) = 3x³ + ax² − 5x + b, where a and b are constants, leaves a remainder of 9 when divided by (x + 2). It is also given that (x − 1) is a factor of q(x). Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence factorise q(x) completely.
parts.working: Divide q(x) = 3x³ + 7x² − 5x − 5 by (x − 1) (M1); the quadratic 3x² + 10x + 5 has no rational roots (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx + c leaves remainders 2, 5 and 14 when divided by (x − 1), (x − 2) and (x − 3) respectively. Find a, b and c.
parts.working: Three equations: a + b + c = 1, 4a + 2b + c = −3, 9a + 3b + c = −13 M1 A1; eliminate c: 3a + b = −4, 5a + b = −10 M1; a = −3, b = 5 A1; c = −1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the equation p(x) = 0 has exactly one real root, and state two consecutive integers between which it lies.
parts.answer: Exactly one real root, between 0 and 1
parts.working: p′(x) = 3x² − 6x + 5, discriminant 36 − 60 < 0 so p′(x) > 0 for all x and p is increasing M1 A1; p(0) = −1 < 0, p(1) = 2 > 0, so root between 0 and 1 B1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (x − 3) is a factor of p(x) = 2x³ + ax² − 11x + 6, find a and factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve the equation 2|x|³ − 3x² − 11|x| + 6 = 0.
parts.working: x² = |x|², so this is p(|x|) = 0 with |x| = 3 or ½ (|x| = −2 rejected) M1; x = ±3, ±½ A1

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence solve the equation 2(27ʸ) − 3(9ʸ) − 11(3ʸ) + 6 = 0, giving any non-exact answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: 3ʸ = 3, ½ (−2 rejected) M1; y = 1 A1; y = ln ½ / ln 3 = −0.631 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + kx² − 4x − 4k, where k is a constant. Show that (x + k) is a factor of p(x) for all values of k.
parts.working: p(−k) = −k³ + k³ + 4k − 4k M1; = 0, so (x + k) is a factor A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: When p(x) is divided by (x − 3) the remainder is 30. Find k and factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the values of k for which the equation p(x) = 0 has exactly two distinct real roots.
parts.working: p(x) = (x + k)(x − 2)(x + 2), so there is a repeated root when −k = 2 or −k = −2 M1; k = ±2 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial f(x) = x⁴ + px² + qx + 4, where p and q are constants, has (x + 1) and (x − 2) as factors. Find the values of p and q.
parts.working: f(−1) = 0 gives p − q = −5 (M1 A1); f(2) = 0 gives 4p + 2q = −20 (M1); solving gives p = −5, q = 0 (A1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Factorise f(x) completely.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the remainder when f(x) is divided by (x − 3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = 2x³ + px² + qx − 12, where p and q are constants, has (x − 2)² as a factor. Find the values of p and q.
parts.working: p(2) = 0 gives 4p + 2q = −4 (M1 A1); p′(x) = 6x² + 2px + q and p′(2) = 0 gives 4p + q = −24 (M1); solving gives p = −11, q = 20 (A1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |2x − 5| = 7.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |3x + 1| < 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |x − 4| = |2x + 1|.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |4 − 3x| = 11.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |5 − 2x| ≤ 9, giving your answer in the form a ≤ x ≤ b.
parts.working: 5 − 2x ≤ 9 gives x ≥ −2 (M1 A1); 5 − 2x ≥ −9 gives x ≤ 7 (M1 A1 for both limits correct)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |2x + 3| > |x − 6|.
parts.working: Square both sides: 4x² + 12x + 9 > x² − 12x + 36 M1; 3x² + 24x − 27 > 0 A1; critical values −9 and 1 A1; x < −9 or x > 1 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sketch, on the same axes, the graphs of y = |x − 2| and y = 3x − 4, labelling where each meets the axes.
parts.answer: V-shape with vertex (2, 0), meeting y-axis at (0, 2); line through (0, −4) and (4/3, 0)
parts.working: V-shaped graph with vertex at (2, 0) and y-intercept 2 B1; straight line y-intercept −4, x-intercept 4/3 B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the inequality |x − 2| ≤ 3x − 4.
parts.working: Intersection on the left branch: 2 − x = 3x − 4 M1; x = 3/2 A1; from the sketch the line is above the graph for x ≥ 3/2 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |x − 3| = 2|x + 1|.
parts.working: x − 3 = 2(x + 1) gives x = −5 M1 A1; x − 3 = −2(x + 1) gives x = 1/3 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve the equation |eʸ − 3| = 2|eʸ + 1|, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: eʸ = 1/3 (eʸ = −5 impossible) M1; y = ln(1/3) = −1.10 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |x − 2| + |x + 4| = 10.
parts.working: For x ≥ 2 the equation is 2x + 2 = 10, giving x = 4 (M1 A1); for x ≤ −4 it is −2x − 2 = 10, giving x = −6 (M1 A1); for −4 < x < 2 the left side is always 6, so there are no solutions there

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |x² − 4| < 5.
parts.working: −5 < x² − 4 < 5 (M1); x² < 9 gives −3 < x < 3 (M1 A1); x² > −1 is always true

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |3x − 2| = 2x + 1.
parts.working: 3x − 2 = 2x + 1 gives x = 3 (M1 A1); 3x − 2 = −(2x + 1) gives x = 1/5 (M1 A1 for both); both values satisfy 2x + 1 ≥ 0

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |2x − 7| < |x + 1|.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find all the integers N that satisfy |2(5^(0.1N)) − 7| < |5^(0.1N) + 1|.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The constant a is positive. Solve the inequality |2x − a| > |x + a|, giving your answer in terms of a.
parts.working: Square: 4x² − 4ax + a² > x² + 2ax + a² M1; 3x² − 6ax > 0 A1; 3x(x − 2a) > 0, critical values 0 and 2a A1; x < 0 or x > 2a A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve the inequality |2 ln t − 3| > |ln t + 3|, giving the boundary value correct to 4 significant figures where appropriate.
parts.working: Put x = ln t, a = 3: ln t < 0 or ln t > 6 M1; 0 < t < 1 A1; t > e⁶ = 403.4 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |x² − 3x| < x.
parts.working: Case 0 < x < 3 (x² − 3x < 0): 3x − x² < x gives x > 2, so 2 < x < 3 (M1 A1); case x ≤ 0 or x ≥ 3: x² − 3x < x gives 0 < x < 4, so 3 ≤ x < 4 (M1 A1); combining the cases gives 2 < x < 4; the RHS must be positive so no solutions with x ≤ 0 (A1 for the correct final set)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation |x − k| = 2x + 1 has exactly one real solution for every real constant k.
parts.answer: For k ≥ −1/2 the solution is x = (k − 1)/3; for k < −1/2 it is x = −k − 1. Exactly one of the two cases gives a valid solution in each case
parts.working: Need 2x + 1 ≥ 0 (x ≥ −1/2). Case x − k = 2x + 1 gives x = −k − 1, valid iff k ≤ −1/2 (M1). Case x − k = −(2x + 1) gives x = (k − 1)/3, valid iff k ≥ −1/2 (M1). At k = −1/2 both cases give x = −1/2, which is one solution (A1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: For k < −1/2, find the solution in terms of k.
parts.working: Only the first case is valid when k < −1/2 (M1); x = −k − 1 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (7x − 1)/((x − 1)(2x + 1)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of the integral of (7x − 1)/((x − 1)(2x + 1)) with respect to x from x = 2 to x = 5, giving your answer in the form a ln 2 + b ln(11/5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + 5)/((x + 1)(x − 1)²) in partial fractions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (7x + 1)/((x − 2)(x + 3)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Write as A/(x − 2) + B/(x + 3) so that 7x + 1 = A(x + 3) + B(x − 2) (M1); x = 2 gives A = 3 (A1); x = −3 gives B = 4 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x + 9)/(x(x + 3)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Write as A/x + B/(x + 3), so 2x + 9 = A(x + 3) + Bx (M1); x = 0 gives A = 3 (A1); x = −3 gives B = −1 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (3x + 1)/((x + 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: A/(x + 1) + B/(x + 2) with 3x + 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x + 1) (M1); x = −1 gives A = −2 and x = −2 gives B = 5 (A1 A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Let f(x) = (4x² + 3x + 14)/((x + 2)(x² + 4)). Express f(x) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Form A/(x + 2) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 4) B1; x = −2: 24 = 8A, A = 3 M1 A1; compare x² and constants: B = 1, C = 1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that the integral of f(x) from x = 0 to x = 2 is equal to (7/2) ln 2 + π/8.
parts.working: 3 ln(x + 2) B1; ½ ln(x² + 4) B1; ½ tan⁻¹(x/2) B1; substitute limits: 3 ln 2 + ½ ln 2 + ½(π/4) M1; = (7/2) ln 2 + π/8 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + 7)/((x − 1)(x + 3)) in the form A + B/(x − 1) + C/(x + 3), where A, B and C are constants.
parts.working: A = 1 (division or comparing x² terms) B1; x² + 7 ≡ (x − 1)(x + 3) + B(x + 3) + C(x − 1) M1; x = 1: B = 2 A1; x = −3: C = −4 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that the integral of (x² + 7)/((x − 1)(x + 3)) from x = 2 to x = 3 is 1 + ln(625/324).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x³ + 3x² − 4x + 1)/(x² − 1) in partial fractions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + 2x + 7)/((x − 1)(x² + 9)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Write as A/(x − 1) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 9) (M1); x = 1 gives A = 1 (A1); comparing x² and constant terms gives B = 0 and C = 2 (M1 A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x + 1)/((x − 1)(x + 1)²) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Write as A/(x − 1) + B/(x + 1) + C/(x + 1)² (M1); x = 1 gives A = 3/4 (A1); x = −1 gives C = 1/2 (A1); x = 0 gives B = −3/4 (M1 A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x² + 3x + 5)/(x(x² + 5)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Write as A/x + (Bx + C)/(x² + 5) (M1); x = 0 gives A = 1 (A1); comparing x² and x terms gives B = 1 and C = 3 (M1 A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Let f(x) = (3x² + 16x + 10)/((1 − 2x)(2 + x)²). Express f(x) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence obtain the expansion of f(x) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x², and state the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + x + 1)/((x + 1)²(x² + 1)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Write as A/(x + 1) + B/(x + 1)² + (Cx + D)/(x² + 1) (M1); x = −1 gives B = 1/2 (A1); equating coefficients gives A = 0, C = 0, D = 1/2 (M1 A1 A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x³ − x² + 7x + 4)/(x(x + 1)²) in partial fractions.
parts.working: The degree of the numerator equals the degree of the denominator, so divide first to get 2 (M1); write the remainder fraction as A/x + B/(x + 1) + C/(x + 1)² (M1); x = 0 gives A = 4 (A1); x = −1 gives C = 6 (A1); x = 1 gives B = −9 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x³ + 2)/(x²(x − 1)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: Divide: x³ + 2 = x²(x − 1) + (x² + 2), so the quotient is 1 (M1); write (x² + 2)/(x²(x − 1)) = A/x + B/x² + C/(x − 1) (M1); x = 0 gives B = −2 (A1); x = 1 gives C = 3 (A1); equating x² coefficients gives A = −2 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand √(1 − 4x) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x³, simplifying the coefficients.
parts.working: (1 + u)^½ = 1 + ½u − ⅛u² + (1/16)u³ M1; with u = −4x A1; 1 − 2x A1; − 2x² − 4x³ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand 1/(2 + x)² in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x², and state the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of x, in the expansion of (1 + 3x)^(1/2).
parts.working: Use (1 + y)^(1/2) = 1 + y/2 + (1/2)(−1/2)y²/2 + …  with y = 3x (M1); the x term is 3/2 x (A1); the x² term is (−1/8) × 9x² = −9/8 x² (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand (1 − x)^(−3) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x³.
parts.working: Coefficient of xʳ is (r + 1)(r + 2)/2 (M1); the coefficients are 1, 3, 6 and 10 (A1 for two correct, A1 for all four correct)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand (1 − 2x)⁴ in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x³, and simplify each coefficient.
parts.working: Binomial coefficients 1, 4, 6, 4 with powers of −2 (M1); each term simplified (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand (1 + 4x)^(−1/2) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x², and state the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid.
parts.working: Coefficients (−1/2)(1) = −1/2 and (−1/2)(−3/2)/2 with (4x)² gives 6x² (M1 A1); validity needs |4x| < 1 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand (1 − 3x)^(−1/3) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (1 + 2x)/∛(1 − 3x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use your answer to part (a), with a suitable value of x, to estimate (0.97)^(−1/3), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2 − 3x)^(−1/2), giving your answer in exact form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Expand (3 + x)/(1 + x)² in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x².
parts.working: (1 + x)^(−2) = 1 − 2x + 3x² + … (M1 A1); multiply by (3 + x) (M1); collect terms: constant 3, x term 3(−2) + 1 = −5, x² term 3(3) + (−2) = 7 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (4 + x)^(1/2), giving your answer as a fraction.
parts.working: (4 + x)^(1/2) = 2(1 + x/4)^(1/2) (M1); the x² coefficient in (1 + y)^(1/2) is (1/2)(−1/2)/2 = −1/8 (M1); with y = x/4 and the factor 2, the coefficient is 2 × (−1/8) × (1/16) = −1/64 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The expansion of (1 + x)^(−1/2) is used to estimate 1/√1.04. (a) Expand (1 + x)^(−1/2) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x². (b) Use the first three terms of your expansion with x = 0.04 to estimate 1/√1.04, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the expansion of (1 + ax)ⁿ in ascending powers of x, the first three terms are 1 − 6x + 24x². Find the values of a and n.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that, for small values of x, √((1 + x)/(1 − x)) ≈ 1 + x + ½x².
parts.working: (1 + x)^½ = 1 + ½x − ⅛x² B1; (1 − x)^(−½) = 1 + ½x + ⅜x² M1 A1; multiply: 1 + x + (⅜ − ⅛ + ¼)x² M1; = 1 + x + ½x² A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: By substituting x = 1/7, show that √3 ≈ 196/113, and find the percentage error in this approximation, correct to 2 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the expansion of (1 + px)(1 − 2x)⁻³ in ascending powers of x, the coefficient of x² is 36. (a) Find the value of p. (b) Find the coefficient of x³.
parts.working: (1 − 2x)⁻³ = 1 + 6x + 24x² + 80x³ + … (M1); the coefficient of x² is 24 + 6p = 36 so p = 2 (M1 A1); the coefficient of x³ is 80 + 24p = 128 (A1 for the expansion, A1 for the answer)

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the expansion of (1 + ax)^(−1/2) in ascending powers of x, the coefficient of x² is twice the coefficient of x. Find the non-zero value of the constant a.
parts.working: Expansion: 1 − (a/2)x + (3/8)a²x² (M1 A1); the x² coefficient 3a²/8 must equal twice the x coefficient, 2(−a/2) = −a (M1); a ≠ 0 gives a = −8/3 (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the quotient and remainder when 2x⁴ − 3x³ + x² + 5x − 4 is divided by x² − x + 2.
parts.working: Long division: first term 2x² M1; quotient 2x² − x − 4 A1 A1; remainder 3x + 4 A1

parts.label: a
