parts.answer: Number the students 001 to 600; use random numbers (calculator, computer or table) to generate three-digit numbers; select the students with those numbers, ignoring numbers above 600 and repeats, until 30 are chosen
parts.working: B1 list and number all 600 students. B1 generate random numbers in the range 001–600. B1 ignore repeats/out-of-range values and continue until 30 chosen.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the principal might use a sample rather than ask all 600 students.
parts.answer: Quicker and cheaper / less effort than a census

parts.label: a
parts.text: A school has 400 students: 240 in Year 10 and 160 in Year 11. A stratified sample of 40 students is taken, with the numbers from each year proportional to the year group size. Find how many students are chosen from each year.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how the students from each year group should be chosen to form the sample.
parts.answer: Number the students in each year group and use random numbers (or a random draw) to select the required number from that group, without repetition
parts.working: Each year group is a stratum, and students are chosen at random within each stratum (B1); selection is without repetition (B1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A researcher uses systematic sampling to choose 25 houses from a numbered list of 500 houses. (a) State the sampling interval. (b) The random start is 7. List the numbers of the first three houses chosen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A market researcher stands outside a shopping centre in Lahore and asks the first 50 shoppers who pass by to answer a questionnaire. (a) Name this sampling method. (b) Give one disadvantage of this method.
parts.answer: (a) Opportunity (convenience) sampling  (b) for example: it is not random, so some groups of people (such as those who shop at other times) are not represented and the sample may be biased
parts.working: (a) opportunity or convenience sampling (B1); (b) any valid disadvantage such as bias, lack of randomness or non-representative sample (B2)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A survey of households in a district uses the list of registered voters as its sampling frame. (a) Define the term sampling frame. (b) Explain one reason why the list of registered voters might not be a suitable sampling frame for a survey of all households.
parts.answer: (a) A list of all members of the population from which the sample is taken  (b) for example: some households may contain non-registered adults, so they cannot be selected
parts.working: (a) a complete list of the population units (B2); (b) a valid reason such as incomplete coverage, out-of-date information or excluded members (B2)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A transport researcher wants to estimate the proportion of adults in a city who use public transport. She interviews people waiting at a Metro bus station between 8 am and 9 am on a Monday. Explain why this sample is likely to be biased.
parts.answer: People at a bus station are already public-transport users, and the time chosen only includes people commuting at that hour, so public-transport use will be overestimated
parts.working: B1 only people at a bus station (users) are sampled. B1 particular time/day excludes other groups; estimate too high.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest a better method of obtaining a sample.
parts.answer: Choose a random sample from a list of all adults in the city (e.g. electoral roll) using random numbers, and contact them
parts.working: B1 use a sampling frame of all adults. B1 random selection.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A survey of households in Punjab uses cluster sampling. Twelve villages are listed. Three villages are chosen at random and every household in each chosen village is surveyed. (a) Describe how the sample is obtained. (b) State one advantage and one disadvantage of cluster sampling in this situation.
parts.answer: (a) Choose 3 of the 12 villages at random and survey all households in them  (b) advantage: cheaper and quicker to reach households in a few places; disadvantage: households within a village may be similar, so the sample may be less representative
parts.working: (a) random selection of clusters, then full survey of each chosen cluster (B2); (b) one advantage (B1) and one disadvantage (B1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A company has 2000 employees in three departments: A has 1200, B has 600 and C has 200. A stratified sample of 60 employees is taken, with the numbers from each department proportional to its size. (a) Find how many employees are sampled from each department. (b) Explain why a stratified sample can give more reliable results than a simple random sample when the departments differ in their opinions.
parts.answer: (a) A: 36, B: 18, C: 6  (b) each department is represented in proportion to its size, so the sample reflects the population structure
parts.working: (a) A: 1200/2000 × 60 = 36, B: 18, C: 6 (M1 A2); (b) each stratum is represented, reducing the chance that a department is missed or over-represented (B1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A researcher wants to estimate the proportion of households in Lahore that have internet access. She telephones numbers from the local telephone directory between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays, and records the first 100 people who answer. (a) Identify two sources of bias in this survey. (b) Suggest one way the survey could be improved.
parts.answer: (a) Households without a listed landline and people who are at work during the calls are excluded; the first people to answer may not be typical  (b) for example use random digit dialling, and call at different times including evenings and weekends
parts.working: (a) any two valid sources of bias (B1 B1); (b) a sensible improvement (B2)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A researcher wants a simple random sample of 30 students from a list of 800 students numbered 001 to 800. Explain why choosing the first 30 students who arrive at the library on a Monday morning does not give a simple random sample.
parts.answer: Not every student has an equal chance of being selected, so the sample is biased towards students who arrive early on Monday
parts.working: Not every student has an equal chance of selection (B1); the sample is biased or unrepresentative (B1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how a table of random three-digit numbers could be used to choose the 30 students.
parts.answer: Read three-digit numbers in order; use a number only if it lies between 001 and 800, ignoring numbers outside this range or already chosen; stop when 30 different students have been selected
parts.working: Use only numbers from 001 to 800 (B1); ignore out-of-range and repeated numbers (B1); stop when 30 different students are chosen (B1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A simple random sample of 3 students is to be chosen from a group of 10 students. (a) Find the number of different possible samples. (b) Find the probability that a particular student is included in the sample.

parts.label: a
parts.text: There are four provinces in a country. Two provinces are chosen at random to be included in a survey. (a) Find the number of different possible pairs of provinces that could be chosen. (b) Find the probability that Punjab is one of the two chosen provinces.
parts.working: (a) number of pairs = C(4, 2) = 6 (M1 A1); (b) pairs containing Punjab = C(3, 1) = 3, so P = 3/6 = 1/2 (M1 A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The 75 members of a cricket club are numbered 01 to 75. The secretary uses the following two-digit random numbers, read from left to right, to choose a sample of 5 members:
53 82 07 53 66 91 24 75 00 38
Write down the numbers of the members chosen, explaining how any unsuitable numbers are dealt with.
parts.working: B1 ignore 82, 91 and 00 (out of range). B1 ignore the second 53 (repeat). B1 53, 07, 66, 24, 75.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between a population and a sample, and state one reason why a sample should be random.
parts.answer: The population is all members of the club; a sample is a subset of them. Random sampling gives every member an equal chance of selection, avoiding bias
parts.working: B1 population/sample distinction. B1 avoids bias / allows valid inference.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A survey sends a questionnaire to a random sample of 400 households. Only 320 households reply. Of these 320, 180 answer 'yes' to a question. The 80 households that did not reply are not known to the surveyor. (a) Find the least and greatest possible values of the proportion of all 400 households who would answer 'yes', if the non-respondents were all 'no' or all 'yes' respectively. (b) Explain why the survey may be biased even though the sample was random.
parts.answer: (a) least 0.45, greatest 0.65  (b) the non-response may be related to the question, so the 320 respondents may not represent the 400 households
parts.working: (a) least = 180/400 = 0.45 (M1 A1); greatest = (180 + 80)/400 = 0.65 (M1 A1); (b) non-response bias: the people who reply may differ from those who do not (A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A systematic sample of 50 members is taken from a list of 1000 members. The sampling interval is 20, and the 50th member selected is numbered 997. (a) Find the random start. (b) List the numbers of the first three members selected.
parts.working: The members selected are r, r + 20, …, r + 49 × 20 (M1); r + 980 = 997, so r = 17 (A2); the first three are 17, 37, 57 (A2)

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particles A and B, of masses 5 kg and 3 kg, are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string which passes over a fixed smooth pulley. The particles hang vertically and are released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles and the tension in the string.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particles P and Q, of masses 0.4 kg and 0.6 kg, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a fixed smooth pulley. Q is held 1.2 m above the floor with both parts of the string vertical and taut. Q is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of Q and the tension in the string.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed with which Q reaches the floor.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block P of mass 2 kg rests on a smooth horizontal table. It is attached to a light inextensible string which passes over a small smooth pulley at the edge of the table. The other end of the string carries a particle Q of mass 0.5 kg, which hangs freely. The system is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Two particles, of masses 0.8 kg and 1.2 kg, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a fixed smooth pulley, and released from rest with the string taut and both parts vertical.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles and the tension in the string.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the force exerted on the pulley by the string.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 3 kg lies on a rough horizontal table, where the coefficient of friction is 0.2. It is connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle of mass 2 kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the block to move 0.7 m, assuming it does not reach the pulley.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particles A and B, of masses 2 kg and 3 kg, are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string passing over a fixed smooth pulley. B is 1.5 m above the ground and A is on the ground, with the string taut. The system is released from rest. When B hits the ground it does not rebound. A does not reach the pulley.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles before B hits the ground.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of A when B hits the ground.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the greatest height of A above the ground.
parts.working: After B lands the string is slack; A moves freely under gravity (M1). Extra height = 6/(2 × 10) = 0.3 m (A1). Greatest height 1.5 + 0.3 = 1.8 m (A1).

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Two particles, of masses 1.5 kg and m kg, where m > 1.5, are connected by a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth pulley. When the system is released from rest, each particle has acceleration 2.5 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the tension in the string.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of m.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the force exerted by the string on the pulley.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle P of mass 4 kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is attached to a light inextensible string which runs parallel to a line of greatest slope, passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane, and carries a particle Q of mass 3 kg hanging vertically. The system is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the string.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block A of mass 5 kg is on a rough plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where tan α = 3/4. The coefficient of friction between A and the plane is 0.25. A is attached to a light inextensible string, parallel to a line of greatest slope, which passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane to a particle B of mass 6 kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest and B moves downwards.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the friction force acting on A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string.

practice.stem: Particle A, of mass 4 kg, rests on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between A and the table is 0.25. A light inextensible string is attached to A, passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table, and is attached to particle B, of mass 6 kg, which hangs freely below the pulley. The system is released from rest with the string taut and B does not reach the floor. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles.
parts.working:
M1 for B: 60 − T = 6a
M1 for A: T − F = 4a, with F = 0.25 × 40 = 10 N
M1 adding: 60 − 10 = 10a
A1 a = 5 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the string.
parts.working:
M1 substitute a = 5 into 60 − T = 6a
A1 T = 30 N (check: T − 10 = 4 × 5 gives T = 30)

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 4 kg rests on a rough horizontal table. It is connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle of mass 1 kg hanging freely. When the system is released from rest, the hanging particle descends 0.5 m in the first second.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the system.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the string and the coefficient of friction between the block and the table.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 8 kg is on a rough plane inclined at angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 0.28 and cos θ = 0.96. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. A light inextensible string attached to the block runs up the plane, parallel to a line of greatest slope, over a smooth pulley at the top, to a particle of mass m kg hanging freely.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of m for which the block is on the point of moving up the plane.
parts.answer: m = 4.544 (the block moves up the plane for any m greater than this)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that m = 6, find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block P of mass 2 kg is on a rough horizontal table, with coefficient of friction 0.4. A light inextensible string attached to P passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table and carries a particle Q of mass 3 kg, which hangs 0.9 m above the floor. The system is released from rest. Q does not rebound when it hits the floor, and P does not reach the pulley.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the system while Q is moving.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of P when Q hits the floor.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by P before it comes to rest.
parts.working: After Q lands, P decelerates at μg = 4 m s⁻² (M1). Distance = 7.92/8 = 0.99 m (A1). Total 0.9 + 0.99 = 1.89 m (A1).

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particles A and B, of masses 3 kg and m kg (m > 3), are connected by a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth pulley and released from rest. After 1.5 s the particles are moving with speed 3 m s⁻¹. At this instant the string breaks. Neither particle hits the pulley or the ground in the motion described.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles before the string breaks, and hence find m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time from the instant the string breaks until A returns to its starting position.
parts.working: A rose ½ × 2 × 1.5² = 2.25 m (B1). After the break, taking up as positive: −2.25 = 3t − 5t² (M1). 5t² − 3t − 2.25 = 0 (A1). t = (3 + √54)/10 = 1.03 s (A1).

practice.stem: Particle A, of mass 5 kg, lies on a smooth horizontal table. A light inextensible string is attached to A, passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table, and is attached to particle B, of mass m kg, which hangs vertically below the pulley. The system is released from rest and the acceleration of A is 2 m s⁻². Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the mass of B.
parts.working:
M1 for B: mg − T = ma
M1 for A: T = 5a = 10 N
A1 m(10 − 2) = 10 gives m = 1.25 kg

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the string.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the speed of A 3 seconds after the system is released from rest, given that B has not reached the floor.
parts.working:
M1 v = u + at = 0 + 2 × 3
A1 v = 6 m s⁻¹

practice.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg tows a trailer of mass 400 kg along a straight horizontal road by means of a light rigid tow-bar. The driving force of the car is 2400 N. The resistances to motion are 300 N on the car and 100 N on the trailer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car and trailer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.

practice.stem: On the Karachi–Hyderabad motorway, a truck of mass 3000 kg tows a broken-down car of mass 1000 kg with a light horizontal rope. The truck's driving force is 5000 N. The resistances are 800 N on the truck and 200 N on the car.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the rope.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken to increase speed from 8 m s⁻¹ to 20 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A car of mass 1100 kg tows a trailer of mass 300 kg along a straight horizontal road by a light tow-bar. The driving force of the car is 2650 N. The resistance to motion is 350 N on the car and 200 N on the trailer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car and trailer.
parts.working:
M1 treat as one system: driving force − resistances = total mass × a
M1 2650 − 350 − 200 = 1400a
A1 a = 1.5 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.

practice.stem: A lorry of mass 4000 kg pulls a trailer of mass 2000 kg along a straight horizontal road with a light tow-bar. The acceleration of the lorry and trailer is 0.5 m s⁻². The resistance to motion is 900 N on the lorry and 300 N on the trailer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the driving force of the lorry.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.

practice.stem: Particles P (mass 4 kg) and Q (mass 1 kg) lie on a smooth horizontal table and are joined by a light string. A horizontal force of 20 N acts on P, pulling both particles along the table in a straight line with the string taut. Take g = 10 m s⁻² where needed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles.
parts.working:
M1 whole system: 20 = (4 + 1)a
A1 a = 4 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the string joining P and Q.
parts.working:
M1 for Q: T = 1 × a
A1 T = 4 N

practice.stem: A car of mass 1400 kg tows a caravan of mass 600 kg along a horizontal road using a light rigid tow-bar. They are travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ when the car's brakes are applied, and they come to rest in 50 m with constant deceleration. The resistances to motion (not including braking) are 300 N on the car and 200 N on the caravan. The braking force acts on the car only.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the deceleration.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the braking force.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the force in the tow-bar, stating whether it is a tension or a thrust.
parts.working: Caravan decelerates at 4 m s⁻², needs 2400 N backwards (M1). Resistance gives 200 N, so tow-bar pushes back with 2200 N (A1): a thrust (A1).

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1000 kg tows a trailer of mass 250 kg up a straight hill inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.05, using a light rigid tow-bar parallel to the road. The driving force is 2000 N. Resistances to motion are 200 N on the car and 80 N on the trailer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car and trailer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Blocks A and B, of masses 3 kg and 2 kg, are on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. They are connected by a light inextensible string parallel to a line of greatest slope, with B below A. A force of 50 N, acting up the plane parallel to a line of greatest slope, is applied to A. The coefficient of friction between each block and the plane is 0.2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the blocks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the tension in the string is 20 N.
parts.working: B: T − 20 sin 30° − 3.464 = 2a (M1). T = 10 + 3.464 + 2 × 3.2679 = 20 N (A1). (Because both blocks have the same μ and slope, T = 50 × 2/5 exactly.)

practice.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg tows a trailer of mass 800 kg up a straight road inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 1/20. The driving force of the car is 4000 N. The resistance to motion is 200 N on the car and 150 N on the trailer. The tow-bar is light and parallel to the road. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car and trailer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.

practice.stem: Particle P, of mass 4 kg, lies on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A light string is attached to P, passes over a smooth pulley fixed at the top of the plane, and is attached to particle Q, of mass 3 kg, which hangs freely. The string is parallel to the plane and the system is released from rest. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles.
parts.working:
M1 whole system: 3g − 4g sin 30° = 7a
M1 30 − 20 = 7a
A1 a = 10/7 = 1.43 m s⁻² (3 s.f.)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the string.

practice.stem: A car of mass 1600 kg tows a trailer of mass 400 kg up a straight road inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 0.1. The driving force of the car is 3600 N, the resistance on the car is 400 N and the resistance on the trailer is 100 N. The tow-bar is light and parallel to the road. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car and trailer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.

practice.stem: A car of mass 900 kg tows a trailer of mass 300 kg along a straight horizontal road using a light rigid tow-bar. The car's driving force is 1800 N; the resistances are 150 N on the car and 90 N on the trailer, and these stay constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration and the tension in the tow-bar.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When the speed is 15 m s⁻¹ the tow-bar breaks. Find the distance the trailer travels after this before coming to rest.
parts.working: Trailer deceleration = 90/300 = 0.3 m s⁻² (M1 A1). 0 = 15² − 2 × 0.3 × s, s = 375 m (A1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the new acceleration of the car, assuming the driving force does not change.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A fixed wedge has two faces: face 1 is smooth and inclined at 30° to the horizontal, and face 2 is rough and inclined at 60° to the horizontal. The faces meet at a ridge where there is a small smooth pulley. Particle A, of mass 4 kg, is on face 1 and particle B, of mass 3 kg, is on face 2. They are connected by a light inextensible string over the pulley, each part parallel to a line of greatest slope. The coefficient of friction between B and face 2 is 0.2. The system is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that B moves down face 2.
parts.answer: Weight component of B down face 2 = 25.98 N > 20 N + friction 3 N
parts.working: B: 30 sin 60° = 25.98 N; A: 40 sin 30° = 20 N (M1). Even with maximum friction 0.2 × 30 cos 60° = 3 N opposing, 25.98 > 23, so B moves down (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles and the tension in the string.

practice.stem: A truck of mass 2000 kg tows a car of mass 1000 kg up a straight road inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 0.05. The truck and car move at constant speed. The resistance to motion is 600 N on the truck and 300 N on the car. The tow-bar is light and parallel to the road. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the driving force of the truck.
parts.working:
M1 constant speed, so the net force is zero for the whole system
M1 F = weight component + resistances = 3000 × 10 × 0.05 + 600 + 300
A1 F = 1500 + 900 = 2400 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar.
parts.working:
M1 car at constant speed: T = 1000 × 10 × 0.05 + 300
A1 T = 500 + 300 = 800 N

practice.stem: Car A, of mass 1000 kg, tows car B, of mass 800 kg, along a straight horizontal road by a light rope. The speed of the cars increases uniformly from 5 m s⁻¹ to 13 m s⁻¹ in 8 seconds. The resistance to motion is 200 N on car A and 100 N on car B.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the two cars.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the driving force of car A.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-rope.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box is released from rest on a smooth plane inclined at 20° to the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the box.
parts.working: ma = mg sin 20° (M1), a = 10 sin 20° = 3.42 m s⁻² (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the box after it has moved 4 m down the plane.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.5 kg slides down a rough plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where tan α = 3/4. The coefficient of friction is 0.5. The particle starts from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction and the friction force.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration and the distance travelled in the first 3 s.

practice.stem: A block of mass 5 kg is at rest on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force P, acting in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the horizontal force P.
parts.working:
M1 resolve parallel to the plane: P cos 30° = 5 × 10 × sin 30° (weight 50 N)
M1 P = 50 tan 30° = 50 × 0.5774
A1 P = 28.9 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the block and the plane.
parts.working:
M1 resolve perpendicular to the plane: R = 5 × 10 × cos 30° + P sin 30°
A1 R = 43.30 + 14.43 = 57.7 N (equivalently R = 50 ÷ cos 30°)

practice.stem: A particle P of mass 2 kg rests in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 0.6. P is held in place by a force of magnitude P acting up the line of greatest slope. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the force P.
parts.working:
M1 equilibrium along the plane: P = 2 × 10 × 0.6
A1 P = 12 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the particle and the plane.
parts.working:
M1 perpendicular to the plane: R = 2 × 10 × 0.8
A1 R = 16 N

practice.stem: A block of mass 6 kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A force of 10 N is applied to the block, acting down the line of greatest slope. The block starts from rest. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the block.
parts.working:
M1 along the plane (down positive): 6 × 10 × sin 30° + 10 = 6a
M1 30 + 10 = 6a
A1 a = 40 ÷ 6 = 6.67 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the block and the plane.
parts.working:
M1 perpendicular to the plane: R = 6 × 10 × cos 30°
A1 R = 51.96 N

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle is projected up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal, with initial speed 8 m s⁻¹. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is 0.3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the deceleration of the particle while it moves up the plane.
parts.working: Friction acts down the plane: a = g sin 25° + 0.3g cos 25° (M1 A1) = 6.95 m s⁻² (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance it travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the particle then slides back down, and find its speed when it returns to its starting point.
parts.answer: tan 25° = 0.466 > 0.3, so it slides; speed 3.73 m s⁻¹
parts.working: tan 25° > μ, so the weight component exceeds limiting friction (B1). Down: a = 10(sin 25° − 0.3 cos 25°) = 1.5073 (M1 A1). v = √(2 × 1.5073 × 4.6076) = 3.73 m s⁻¹ (A1).

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 15 kg is pulled up a rough ramp inclined at 15° to the horizontal by a rope. The rope makes an angle of 20° above the line of greatest slope of the ramp, and the tension in it is 120 N. The coefficient of friction is 0.35.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the crate and the ramp.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the crate.

practice.stem: A block of mass 10 kg is at rest on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. No other force acts on the block. The friction force on the block acts up the plane. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the friction force and the normal reaction acting on the block.
parts.answer: friction 50 N; normal reaction 86.6 N (3 s.f.)
parts.working:
M1 friction F = 10 × 10 × sin 30° = 50 N
M1 normal reaction R = 10 × 10 × cos 30°
A1 R = 86.6 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the block can rest in equilibrium on this plane only if the coefficient of friction μ is at least 0.577.
parts.working:
M1 limiting condition F ≤ μR
A1 μ ≥ 50/86.6 = 0.577 (3 s.f.)

practice.stem: A block of mass 3 kg rests on a smooth plane inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 0.8 and cos θ = 0.6. The block is pushed up the plane by a horizontal force P, in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope, and accelerates up the plane at 2 m s⁻². Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the block and the plane.
parts.working:
M1 perpendicular to the plane: R = mg cos θ + P sin θ = 3 × 10 × 0.6 + 50 × 0.8
A1 R = 18 + 40 = 58 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the horizontal force P.
parts.working:
M1 along the plane: P cos θ − mg sin θ = ma
M1 0.6P − 24 = 3 × 2
A1 P = 50 N

practice.stem: A particle of mass 5 kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A force of 40 N acts on the particle parallel to the plane, pulling it up the line of greatest slope. The particle starts from rest. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particle up the plane.
parts.working:
M1 along the plane: 40 − 5 × 10 × sin 30° = 5a
M1 40 − 25 = 5a
A1 a = 3 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the particle and the plane.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A small block is released from rest on a rough plane inclined at 35° to the horizontal. It slides 6 m down a line of greatest slope in the first 2 s.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the block.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the block and the plane.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one assumption made in your model.
parts.answer: e.g. the block is a particle / no air resistance / friction is constant

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 4 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.25. A horizontal force of 60 N, in the vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope, pushes the particle up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction and the acceleration of the particle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When the particle's speed is 5 m s⁻¹ the horizontal force is removed. Find how much further the particle travels up the plane.

practice.stem: A crate of mass 12 kg is pulled up a rough straight ramp inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 5/13 and cos θ = 12/13. The crate is pulled by a rope of tension 100 N acting parallel to the ramp. The coefficient of friction between the crate and the ramp is 0.3. The crate moves up the ramp. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the crate and the ramp.
parts.working:
M1 perpendicular to the ramp: R = 12 × 10 × cos θ, with cos θ = 12/13
A1 R = 1440/13 = 110.8 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the crate up the ramp.
parts.working:
M1 friction F = 0.3 × 110.8 = 33.2 N, acting down the ramp
M1 weight component down the ramp: 120 × 5/13 = 46.2 N
M1 12a = 100 − 46.2 − 33.2
A1 a = 1.72 m s⁻²

practice.stem: A particle is placed on a rough plane. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is 0.4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle rests in equilibrium on a rough plane with coefficient of friction 0.4. Find the greatest angle θ to the horizontal for which the particle can rest in equilibrium with no other force acting.
parts.working:
M1 limiting equilibrium: mg sin θ = μ mg cos θ, so tan θ = μ
A1 θ = arctan 0.4 = 21.8°

parts.label: b
parts.text: The same particle is now released from rest on a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Find its acceleration down the plane. Take g = 10 m s⁻².
parts.working:
M1 perpendicular: R = mg cos 30°
M1 along the plane: ma = mg sin 30° − 0.4 × mg cos 30°
A1 a = 10(0.5 − 0.4 × 0.866) = 1.54 m s⁻²

practice.stem: A block of mass m kg is released from rest at the top of a rough plane inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where sin θ = 0.6 and cos θ = 0.8. It slides a distance of 20 m down a line of greatest slope in 4 seconds. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the block down the plane.
parts.working:
M1 s = ½at², so 20 = ½ × a × 16
A1 a = 2.5 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the block and the plane.
parts.working:
M1 along the plane: ma = mg sin θ − μ mg cos θ, so 2.5 = 10(0.6 − 0.8μ)
M1 0.25 = 0.6 − 0.8μ
A1 μ = 0.35/0.8 = 0.4375

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 50 kg is pulled across a rough horizontal warehouse floor by a horizontal force of 180 N. The coefficient of friction is 0.3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the crate.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Starting from rest, find the speed after 5 s.

practice.stem: A trolley of mass 8 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the trolley and the floor is 0.3. The trolley is pushed by a force of 40 N acting at 30° below the horizontal. The trolley moves in a straight line. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the trolley and the floor.
parts.working:
M1 vertically: R = 80 + 40 sin 30°
A1 R = 80 + 20 = 100 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the trolley.
parts.working:
M1 friction = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N
M1 horizontally: 40 cos 30° − 30 = 8a
A1 a = (34.64 − 30) ÷ 8 = 0.58 m s⁻²

practice.stem: A block of mass 6 kg lies on a rough horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.2. A horizontal force of 30 N acts on the block and it moves in the direction of the force. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the friction force acting on the block.
parts.working:
M1 friction = μR = 0.2 × 60
A1 F = 12 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the block.

practice.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg is travelling along a straight horizontal road at 20 m s⁻¹ when the driver applies the brakes. The braking force is 4000 N and the resistance to motion is 800 N. The car is brought to rest with uniform deceleration.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the deceleration of the car.
parts.working:
M1 total retarding force 4000 + 800 = 4800 N
A1 deceleration = 4800 ÷ 1200 = 4 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance the car travels before it stops.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A child pulls a sledge of mass 30 kg across level snow in Naltar using a rope inclined at 25° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is 100 N and the coefficient of friction between the sledge and the snow is 0.15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction on the sledge.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the sledge.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². An ice-hockey puck slides in a straight line on a horizontal rink. Its speed falls from 12 m s⁻¹ to 4 m s⁻¹ while it travels 40 m. The only horizontal force is friction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the deceleration of the puck.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for this part of the motion.

practice.stem: A block of mass 4 kg rests on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between the block and the table is 0.5. A horizontal force P acts on the block, and the block accelerates in the direction of P at 3 m s⁻². Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the friction force acting on the block.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the horizontal force P.

practice.stem: A block of mass 5 kg is pulled along a rough horizontal floor at constant speed by a light rope. The tension in the rope is 15 N and the rope is inclined at 20° above the horizontal. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the block and the floor.
parts.working:
M1 vertically: R + 15 sin 20° = 5 × 10
A1 R = 50 − 5.13 = 44.9 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the block and the floor.
parts.working:
M1 constant speed, so horizontal forces balance: 15 cos 20° = F
M1 F = μR
A1 μ = 14.10 ÷ 44.87 = 0.314

practice.stem: A crate of mass 12 kg is pulled along a rough horizontal floor by a horizontal force of 60 N. The crate accelerates at 1.5 m s⁻² in the direction of the force. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the friction force acting on the crate.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 3 kg slides along a rough horizontal plane. It passes a point with speed 8 m s⁻¹ and comes to rest 16 m further along the plane after a uniform deceleration over 4 seconds. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the deceleration of the particle.
parts.working:
M1 a = (8 − 0) ÷ 4
A1 deceleration 2 m s⁻²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the friction force acting on the particle.
parts.working:
M1 friction is the only horizontal force: F = 3 × 2
A1 F = 6 N

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane.
parts.working:
M1 normal reaction R = 3 × 10 = 30 N
A1 μ = 6 ÷ 30 = 0.2

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 20 kg is on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.4. A force of magnitude P N is applied to the box, directed downwards at 30° below the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that the box moves at constant speed, find P, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the box when P = 150.

practice.stem: A crate of mass 25 kg lies on a rough horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor is 0.4. A force P acts on the crate at 15° below the horizontal and pushes it in the direction of motion. The crate accelerates at 0.9 m s⁻². Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the force P.
parts.working:
M1 vertically: R = 25 × 10 + P sin 15° (P pushes down)
M1 friction F = 0.4R
M1 horizontally: P cos 15° − F = 25 × 0.9 = 22.5
M1 P cos 15° − 0.4(250 + P sin 15°) = 22.5 gives P(cos 15° − 0.4 sin 15°) = 122.5
A1 P = 122.5 ÷ 0.8624 = 142 N

practice.stem: A sled of mass 40 kg is pulled across horizontal snow by a light rope of tension 200 N. The rope is inclined at 30° above the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the sled and the snow is 0.25. The sled moves in a straight line. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the sled and the snow.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the sled.

practice.stem: A crate of mass 60 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor, and the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor is 0.5. A force P is applied to the crate at 40° below the horizontal, pushing it. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: The crate is at rest and P is gradually increased. Find the value of P at the instant the crate is on the point of moving.
parts.working:
M1 vertically: R = 600 + P sin 40°
M1 limiting friction F = μR = 0.5R
M1 horizontally: P cos 40° = 0.5(600 + P sin 40°)
A1 P(cos 40° − 0.5 sin 40°) = 300, so P = 300 ÷ 0.4446 = 675 N

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the direction of the friction force at the instant the crate is on the point of moving.
parts.answer: Friction acts opposite to the horizontal component of P (backwards), at its limiting value μR = 0.5R.
parts.working: B1 friction opposes the tendency to move, so acts opposite to the horizontal component of P, at its limiting value

practice.stem: A block of mass 4 kg lies on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between the block and the table is 0.3. A light string attached to the block is inclined at 35° above the horizontal and the block is pulled in the direction of the string. The block accelerates at 1.2 m s⁻². Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the tension T in the string.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the normal reaction between the block and the table.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 5 kg rests in equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction and the frictional force acting on the box.
parts.answer: R = 45.3 N, F = 21.1 N up the slope
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular: R = 50 cos 25°; A1 45.3 N; B1 F = 50 sin 25° = 21.1 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least possible value of the coefficient of friction.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of mass 3 kg is on the point of slipping down a rough plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.6. Find the normal reaction, the frictional force and the coefficient of friction.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1200 kg is parked with its brakes on, at rest on a straight road on a hill near Murree. The road is inclined at 8° to the horizontal. Treat the car as a particle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the frictional force and the normal reaction acting on the car.
parts.working: M1 resolve along and perpendicular to the road; A1 F = 12000 sin 8° = 1670 N; A1 R = 12000 cos 8° = 11 900 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least possible coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box of mass 4 kg rests in equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at 15° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the normal reaction and the frictional force acting on the box.
parts.answer: R = 37.9 N; F = 10.1 N (up the plane)
parts.working: Resolve perpendicular to plane: R = 4g cos 15° = 37.9 N. Resolve along plane: F = 4g sin 15° = 10.1 N. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The coefficient of friction between the box and the plane is 0.3. Show that the box is in equilibrium.
parts.answer: Limiting friction = 0.3 × 37.9 = 11.4 N > 10.1 N, so the box is in equilibrium
parts.working: The friction needed (10.1 N) is less than the greatest friction possible (11.4 N), so equilibrium is maintained. M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of mass 2.5 kg is on the point of slipping down a rough plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where tan α = 5/12. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the normal reaction and the frictional force acting on the particle.
parts.answer: R = 22.6 N; F = 9.42 N (up the plane)
parts.working: sin α = 5/13, cos α = 12/13. R = 2.5g cos α = 24.5 × 12/13 = 22.6 N. Limiting friction along the plane = 2.5g sin α = 24.5 × 5/13 = 9.42 N, acting up the plane. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 8 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 20° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. A force of magnitude P N acts on the crate up the line of greatest slope.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the least value of P for which the crate remains at rest.
parts.working: M1 R = 80 cos 20° = 75.18 N; M1 friction acts up the slope, F = 0.3R = 22.55 N; M1 P + F = 80 sin 20°; A1 P = 4.81 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of P for which the crate remains at rest.
parts.working: M1 friction now down the slope: P = 80 sin 20° + 22.55; A1 49.9 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 4 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.2. A horizontal force of magnitude P N, in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope, acts on the block towards the plane, and the block is about to move up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the normal reaction is (40 cos 30° + P sin 30°) N.
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular to the plane, horizontal force has component P sin 30° into the plane; A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of P.
parts.working: M1 resolve along the plane: P cos 30° = 40 sin 30° + F; M1 F = 0.2R; A1 P(cos 30° − 0.2 sin 30°) = 20 + 8 cos 30°; A1 P = 35.2.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 6 kg is on a rough ramp inclined at 10° to the horizontal at a warehouse in Faisalabad. A rope pulls the box with a force of 30 N acting at 15° above the line of greatest slope, up the ramp. The box is about to move up the ramp.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the box and the ramp.
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular: R + 30 sin 15° = 60 cos 10°; A1 R = 51.32 N; M1 resolve parallel: 30 cos 15° = F + 60 sin 10°; A1 F = 18.56 N; M1 μ = F/R; A1 0.362.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass 5 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.2. A light rope, parallel to a line of greatest slope, pulls the block up the plane with tension T N. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Show that the block remains in equilibrium provided 11.8 ≤ T ≤ 29.6.
parts.answer: Limits: T = mg sin 25° ± μmg cos 25° = 20.7 ± 8.9, so 11.8 ≤ T ≤ 29.6
parts.working: mg sin 25° = 20.71 N, μmg cos 25° = 0.2 × 44.41 = 8.88 N. Friction must act down the plane for T > 20.7 and up the plane for T < 20.7, with magnitude at most 8.89 N. M1 resolving, M1 friction limits, A1 both limits.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the frictional force on the block when T = 25 N, and state its direction.
parts.working: With T = 25 N the block would tend to move up, so friction acts down the plane: F = T − mg sin 25° = 25 − 20.71 = 4.3 N. M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass 6 kg lies on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A horizontal force of magnitude 25 N acts on the block, in the vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope, pushing the block towards the plane and up the slope. The block is on the point of sliding down the slope. Find the normal reaction between the block and the plane.
parts.working: R = mg cos 30° + 25 sin 30° = 50.9 + 12.5 = 63.4 N. M1 resolve perpendicular, M1 horizontal force component, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least coefficient of friction needed to keep the block in equilibrium.
parts.working: Along the plane: friction F = mg sin 30° − 25 cos 30° = 29.4 − 21.65 = 7.75 N up the plane. μ ≥ F/R = 7.75/63.4 = 0.122. M1 friction, M1 divide, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A trolley of mass 25 kg is on a rough plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where tan α = 5/12. The coefficient of friction is 0.4. A light rope parallel to the line of greatest slope pulls the trolley up the plane. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the least tension in the rope for the trolley to begin to move up the plane.
parts.working: sin α = 5/13, cos α = 12/13. Limiting case: T = mg sin α + μmg cos α = 245(5/13 + 0.4 × 12/13) = 245 × 9.8/13 = 184.7 N. M1 resolving, M1 limiting friction, M1 substitute, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When the tension is 100 N, the trolley is in equilibrium. Find the frictional force acting on the trolley, stating its direction.
parts.working: mg sin α = 245 × 5/13 = 94.2 N, which is less than 100 N, so friction acts down the plane: F = 100 − 94.2 = 5.8 N. M1 comparison, M1 F, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle A of mass 4 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.2. A light string attached to A runs parallel to a line of greatest slope, passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane and is attached to a particle B hanging freely below the pulley. Find the range of the mass of B for which the system is in equilibrium.
parts.working: For B: T = mg. For A: T − 4g sin 30° = F with |F| ≤ μ × 4g cos 30°. So mg ∈ [4g sin 30° − μ(4g cos 30°), 4g sin 30° + μ(4g cos 30°)], giving m ∈ [2 − 0.693, 2 + 0.693] = [1.31, 2.69] kg. M1 for B, M1 for A, M1 limits, A1 both limits, A1 interval.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 2.5 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 35° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.4. A force of magnitude P N acts on the particle at an angle of 20° above the line of greatest slope, directed up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the set of values of P for which the particle remains in equilibrium.
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular: R = 25 cos 35° − P sin 20°; M1 about to slide up: P cos 20° = 25 sin 35° + 0.4R; A1 P = 20.9; M1 about to slide down: P cos 20° + 0.4R = 25 sin 35°; A1 P = 7.66; M1 both cases used with correct friction directions; A1 7.66 ≤ P ≤ 20.9; B1 check R > 0 in both cases.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest angle of a slope on which a block can rest without any applied force, if the coefficient of friction is 0.5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A block of mass 3 kg is placed on a slope inclined at 40° with the same coefficient of friction, and a force of 12 N acts on it up the line of greatest slope. Determine whether the block remains at rest, and find the magnitude and direction of the frictional force.
parts.answer: Remains at rest; friction 7.28 N up the slope
parts.working: M1 R = 30 cos 40° = 22.98 N; A1 maximum friction 11.49 N; M1 force needed to hold: 30 sin 40° − 12 = 7.28 N; A1 7.28 < 11.49 so at rest; A1 friction 7.28 N acting up the slope.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box of mass 10 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 20° to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.6. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². A force of magnitude P N acts parallel to a line of greatest slope, with P taken positive when the force acts up the plane. Find the range of values of P for which the box remains in equilibrium.
parts.answer: −21.7 ≤ P ≤ 88.8, i.e. from 21.7 N down the plane to 88.8 N up the plane
parts.working: Friction limits: P − mg sin 20° ∈ [−μmg cos 20°, μmg cos 20°]. mg sin 20° = 33.52 N, μmg cos 20° = 55.25 N. So P ∈ [33.52 − 55.25, 33.52 + 55.25] = [−21.73, 88.77], i.e. −21.7 ≤ P ≤ 88.8. M1 friction limits, M1 numbers, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the greatest force up the plane and the greatest force down the plane for which the box stays at rest.
parts.answer: Up the plane: 88.8 N; down the plane: 21.7 N
parts.working: Positive P is up the plane (P = 88.8 N); negative P is down the plane (P = −21.7 N, i.e. 21.7 N down). B1, B1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three horizontal forces act on a particle: 12 N due east, 9 N due north and 5 N due west. Find the magnitude of the resultant force and the angle it makes with due east.
parts.working: M1 resultant components 7 N east, 9 N north; M1 √(7² + 9²); A1 11.4 N; A1 tan⁻¹(9/7) = 52.1° north of east.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three horizontal forces act at a point O: 4 N due north, 3 N due east and 2 N due south. Find the magnitude of the resultant force.
parts.working: Resultant components: east 3 N, north 4 − 2 = 2 N. Magnitude = √(3² + 2²) = √13 = 3.61 N. M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the bearing of the resultant force, correct to the nearest degree.
parts.working: Bearing = tan⁻¹(3/2) = 56.3° from north towards east, so 056°. M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes 8 N and 6 N act at a point. The 8 N force acts at 45° above the positive x-axis and the 6 N force acts at 135° above the positive x-axis. Find the x- and y-components of the resultant.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A third force F is applied at the same point so that the three forces are in equilibrium. Find the magnitude of F, and the angle it makes with the positive x-axis, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.answer: F = 10.0 N at 261.9° to the positive x-axis
parts.working: F is equal and opposite to the resultant, so |F| = 10.0 N and its direction is 180° + 81.9° = 261.9°. M1 F opposite to the resultant, M1 magnitude, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes 20 N and 15 N act at a point O. The 20 N force acts at 30° above the positive x-axis and the 15 N force acts at 120° to the positive x-axis. Find the magnitude of the resultant and the angle it makes with the positive x-axis.
parts.answer: 25 N at 66.9° to the positive x-axis
parts.working: M1 the forces are perpendicular (or resolve both); A1 magnitude 25 N; M1 angle with the 20 N force tan⁻¹(15/20) = 36.9°; A1 30° + 36.9° = 66.9°.

practice.stem: Forces of magnitudes 10 N, 14 N and P N act at a point. The 10 N force acts along the positive x-axis, the 14 N force acts at 60° anticlockwise from the positive x-axis and the P N force acts along the negative y-axis. The resultant of the three forces acts along the positive x-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of P.
parts.working: M1 resultant has no y-component: 14 sin 60° − P = 0; A1 P = 7√3 = 12.1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the resultant.

practice.stem: Three horizontal ropes pull on a ring fixed to a post on a boat at Keamari harbour. The forces are 25 N on a bearing of 040°, 18 N on a bearing of 160° and 30 N on a bearing of 270°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the resultant force and its bearing.
parts.working: M1 resolve east: 25 sin 40° + 18 sin 160° − 30 = −7.774; M1 resolve north: 25 cos 40° + 18 cos 160° = 2.237; A1 both components; M1 magnitude √(7.774² + 2.237²); A1 8.09 N; A1 bearing 270° + tan⁻¹(2.237/7.774) = 286°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three forces act at a point: 12 N along the positive x-axis, 8 N at 120° anticlockwise from the positive x-axis, and 5 N at 240° anticlockwise from the positive x-axis. Find the magnitude of the resultant.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle the resultant makes with the positive x-axis, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces P and Q act at a point. The angle between their directions is 150°. Their resultant R has magnitude 12 N and is perpendicular to P. Find P and Q in exact form.
parts.working: R is perpendicular to P, so P + Q cos 150° = 0, giving P = Q√3/2. The magnitude of R is Q sin 150° = Q/2 = 12, so Q = 24 and P = 12√3. M1 perpendicular condition, M1 magnitude, A1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes 9 N and 15 N act at a point. Their resultant has magnitude 20 N. Find the angle between the directions of the two forces, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A boat is acted on by two horizontal forces: 40 N on a bearing of 075° and 25 N on a bearing of 200°. Find the magnitude of the resultant force, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the bearing of the resultant force, correct to the nearest degree.

practice.stem: Three forces act at a point O: 6 N along the positive x-axis, 8 N along the positive y-axis, and F N acting in the third quadrant at an angle θ below the negative x-axis. The resultant of the three forces is 5 N along the positive y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find F and θ.
parts.working: M1 resolve along x: 6 − F cos θ = 0; M1 resolve along y: 8 − F sin θ = 5; A1 F cos θ = 6, F sin θ = 3; A1 F = √45 = 6.71; A1 θ = tan⁻¹(0.5) = 26.6°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes P N and Q N act at a point, and the angle between their directions is 130°. Their resultant has magnitude 20 N and is perpendicular to the force of magnitude P N. Find Q and P.
parts.working: M1 resolve along P: P + Q cos 130° = 0; M1 resolve perpendicular to P: Q sin 130° = 20; A1 Q = 20/sin 50° = 26.1; M1 P = Q cos 50°; A1 16.8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three forces act at a point: F₁ = (3i + 4j) N, F₂ = (−i + 5j) N and F₃ = (ai + bj) N. The resultant of the three forces is (10i) N. Find a and b.
parts.working: Sum of i components: 3 − 1 + a = 10, so a = 8. Sum of j components: 4 + 5 + b = 0, so b = −9. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of F₃ and the angle it makes with the positive x-axis, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.answer: √145 ≈ 12.0 N at −48.4° to the positive x-axis

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes 6 N and 10 N act at a point, and the angle between their directions is θ. The magnitude of their resultant is 12 N. Show that cos θ = 1/15 and find θ in degrees, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: R² = 6² + 10² + 2 × 6 × 10 cos θ, so 144 = 136 + 120 cos θ, giving cos θ = 8/120 = 1/15. θ = 86.2°. M1 cosine rule, M1 substitution, A1 cos θ, A1 θ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle the resultant makes with the 6 N force, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: Taking the 6 N force along the x-axis, the resultant is (6 + 10 cos θ, 10 sin θ) = (6.67, 9.98), so its angle with the 6 N force is tan⁻¹(9.98/6.67) = 56.3°. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes 4 N and 7 N act at a point. The angle between their directions can take any value θ, where 0 ≤ θ ≤ 180°. Find the greatest and least possible magnitudes of the resultant.
parts.working: R² = 16 + 49 + 56 cos θ = 65 + 56 cos θ, which is greatest when cos θ = 1 and least when cos θ = −1. R = 11 N or R = 3 N. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of θ for which the magnitude of the resultant is 9 N, correct to 1 decimal place.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A lantern of mass 2 kg hangs in equilibrium from two light strings. One string makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal and the other makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal, on the other side.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the tension in each string.
parts.working: M1 resolve horizontally: T₁ cos 30° = T₂ cos 60°; M1 resolve vertically: T₁ sin 30° + T₂ sin 60° = 20; A1 one equation solved for a ratio, T₂ = √3 T₁; A1 T₁ = 10 N; A1 T₂ = 17.3 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.8 kg hangs in equilibrium from two light strings, each making an angle of 40° with the vertical.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the tension in each string.
parts.working: M1 by symmetry the tensions are equal; M1 2T cos 40° = 8; A1 T = 5.22 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of mass 5 kg is suspended in equilibrium by two light strings. One string makes an angle of 35° with the horizontal and the other makes an angle of 55° with the horizontal, on the opposite side. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the tension in each string.
parts.answer: T (35° string) = 28.1 N; T (55° string) = 40.1 N
parts.working: Horizontal: T₁ cos 35° = T₂ cos 55°. Vertical: T₁ sin 35° + T₂ sin 55° = 49. Solving: T₁ = 28.1 N, T₂ = 40.1 N. M1 horizontal, M1 vertical, M1 solve, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of mass 2.5 kg hangs in equilibrium from a light string. A horizontal force of 20 N holds the particle so that the string makes an angle θ with the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the tension in the string.
parts.working: Tension T = √(24.5² + 20²) = √(600.25 + 400) = 31.6 N. M1 components, M1 Pythagoras, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle θ, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of weight 40 N is held in equilibrium by two light strings. String A makes an angle of 60° above the horizontal and string B is horizontal. Find the tension in each string, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Vertical: T_A sin 60° = 40, so T_A = 46.2 N. Horizontal: T_B = T_A cos 60° = 23.1 N. M1, M1, A1, A1.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A ball of mass 3 kg is attached to one end of a light string whose other end is fixed. The ball is held in equilibrium, with the string taut, by a horizontal force of 12 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the angle the string makes with the vertical and the tension in the string.
parts.working: M1 resolve: T sin α = 12, T cos α = 30; A1 tan α = 0.4, α = 21.8°; M1 T = √(12² + 30²); A1 32.3 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Two points A and B are on a horizontal ceiling, 1.0 m apart. A particle C of mass 5 kg is attached to light inextensible strings AC and BC, of lengths 0.8 m and 0.6 m, and hangs in equilibrium below AB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that angle ACB is a right angle, and find the angles that AC and BC make with the horizontal.
parts.answer: AC at 36.9°, BC at 53.1° to the horizontal

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tensions in AC and BC.
parts.working: M1 horizontal: 0.8 T_A = 0.6 T_B; M1 vertical: 0.6 T_A + 0.8 T_B = 50; A1 T_A = 30 N; A1 T_B = 40 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of mass 7 kg is in equilibrium under the action of two light strings. One string makes an angle of 50° above the horizontal, on the left, and the other makes an angle of 30° above the horizontal, on the right. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the tension in each string, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Horizontal: T₁ cos 50° = T₂ cos 30°. Vertical: T₁ sin 50° + T₂ sin 30° = 68.6. Then T₁ = 60.3 N and T₂ = 44.8 N. M1 horizontal, M1 vertical, M1 solve, A1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is held in equilibrium by a light string, which makes an angle of 35° with the vertical, and by a horizontal force. The tension in the string is 25 N. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the mass of the particle, correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.working: Vertical: T cos 35° = mg, so m = 25 cos 35°/9.8 = 2.09 kg. M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the horizontal force, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: Horizontal: H = T sin 35° = 25 sin 35° = 14.3 N. M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of mass 4 kg rests in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is held there by a light string parallel to a line of greatest slope. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the tension in the string and the normal reaction between the particle and the plane.
parts.working: Along the plane: T = mg sin 30° = 19.6 N. Perpendicular to the plane: R = mg cos 30° = 33.9 N. M1, M1, A1, A1.

practice.stem: A particle of weight 20 N hangs in equilibrium from two light strings. One string has tension 15 N and makes an angle of 25° above the horizontal. The other string, on the opposite side, has tension T N and makes an angle θ above the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find T and θ.
parts.working: M1 horizontal: T cos θ = 15 cos 25°; M1 vertical: T sin θ + 15 sin 25° = 20; A1 T cos θ = 13.59, T sin θ = 13.66; A1 T = 19.3; A1 θ = 45.1°.

practice.stem: A light inextensible string of length 1.8 m has its ends fixed at points A and B on the same horizontal level, 1.2 m apart. A small smooth ring of weight 6 N is threaded on the string.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The ring hangs at rest at the midpoint of the string. Find the tension in the string, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 each half 0.9 m with horizontal 0.6 m, so vertical drop √(0.9² − 0.6²) = √0.45 = 0.671 m and sine of angle to horizontal = 0.671/0.9 = 0.745; M1 2T × 0.745 = 6; A1 T = 4.02 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A horizontal force of magnitude F N, acting in the direction from A to B, is now applied to the ring, so that it rests vertically below B with both parts of the string taut. Show that the ring is 0.5 m below B, and find the tension in the string and the value of F.
parts.working: M1 AR = 1.8 − BR and AR² = 1.2² + BR², so (1.8 − d)² = 1.44 + d²; A1 d = 0.5, AR = 1.3; B1 tension the same in both parts (smooth ring); M1 vertical: T + T × (5/13) = 6, so T = 13/3 = 4.33 N; A1 horizontal: F = T × 12/13 = 4 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of weight 60 N is held in equilibrium by a light string inclined at 40° to the vertical and by a force of magnitude P N. The force P is as small as possible. Find the least value of P, and the tension in the string when P has this value. Give each answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: The three forces form a triangle. The smallest P is perpendicular to the string: P = 60 sin 40° = 38.6 N. The tension then equals 60 cos 40° = 46.0 N. M1 triangle of forces, M1 perpendicular, M1 P, M1 T, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle A of mass 6 kg is on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A light string attached to A runs parallel to a line of greatest slope, passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane and carries a particle B of mass m kg hanging freely. Show that the system is in equilibrium only when m = 3.
parts.answer: Equilibrium: T = 6g sin 30° and T = mg, so m = 3
parts.working: Plane is smooth, so the equation for A: T = 6g sin 30° = 3g. For B: T = mg. So m = 3. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The plane is now rough, with coefficient of friction 0.2. Find the range of values of m for which the system remains in equilibrium, giving your answers correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.working: Friction in the range ±μ × 6g cos 30°: m ∈ [6 sin 30° − 0.2 × 6 cos 30°, 6 sin 30° + 0.2 × 6 cos 30°] = [1.96, 4.04]. M1 friction limits, M1 both limits, A1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle P of mass 6 kg is suspended from two light strings PA and PB, where A and B are fixed points on a horizontal ceiling with AB = 1.6 m, AP = 1.0 m and BP = 1.2 m. The strings make angles α and β with the ceiling, at A and B respectively. Show that cos α = 0.6625 and cos β = 0.78125 by the cosine rule.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in each string, correct to 3 significant figures, taking g = 9.8 m s⁻².
parts.working: Horizontal: T_A cos α = T_B cos β. Vertical: T_A sin α + T_B sin β = 58.8. Solving: T_A = 46.0 N and T_B = 39.0 N. M1 horizontal, M1 vertical, M1 solve, A1, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three horizontal forces: 6 N due east, 8 N due north and a third force. Find the magnitude and bearing of the third force.
parts.working: M1 third force has components 6 W and 8 S; A1 10 N; A1 bearing 180° + tan⁻¹(6/8) = 216.9°.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: A particle of weight 12 N rests on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force of magnitude P N acting towards the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of P and the normal reaction.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: R cos 30° = 12; A1 R = 13.9 N; M1 resolve horizontally: P = R sin 30°; A1 P = 12 tan 30° = 6.93.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces. Two of the forces are 12 N along the positive x-axis and 9 N along the positive y-axis. Find the magnitude of the third force.
parts.working: Third force = −(12i + 9j), magnitude √(12² + 9²) = √225 = 15 N. M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the direction of the third force, measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis, correct to 1 decimal place.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces: 5 N along the positive x-axis, 7 N at 120° anticlockwise from the positive x-axis, and a third force F N. Find the magnitude of F, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Sum of components: x: 5 + 7 cos 120° + F_x = 0, so F_x = −1.5 N. y: 7 sin 120° + F_y = 0, so F_y = −6.06 N. |F| = √(1.5² + 6.06²) = 6.24 N. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle that F makes with the positive x-axis, correct to 1 decimal place.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle of weight 15 N is in equilibrium under three forces: its weight, a horizontal force P N acting to the left, and a force of 25 N acting at an angle θ above the horizontal and to the right. Find the value of θ, correct to 1 decimal place, and the value of P.
parts.working: Vertical: 25 sin θ = 15, so sin θ = 0.6 and θ = 36.9°. Horizontal: P = 25 cos θ = 25 × 0.8 = 20 N. M1 vertical, M1 θ, M1 horizontal, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: Three forces of magnitudes 10 N, P N and Q N act on a particle, which is in equilibrium. The 10 N force acts at 30° above the positive x-axis, the P N force acts along the negative x-axis and the Q N force acts at 60° below the positive x-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of P and Q.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: 10 sin 30° = Q sin 60°; A1 Q = 5.77; M1 resolve horizontally: P = 10 cos 30° + Q cos 60°; A1 cos values correct; A1 P = 11.5.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces. Two of them have magnitudes 12 N and 15 N, and the angle between their directions is 70°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the third force.
parts.working: M1 third force balances the resultant of the other two; M1 R² = 12² + 15² + 2(12)(15) cos 70°; A1 22.2 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle between the third force and the 12 N force.
parts.working: M1 angle between resultant and 12 N force: sin φ = 15 sin 70°/22.18; A1 φ = 39.4°; A1 third force at 180° − 39.4° = 140.6° to the 12 N force.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three coplanar forces of magnitudes 13 N, 14 N and 15 N. Show that the angle between the directions of the 13 N and 14 N forces is 112.6°, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: The three forces form a triangle with sides 13, 14 and 15. The interior angle opposite the 15 N side has cos = (13² + 14² − 15²)/(2 × 13 × 14) = 140/364 = 0.3846, so the angle is 67.4°. The angle between the force directions is 180° − 67.4° = 112.6°. M1 triangle, M1 cosine rule, M1 supplement, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three coplanar forces P, Q and R, where R = 20 N. The angle between P and Q is 110°, the angle between Q and R is 130°, and the angle between R and P is 120°. Use the triangle of forces and the sine rule to find P and Q, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Interior angles of the triangle of forces: 50° opposite P, 60° opposite Q, 70° opposite R. Sine rule: P = 20 sin 50°/sin 70° = 16.3 N and Q = 20 sin 60°/sin 70° = 18.4 N (equivalently Lami's theorem). M1 correct angles, M1 sine rule, M1 P, A1 Q, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces. A force of 20 N acts due east, a force of 15 N acts on a bearing of 300°, and a third force F acts on the particle. Find the magnitude and the bearing of the third force, correct to 1 decimal place for the magnitude and to the nearest degree for the bearing.
parts.answer: F ≈ 10.3 N on a bearing of 223°
parts.working: 15 N on bearing 300°: east = 15 sin 300° = −12.99 N; north = 15 cos 300° = 7.5 N. Sum of the two forces: east 7.01 N, north 7.5 N. Third force = −(7.01, 7.5), magnitude √(7.01² + 7.5²) = 10.3 N, bearing 180° + tan⁻¹(7.01/7.5) = 223°. M1 components, M1 sum, M1 magnitude, M1 bearing, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: A particle is in equilibrium under four forces: 8 N along the positive x-axis, 6 N along the positive y-axis, 10 N acting at an angle θ above the negative x-axis, and F N along the negative y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find θ and F.
parts.working: M1 resolve along x: 10 cos θ = 8; A1 θ = 36.9°; M1 resolve along y: 6 + 10 sin θ = F; A1 F = 12.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three forces of magnitudes 20 N, 25 N and 30 N act at a point and are in equilibrium. Find the angle between the directions of the 20 N and 25 N forces.
parts.working: M1 resultant of 20 N and 25 N has magnitude 30 N; M1 30² = 20² + 25² + 2(20)(25) cos θ; A1 cos θ = −0.125, θ = 97.2°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the other two angles between the directions of the forces.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces of magnitudes 6 N, 8 N and 10 N. Find the angle between the directions of the 6 N and 8 N forces.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle between the directions of the 10 N force and the 6 N force.
parts.working: The 6 N and 8 N forces at right angles have resultant 10 N, which makes angle tan⁻¹(8/6) = 53.1° with the 6 N force. The third force is equal and opposite to this resultant, so the angle is 180° − 53.1° = 126.9°. M1 resultant, M1 angle with 6 N, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces of magnitudes 10 N, 14 N and F N. Given that F = 10 N, find the angle between the directions of the 10 N and 14 N forces, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.working: Equilibrium: the third force is −(10 + 14 vector). Using F² = 10² + 14² + 2 × 10 × 14 cos θ with F = 10: 100 = 296 + 280 cos θ, so cos θ = −0.7 and θ = 134.4°. M1 cosine rule, M1 substitution, A1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the range of possible values of F.
parts.working: The third force must balance the resultant of the other two, which ranges from 14 − 10 = 4 N to 14 + 10 = 24 N. M1, A1.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces (2i + 5j) N, (−6i + aj) N and (bi − 3j) N. Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of each of the three forces, correct to 2 decimal places.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 6 kg rests on rough horizontal ground. The coefficient of friction is 0.35. A horizontal force of 15 N acts on the box.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine whether the box moves, and state the magnitude of the frictional force.
parts.answer: It does not move; friction is 15 N
parts.working: M1 R = 60 N; A1 maximum friction 0.35 × 60 = 21 N; A1 15 < 21, so at rest with friction 15 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A trunk of mass 7 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor in a warehouse in Karachi. The coefficient of friction is 0.25. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the greatest horizontal force that can be applied without the trunk moving.
parts.working: Limiting friction F = μR = 0.25 × 7 × 9.8 = 17.15 N. M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A horizontal force of 12 N is now applied to the trunk. Find the frictional force acting on the trunk.
parts.working: Since 12 N < 17.15 N, the trunk stays at rest and friction equals the applied force: F = 12 N. M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A crate of mass 8 kg rests on rough horizontal ground, with coefficient of friction 0.4. A rope attached to the crate has tension 50 N and makes an angle of 20° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the normal reaction between the crate and the ground.
parts.working: Vertical: R + 50 sin 20° = 8 × 9.8 → R = 78.4 − 17.10 = 61.3 N. M1 vertical equation, M1 solve, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the crate moves.
parts.answer: Horizontal component 46.98 N exceeds limiting friction 0.4 × 61.3 = 24.5 N, so the crate moves
parts.working: Horizontal component of tension = 50 cos 20° = 46.98 N. Limiting friction = 0.4 × 61.3 = 24.52 N. 46.98 > 24.52, so the crate moves. M1, M1, A1.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 10 kg on rough horizontal ground is pulled by a rope inclined at 25° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is 40 N and the crate is about to move.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: R + 40 sin 25° = 100; A1 R = 83.1 N; M1 resolve horizontally: F = 40 cos 25° = 36.25 N; M1 μ = F/R; A1 0.436.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A worker pushes a box of mass 12 kg across a rough horizontal floor with a force of magnitude P N directed at 30° below the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.25.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of P for which the box is about to move.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: R = 120 + P sin 30°; M1 resolve horizontally: P cos 30° = F; M1 F = 0.25R; A1 P(cos 30° − 0.25 sin 30°) = 30; A1 P = 40.5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box of mass 10 kg lies on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.3. A force of magnitude P N is applied at 35° above the horizontal, pulling the box. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Show that P = μmg/(cos θ + μ sin θ) when the box is about to move, and find the least value of P needed to start the box moving.
parts.working: Horizontal: P cos 35° = F; vertical: R = mg − P sin 35°. Limiting: P cos 35° = μ(mg − P sin 35°), so P = μmg/(cos 35° + μ sin 35°) = 29.4/0.9912 = 29.7 N. M1 horizontal, M1 vertical, M1 limiting, M1 rearrange, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box of mass 5 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor with coefficient of friction 0.5. Two horizontal forces act on the box: 16 N due east and 12 N due north. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Show that the box remains at rest.
parts.answer: Resultant 20 N; limiting friction 24.5 N > 20 N, so the box remains at rest
