parts.working: Resultant of 16 N east and 12 N north has magnitude √(16² + 12²) = 20 N. Limiting friction = 0.5 × 5 × 9.8 = 24.5 N. Since 20 < 24.5, the box stays at rest. M1 resultant, M1 limiting, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the magnitude and direction of the frictional force on the box.
parts.answer: 20 N, on bearing 233° (opposite to the resultant of the two forces, which is on bearing 053°)
parts.working: The friction balances the resultant, so it has magnitude 20 N and acts opposite to the resultant. Resultant bearing: tan⁻¹(16/12) = 53.1° from north, so friction bearing 233°. M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass 4 kg rests on a rough horizontal table with coefficient of friction 0.4. A light string attached to the block passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table and carries a particle of mass 1.5 kg hanging freely. The system is in equilibrium. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the frictional force on the block.
parts.working: Tension T = 1.5g = 14.7 N. Equilibrium of the block: friction F = T = 14.7 N, acting away from the pulley (opposing the tension). M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the system is in equilibrium, i.e. the limiting friction 0.4 × 4 × 9.8 = 15.7 N is greater than the friction needed.
parts.answer: 15.7 N > 14.7 N, so equilibrium is possible
parts.working: Limiting friction = μR = 0.4 × 39.2 = 15.68 N > 14.7 N. B1, B1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box of mass 10 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.3. A force of magnitude P N is applied to the box at 20° below the horizontal, pushing it. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the least value of P for which the box is about to move.
parts.working: Horizontal: P cos 20° = F; vertical: R = mg + P sin 20°. Limiting: P cos 20° = μ(mg + P sin 20°), so P = μmg/(cos 20° − μ sin 20°) = 29.4/0.8371 = 35.1 N. M1, M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass 3 kg rests on a rough horizontal table with coefficient of friction 0.6. A horizontal force of 5 N due east and a horizontal force of P N due north act on the block. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the greatest value of P for which the block remains at rest.
parts.working: Limiting friction = 0.6 × 3 × 9.8 = 17.64 N. The friction balances the resultant, so the resultant must satisfy √(5² + P²) ≤ 17.64, giving P² ≤ 286.2 and P ≤ 16.9. M1 limiting friction, M1 resultant, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass m kg rests on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.5. A horizontal force of 60 N is applied to the block, but the block remains in equilibrium. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the least possible mass of the block.
parts.working: Friction needed = 60 N ≤ μR = 0.5 × m × 9.8, so m ≥ 60/4.9 = 12.24. The least mass is 12.2 kg. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one assumption you have made in part (a).
parts.answer: The block is not acted on by any other horizontal force, and the friction is at its limiting value in the limiting case
parts.working: B1 for a valid assumption (e.g. no other horizontal forces; the floor is horizontal).

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A sack of rice of mass 20 kg lies on a rough horizontal floor in a godown. The coefficient of friction is 0.5. A force of magnitude P N is applied at an angle θ above the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the sack is about to move when P = 100/(cos θ + 0.5 sin θ).
parts.working: M1 R = 200 − P sin θ; M1 P cos θ = 0.5R; A1 rearrange to the given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of P when θ = 30°, and the corresponding normal reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compare your answer to part (b) with the force needed when the sack is pulled horizontally, and explain the difference.
parts.answer: Horizontal pull needs P = 100 N, more than 89.6 N; pulling upwards reduces the normal reaction and hence the maximum friction
parts.working: B1 θ = 0 gives P = 100 N > 89.6 N; B1 the upward component reduces R, so limiting friction 0.5R is smaller.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of weight W rests on a rough horizontal floor with coefficient of friction μ. A force of magnitude P is applied at an angle θ above the horizontal, and the block is on the point of moving. Show that P = μW/(cos θ + μ sin θ).
parts.answer: P = μW/(cos θ + μ sin θ)
parts.working: Horizontal: P cos θ = F = μR; vertical: R = W − P sin θ. Then P cos θ = μ(W − P sin θ), so P(cos θ + μ sin θ) = μW. M1, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: For μ = 0.3 and W = 98 N, find the angle θ for which P is least, and the least value of P.
parts.working: P is least when cos θ + μ sin θ is greatest, which is when tan θ = μ, so θ = arctan 0.3 = 16.7°. Then cos θ + 0.3 sin θ = √1.09 = 1.044 and P = 29.4/1.044 = 28.2 N. M1 maximise denominator, M1 θ, M1 √(1 + μ²), A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box of mass 12 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor. A force of 40 N is applied at 25° above the horizontal, and the box is in equilibrium. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the least possible coefficient of friction between the box and the floor.
parts.working: Horizontal: F = 40 cos 25° = 36.25 N. Vertical: R = 117.6 − 40 sin 25° = 100.7 N. Equilibrium requires F ≤ μR, so μ ≥ 36.25/100.7 = 0.360. M1 horizontal, M1 vertical, M1 inequality, A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two boxes A (mass 4 kg) and B (mass 6 kg) are in contact on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.2 for each box. A horizontal force P N is applied to A, pushing A towards B, which pushes B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find the greatest value of P for which both boxes remain at rest.
parts.working: Total limiting friction = 0.2 × (4 + 6) × 9.8 = 19.6 N. For the boxes to stay at rest, P ≤ 19.6 N. M1 total friction, M1, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When P = 15 N, find the range of values of the contact force between A and B.
parts.working: Let X be the contact force. For B: friction on B = X ≤ 0.2 × 6 × 9.8 = 11.76 N. For A: friction on A = 15 − X ≤ 0.2 × 4 × 9.8 = 7.84 N, so X ≥ 7.16 N. So 7.16 ≤ X ≤ 11.76. M1 B equation, M1 A equation, M1, A1 each bound.

practice.stem:
The times, in minutes, taken by 15 students in Karachi to travel to college one morning are shown in the stem-and-leaf diagram.
1 | 2 5 8
2 | 1 2 4 5 7 8
3 | 1 3 6 8
4 | 2
5 | 5
Key: 2 | 4 means 24 minutes

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the interquartile range of the times.
parts.answer: Median 27 minutes; LQ 21, UQ 36, IQR 15 minutes
parts.working:
B1 median 27
B1 quartiles 21 and 36
B1 IQR 15

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the mean time, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give a reason why the median may be a better average than the mean for these data.
parts.answer: The value 55 is much larger than the rest (data positively skewed), so it pulls the mean up; the median is not affected by extreme values

practice.stem:
The marks out of 50 scored in a quiz by 11 students in class P and 11 students in class Q are shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram. Leaves for class P are on the left.
8 | 1 |
9 5 2 | 2 | 1 6
7 4 3 1 | 3 | 0 2 5 8 8
7 4 0 | 4 | 1 3 5 9
Key: 5 | 2 | 6 means 25 marks for a student in class P and 26 marks for a student in class Q

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the interquartile range for each class.
parts.answer: Class P: median 33, IQR 40 − 25 = 15. Class Q: median 38, IQR 43 − 30 = 13
parts.working:
B1 medians 33 and 38
B1 quartiles for P: 25, 40
B1 quartiles for Q: 30, 43
B1 IQRs 15 and 13

parts.label: b
parts.text: Make two comparisons between the marks of the two classes.
parts.answer: Class Q scored higher on average (median 38 > 33); Class Q's marks were slightly less spread (IQR 13 < 15)

B1 average comparison in context
B1 spread comparison in context

A driving school in Lahore measured the reaction times, in seconds, of 15 learner drivers using a computer test.

0.3 | 0 1 3 5 6 8 9
0.4 | 2 4 7

M1 Q1 = 4th value 0.30, Q3 = 12th value 0.44
A1 IQR 0.14 s

practice.stem:
A botanist in Murree measured the heights, in cm, of 19 young pine seedlings after one year. The results are shown below.
3 | 4
4 | 1 5 7 8
5 | 2 3 5 6 8 9
6 | 1 2 4 6 7
7 | 1 4
8 | 
9 | 6
Key: 5 | 3 means 53 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the quartiles of the heights.
parts.answer: Median 58 cm, LQ 48 cm, UQ 66 cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: An outlier is defined as any value more than 1.5 × IQR above the upper quartile or below the lower quartile. Determine whether there are any outliers, showing your working.
parts.answer: IQR = 18; 1.5 × 18 = 27; limits 21 and 93; 96 > 93 so 96 cm is an outlier; no low outliers
parts.working:
M1 1.5 × 18 = 27
A1 limits 21 and 93
A1 96 is the only outlier

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest one reason why the researcher might keep the value 96 in the data.
parts.answer: It may be a genuine measurement of an unusually tall plant, not a mistake

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The stem-and-leaf diagram shows the masses, in grams, of 15 guavas from a market stall, where x is an unknown digit.
3 | 2 5 8
4 | 0 1 3 x 6 7 9
5 | 0 2 4 7 8
Key: 4 | 1 means 41 g
Given that the mean mass is 45.8 g, find the value of x.
parts.working:
M1 sum of the other 14 values = 642

parts.answer: Mean 54.6 thousand rupees (491/9); median 40 thousand rupees

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain which average better represents a typical worker at factory P.
parts.answer: The median: the mean is pulled up by the single very high income of 180

parts.label: c
parts.text: At factory Q, the monthly incomes of 9 workers have median 42 thousand rupees and mean 43 thousand rupees. A worker claims that the workers at factory P earn more because 54.6 > 43. Comment on this claim.
parts.answer: Not justified: the high mean at P is due to one outlier (180); the median at Q (42) is higher than at P (40), so a typical worker at Q earns slightly more
parts.working:
M1 compare medians
A1 conclusion with reason

practice.stem:
Two machines fill packets of lentils with a target mass of 600 g.
Machine A (20 packets): mean 600 g, standard deviation 6.5 g
Machine B (25 packets): Σ(x − 600) = 50, Σ(x − 600)² = 590, where x g is the mass of a packet.

parts.label: a
parts.text: For machine B, find the mean and the standard deviation of the masses.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the mean and the standard deviation of all 45 packets from both machines together.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State which machine is better at filling packets with close to 600 g, giving two reasons.
parts.answer: Either machine can be defended if both comparisons are made: machine A is accurate on average (mean 600 g, while B averages 602 g), but machine B is more consistent (sd 4.43 g against 6.5 g).
parts.working:
B1 mean comparison
B1 sd comparison and reasoned choice

practice.stem: Two classes sat the same test. Class A has 20 students with mean mark 62 and standard deviation 8 marks. Class B has 30 students with mean mark 58 and standard deviation 10 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the mean and the standard deviation of the marks of all 50 students together.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the combined standard deviation is greater than the weighted average of the two standard deviations (8 and 10).
parts.answer: The weighted average of the standard deviations is 9.2, but the combined value is 9.46 because the two group means (62 and 58) differ, adding between-group variation to the spread.
parts.working:
B1 weighted average of 8 and 10 with weights 20 and 30 is 9.2, which is less than 9.46
B1 explanation: the difference between the group means adds to the spread (between-group variation)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The point P(5, 3) lies on the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25. Find the gradient of the radius through P.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P, giving your answer in the form ax + by = c.
parts.working: M1 tangent gradient = −3/4 (negative reciprocal). M1 y − 3 = −¾(x − 5). A1 3x + 4y = 27.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circle C has equation x² + y² − 6x − 4y − 12 = 0. Find the centre and radius of C, and show that the point A(7, 5) lies on C.
parts.working: M1 (x − 3)² + (y − 2)² = 25. A1 centre (3, 2), r = 5. B1 substitution of (7, 5) gives 25.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to C at A.
parts.working: M1 the normal passes through the centre: gradient (5 − 2)/(7 − 3) = 3/4. A1 3x − 4y = 1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to C at A.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The normals to a circle at the points A(1, 4) and B(3, −2) have equations y = 2x + 2 and x + 2y = −1 respectively. Find the coordinates of the centre of the circle.
parts.working: M1 solve simultaneously: x + 2(2x + 2) = −1. A1 x = −1, y = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at B.
parts.working: M1 tangent ⟂ normal (gradient −½), so tangent gradient 2. A1 y + 2 = 2(x − 3), y = 2x − 8.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0. The point P(5, 1) lies on C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the centre of C and its radius.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to C at P, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: Gradient of radius from (2, −3) to (5, 1) is 4/3, so the tangent has gradient −3/4. y − 1 = −3/4(x − 5), giving 3x + 4y − 19 = 0.

practice.stem: A circle C has centre (−1, 3) and radius √13. The point Q(1, 0) lies on C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that Q lies on C.
parts.working: Distance² from (−1, 3) to (1, 0) is (1 + 1)² + (0 − 3)² = 4 + 9 = 13 = r², so Q lies on C.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to C at Q, in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: The normal passes through the centre (−1, 3) and Q(1, 0). Its gradient is (0 − 3)/(1 + 1) = −3/2, so y = −3/2(x − 1), i.e. 3x + 2y − 3 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where the normal meets the y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points A(5, 5) and B(7, −1) lie on the circle x² + y² = 50. Find the equations of the tangents to the circle at A and at B.
parts.answer: At A: x + y = 10; at B: 7x − y = 50
parts.working: M1 gradient OA = 1 so tangent gradient −1. A1 x + y = 10. M1 gradient OB = −1/7 so tangent gradient 7. A1 7x − y = 50.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tangents meet at T. Find the coordinates of T and show that TA = TB.
parts.working: M1 solve simultaneously. A1 T(7.5, 2.5). A1 TA² = 2.5² + 2.5² = 12.5 and TB² = 0.5² + 3.5² = 12.5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The point P(6, 7) lies on the circle (x − 4)² + (y − 3)² = 20. Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P.
parts.working: M1 radius gradient (7 − 3)/(6 − 4) = 2. M1 tangent gradient −½. A1 y − 7 = −½(x − 6), x + 2y = 20.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tangent meets the x-axis at Q and the y-axis at R. Find the area of triangle OQR, where O is the origin.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact length PQ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle has equation (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 10. Show that the point T(5, 4) lies outside the circle.
parts.answer: Distance from centre (−1, 2) to T is √40 > √10

parts.label: b
parts.text: A tangent is drawn from T to touch the circle at S. Find the exact length TS.
parts.working: M1 angle CST = 90°, so TS² = CT² − r² = 40 − 10. A1 TS = √30.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the kite formed by T, the centre C and the two points of contact of the tangents from T.
parts.working: M1 two right-angled triangles each of area ½ × √10 × √30. A1 √300 = 10√3.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25. The point A(15, −1) lies outside C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the length of the tangent from A to C, giving an exact answer.
parts.working: AC² = (15 − 2)² + (−1 + 1)² = 169. Tangent length² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the length is 12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equations of the two tangents from A to C.
parts.working: A line through A is y + 1 = m(x − 15), i.e. mx − y − 15m − 1 = 0. Distance from (2, −1) equals 5: |2m + 1 − 15m − 1|/√(m² + 1) = 5, so 169m² = 25(m² + 1), 144m² = 25, m = ±5/12. Tangents: y + 1 = ±5/12(x − 15), giving 5x − 12y − 87 = 0 and 5x + 12y − 63 = 0.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation x² + y² − 6x + 2y = 0. The point P(6, −2) lies on C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that P lies on C, and find the equation of the tangent to C at P, in the form y = mx + c.
parts.working: P: 36 + 4 − 36 − 4 = 0, so P lies on C. Centre (3, −1). Gradient of radius = (−2 + 1)/(6 − 3) = −1/3, so the tangent has gradient 3. y + 2 = 3(x − 6), so y = 3x − 20.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinate of the point where the tangent meets the x-axis.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation x² + y² = 25.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equations of the two tangents to C that have gradient 3/4.
parts.working: A tangent with gradient 3/4 is y = 3x/4 + c, i.e. 3x − 4y + 4c = 0. Distance from the origin is |4c|/5 = 5, so 4c = ±25.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points where these tangents touch C.
parts.working: The point of contact is the foot of the perpendicular from O. For 3x − 4y + 25 = 0 it is (−3, 4); for 3x − 4y − 25 = 0 it is (3, −4). Both lie on C since 9 + 16 = 25.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Lines of gradient 2 are tangents to the circle x² + y² = 20. By considering the equation y = 2x + c, find the two possible values of c.
parts.working: M1 substitute: x² + (2x + c)² = 20 → 5x² + 4cx + c² − 20 = 0. M1 discriminant = 0: 16c² − 20(c² − 20) = 0. A1 c² = 100. A1 c = ±10.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points of contact.
parts.working: M1 x = −4c/10 (repeated root). A1 (−4, 2) for c = 10 and (4, −2) for c = −10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = mx passes through the origin and is a tangent to the circle (x − 6)² + (y − 2)² = 4. Show that 32m² − 24m = 0.
parts.answer: Substituting gives (1 + m²)x² − (12 + 4m)x + 36 = 0; discriminant (12 + 4m)² − 144(1 + m²) = 0 simplifies to 32m² − 24m = 0 (after dividing by −4)
parts.working: M1 substitute y = mx and expand: (1 + m²)x² − (12 + 4m)x + 36 = 0. M1 use b² − 4ac = 0. A1 (12 + 4m)² = 144(1 + m²). A1 −128m² + 96m = 0, i.e. 32m² − 24m = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the equations of the two tangents from the origin to the circle and the coordinates of the point of contact on the tangent that is not an axis.
parts.answer: y = 0 and y = ¾x; point of contact (4.8, 3.6)

practice.stem: A circle C has its centre on the line y = 2x. C touches the x-axis at (3, 0).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of C.
parts.working: The circle touches the x-axis at (3, 0), so its centre is directly above, at (3, r) for radius r. The centre lies on y = 2x, so r = 6 and the centre is (3, 6). Equation (x − 3)² + (y − 6)² = 36.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points on C where the tangent is parallel to the y-axis.
parts.working: The tangent is vertical where the radius is horizontal, so y = 6 and x = 3 ± 6, giving (−3, 6) and (9, 6).

practice.stem: The circle C has equation x² + y² = 10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the two points on C where the tangent has gradient −3.
parts.working: The radius to the point has gradient 1/3, so y = x/3. Substituting: x² + x²/9 = 10, so x² = 9, x = ±3 and y = ±1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact distance between the two tangents with gradient −3.
parts.working: The tangents are 3x + y − 10 = 0 at (3, 1) and 3x + y + 10 = 0 at (−3, −1). Distance between parallel lines = |−10 − 10|/√(3² + 1²) = 20/√10 = 2√10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = x + 1 meets the circle x² + y² = 25.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact length of the chord joining these points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the line 3x + 4y = 25 is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 25, and find the point of contact.
parts.answer: Substitution gives x² − 6x + 9 = 0, a repeated root; point of contact (3, 4)
parts.working: M1 substitute y = (25 − 3x)/4. A1 25x² − 150x + 225 = 0 → (x − 3)² = 0. A1 repeated root so tangent. A1 (3, 4).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write down the equation of the tangent to the same circle at the point (−3, −4).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circle (x − 2)² + (y − 3)² = 25 meets the x-axis at A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact coordinates of the points where the circle meets the y-axis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the triangle formed by A, B and the centre of the circle.

practice.stem: The line y = 2x − 1 meets the circle x² + y² = 13 at the points A and B.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of A and B, the points where the line meets the circle.
parts.working: Substitute y = 2x − 1: x² + (2x − 1)² = 13, so 5x² − 4x − 12 = 0 and (x − 2)(5x + 6) = 0. x = 2 gives y = 3; x = −6/5 gives y = −17/5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact length of the chord AB.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation (x − 1)² + (y + 2)² = 25.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the line 3x + 4y = 20 is a tangent to C.
parts.working: Centre (1, −2), radius 5. Distance = |3(1) + 4(−2) − 20|/√(3² + 4²) = |−25|/5 = 5, which equals the radius, so the line is a tangent.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point of contact.
parts.working: The point (1 + 3t, −2 + 4t) lies on the line when 3(1 + 3t) + 4(−2 + 4t) = 20, so 25t = 25 and t = 1. The point is (4, 2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of k for which the line y = kx is a tangent to the circle (x − 4)² + y² = 8.
parts.working: M1 substitute: (1 + k²)x² − 8x + 8 = 0. M1 discriminant: 64 − 32(1 + k²) = 0. A1 k² = 1. A1 k = ±1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the set of values of k for which the line meets the circle at two distinct points.

parts.label: c
parts.text: For k = 1, find the point of contact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line x + y = k meets the circle x² + y² − 4x − 2y − 20 = 0. Show that the x-coordinates of the points of intersection satisfy 2x² − (2k + 2)x + k² − 2k − 20 = 0.
parts.answer: Substituting y = k − x and simplifying gives 2x² − (2k + 2)x + (k² − 2k − 20) = 0
parts.working: M1 substitute y = k − x and expand. A1 correct simplification to the given equation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact values of k for which the line is a tangent to the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = x − 1 meets the circle (x − 1)² + (y − 2)² = 10 at the points A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the midpoint M of AB and show that CM is perpendicular to AB, where C is the centre of the circle.
parts.answer: M(2, 1); gradient CM = −1, gradient AB = 1, product −1
parts.working: B1 M(2, 1). B1 gradients −1 and 1 so perpendicular.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact perpendicular distance from C to the line AB.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation (x − 3)² + y² = 9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k for which the line y = kx + 1 is a tangent to C.
parts.working: The line is kx − y + 1 = 0. Distance from (3, 0) = |3k + 1|/√(k² + 1) = 3, so (3k + 1)² = 9(k² + 1). This gives 6k + 1 = 9 and k = 4/3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the set of values of k for which the line meets C at two distinct points.
parts.working: Two distinct points need distance < 3: (3k + 1)² < 9(k² + 1), so 6k < 8 and k < 4/3.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation x² + y² − 2x − 4y − 20 = 0. The line x − 2y + 5 = 0 meets C at A and B.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of A and B, the points where the line meets the circle.
parts.working: Substitute x = 2y − 5: 5y² − 28y + 15 = 0, so (y − 5)(5y − 3) = 0. y = 5 gives x = 5; y = 3/5 gives x = −19/5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact length of AB.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation x² + y² = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of c for which the line y = 2x + c is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 5.
parts.working: The line is 2x − y + c = 0. Distance from the origin is |c|/√5 = √5, so |c| = 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: For c = 5, find the coordinates of the point of contact.
parts.working: The foot of the perpendicular from O to 2x − y + 5 = 0 is −5/5 × (2, −1) = (−2, 1). Check: (−2)² + 1² = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = x + c and the circle (x − 5)² + (y + 2)² = 18 are given. Show that the x-coordinates of any points of intersection satisfy 2x² + (2c − 6)x + c² + 4c + 11 = 0.
parts.working: M1 substitute and expand (x − 5)² + (x + c + 2)² = 18. A1 given equation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the set of values of c for which the line does not meet the circle.
parts.working: M1 discriminant < 0: (2c − 6)² − 8(c² + 4c + 11) < 0. A1 −4c² − 56c − 52 < 0, i.e. c² + 14c + 13 > 0. M1 critical values −13, −1. A1 c < −13 or c > −1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = 2x + 5 meets the circle x² + y² − 2x − 4y − 20 = 0 at A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle which has AB as a diameter.
parts.working: B1 centre (−1, 3). M1 r² = 2² + 4² = 20. A1 equation.

parts.label: c
parts.text: C is the centre of the original circle. Find the area of triangle ABC.
parts.working: M1 C(1, 2); e.g. ½|0 × (−3) − 5 × (−4)|, or base CA = 5 vertical with horizontal distance 4 to B. A1 10.

practice.stem: The circle C has equation (x − 2)² + y² = 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of m for which the line y = mx + 1 is a tangent to C, and the coordinates of the point of contact.
parts.working: Line mx − y + 1 = 0. Distance from (2, 0) is |2m + 1|/√(m² + 1) = 2, so (2m + 1)² = 4(m² + 1) and m = 3/4. The line is 3x − 4y + 4 = 0. The foot of the perpendicular from (2, 0) is (2, 0) − 10/25 × (3, −4) = (4/5, 8/5).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the set of values of m for which the line meets C at two distinct points.
parts.working: Two distinct points need |2m + 1|/√(m² + 1) < 2, so (2m + 1)² < 4(m² + 1), giving 4m < 3, so m < 3/4.

practice.stem: A circle C has centre (2, 1) and touches the line 3x − 4y + 1 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the radius of C.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where C touches the line.
parts.working: The point is the foot of the perpendicular from (2, 1). Value f = 3(2) − 4(1) + 1 = 3, so the point is (2, 1) − 3/25 × (3, −4) = (41/25, 37/25).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle has centre (3, −2) and radius 5. Write down the equation of the circle.
parts.working: B1 for (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25 or the expanded form x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine whether the point (6, 2) lies on, inside or outside the circle.
parts.working: M1 substitute (6, 2) into the equation or find its distance from the centre. A1 25 = 25 (distance 5), so the point lies on the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the centre and the radius of the circle with equation x² + y² − 8x + 6y − 11 = 0.
parts.working: M1 complete the square: (x − 4)² + (y + 3)² = 11 + 16 + 9. A1 centre (4, −3). A1 radius √36 = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact distance from the origin to the centre, and hence state whether the origin lies inside or outside the circle.
parts.answer: Distance 5; 5 < 6 so the origin is inside the circle

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points A(−1, 4) and B(7, −2) are the ends of a diameter of a circle. Find the coordinates of the centre and the radius of the circle.
parts.working: B1 midpoint (3, 1). M1 AB = √(8² + 6²) = 10 or distance from centre to A. A1 radius 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle, giving your answer in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.

practice.stem: A circle C has centre (−2, 5) and radius 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the equation of C in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine whether the point (1, 6) lies inside, on or outside C.
parts.working: Distance² from the centre = (1 + 2)² + (6 − 5)² = 10, which is greater than r² = 9, so the point is outside C.

practice.stem: A circle passes through the points O(0, 0), A(4, 0) and B(0, 6).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle through O, A and B, in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: O on the circle gives c = 0. A: 16 + 4a = 0, so a = −4. B: 36 + 6b = 0, so b = −6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the centre and radius of the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points P(1, 1), Q(7, 1) and R(1, 9) lie on a circle. Show that angle QPR = 90° and explain why QR is a diameter of the circle.
parts.answer: PQ is horizontal and PR is vertical, so angle QPR = 90°; the angle in a semicircle is 90°, so QR is a diameter
parts.working: B1 PQ along y = 1 and PR along x = 1 (or gradients 0 and undefined), so perpendicular. B1 angle in a semicircle / converse, so QR is a diameter.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle.
parts.working: B1 centre = midpoint of QR = (4, 5). M1 radius = ½√(6² + 8²) = 5. A1 (x − 4)² + (y − 5)² = 25.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at R, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: M1 gradient of radius from (4, 5) to R(1, 9) = −4/3. M1 tangent gradient 3/4 through R. A1 3x − 4y + 33 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle passes through the points A(2, 0) and B(6, 4). Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB.
parts.working: B1 midpoint (4, 2). B1 gradient AB = 1 so perpendicular gradient −1. A1 y − 2 = −(x − 4), i.e. y = 6 − x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The centre of the circle lies on the line y = 2x − 3. Find the equation of the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circle C has equation x² + y² + 2x − 10y + k = 0, where k is a constant. The radius of C is 4. Find the value of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact y-coordinates of the points where C meets the y-axis.
parts.working: M1 x = 0: y² − 10y + 10 = 0. M1 formula or completing square: (y − 5)² = 15. A1 y = 5 ± √15.

practice.stem: A(−2, 3) and B(4, −1) are the ends of a diameter of a circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle with AB as a diameter, in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: Centre = midpoint (1, 1). Radius² = (AB/2)² = (6² + 4²)/4 = 13. Then (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 13, giving x² + y² − 2x − 2y − 11 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine whether the origin lies inside, on or outside the circle.
parts.working: Distance² from (1, 1) to (0, 0) is 2, which is less than 13, so the origin is inside.

practice.stem: A circle C touches the x-axis and passes through the points (1, 2) and (5, 2). The centre of C is above the x-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of C, in the form (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r².
parts.working: Centre (a, r) since C touches the x-axis from above. Equal distances to (1, 2) and (5, 2) give a = 3. Then (3 − 1)² + (r − 2)² = r², so 4 + r² − 4r + 4 = r² and r = 2. Centre (3, 2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to C at the point (5, 2).
parts.working: The radius from (3, 2) to (5, 2) is horizontal, so the tangent is vertical: x = 5.

practice.stem: A circle C has equation x² + y² + ax − 6y + c = 0. Its centre is (3, b) and its radius is 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of a, b and c.
parts.working: Centre (−a/2, 3) = (3, b), so a = −6 and b = 3. Radius² = (a/2)² + 3² − c = 9 + 9 − c = 25, so c = −7.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle lies in the first quadrant and touches both the x-axis and the y-axis. Explain why its equation can be written as (x − r)² + (y − r)² = r², where r is the radius.
parts.answer: Touching both axes means the centre is a distance r from each axis, so the centre is (r, r)
parts.working: B1 centre at distance r from both axes, so (r, r).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The circle passes through the point (2, 1). Find the two possible equations of the circle.
parts.working: M1 (2 − r)² + (1 − r)² = r². A1 r² − 6r + 5 = 0. M1 r = 1 or r = 5. A1 both equations.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance between the centres of the two circles, giving your answer in exact form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Circle C₁ has centre (1, 2) and radius 3. Circle C₂ has centre (7, 10) and radius 7. Show that the two circles touch externally.
parts.answer: Distance between centres = √(6² + 8²) = 10 = 3 + 7, so they touch externally
parts.working: M1 distance between centres √(36 + 64). A1 10. A1 equals sum of radii 3 + 7, so they touch (externally).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where the circles touch.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the common tangent to the two circles at this point.
parts.working: M1 gradient of line of centres 4/3, so tangent gradient −3/4. A1 3x + 4y = 26.

practice.stem: A circle passes through the three points (1, 2), (3, −2) and (5, 2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle through (1, 2), (3, −2) and (5, 2), in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the centre and radius of the circle.

practice.stem: A circle C passes through O(0, 0) and (6, 0). The centre of C lies on the line y = x + 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of C in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: The centre has x = 3, since it is equidistant from O and (6, 0). On y = x + 1 this gives y = 4. Radius² = 9 + 16 = 25 and C is (x − 3)² + (y − 4)² = 25, i.e. x² + y² − 6x − 8y = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that (6, 8) lies on C.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to C at O, in the form ax + by = 0.
parts.working: The radius from (3, 4) to O has gradient 4/3, so the tangent has gradient −3/4. Its equation is y = −3x/4, i.e. 3x + 4y = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points A(−2, 5) and B(4, 1) are given. Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: B1 midpoint (1, 3). B1 gradient AB = −2/3. M1 perpendicular gradient 3/2 through midpoint. A1 3x − 2y + 3 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the line through (3, −1) that is parallel to the line 2x + 5y = 7.
parts.working: M1 gradient −2/5 (or same left-hand side). A1 2x + 5y = 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: This line meets the x-axis at P and the y-axis at Q. Find the exact length PQ.

practice.stem: The points A(−3, 2) and B(5, 6) are given.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB, in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: Midpoint (1, 4). Gradient of AB = 4/8 = 1/2, so the perpendicular bisector has gradient −2. y − 4 = −2(x − 1), giving 2x + y − 6 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where the perpendicular bisector meets the x-axis.

practice.stem: The point (−2, 4) is given.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the line through (−2, 4) perpendicular to y = 3x − 1, in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: The given line has gradient 3, so the perpendicular has gradient −1/3. y − 4 = −1/3(x + 2), so 3y − 12 = −x − 2, giving x + 3y − 10 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the triangle formed by this line and the coordinate axes.
parts.working: Intercepts: x = 10 when y = 0; y = 10/3 when x = 0. Area = 1/2 × 10 × 10/3 = 50/3.

practice.stem: A straight line passes through the points (1, 7) and (4, −2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the line through (1, 7) and (4, −2), in the form y = mx + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where this line meets the line y = x.
parts.working: −3x + 10 = x gives x = 5/2, so the point is (5/2, 5/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 2), B(9, 6) and C(3, 8). Find the equation of AB.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the foot F of the perpendicular from C to AB.
parts.working: M1 line through C with gradient −2: y = −2x + 14. M1 solve with AB. A1 (5, 4).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the area of triangle ABC.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A(2, 1) and B(8, 5) are two points. The point C lies on the y-axis and is equidistant from A and B. Find the coordinates of C.
parts.working: M1 perpendicular bisector: midpoint (5, 3), gradient −3/2. A1 y − 3 = −3/2(x − 5). M1 x = 0. A1 y = 10.5. (Or M1 A1 using CA² = CB² with C(0, c).)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of triangle ABC.
parts.working: M1 shoelace or ½ × base × height. A1 32.5.

practice.stem: Triangle PQR has vertices P(0, 0), Q(8, 2) and R(3, 7).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of PQ.
parts.working: Midpoint (4, 1). Gradient of PQ = 2/8 = 1/4, so the perpendicular gradient is −4. y − 1 = −4(x − 4), giving 4x + y − 17 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of PR, and hence the coordinates of the circumcentre of triangle PQR.
parts.working: Midpoint of PR is (3/2, 7/2); gradient PR = 7/3, so the perpendicular gradient is −3/7. y − 7/2 = −3/7(x − 3/2), giving 3x + 7y − 29 = 0. Solving with 4x + y − 17 = 0: x = 18/5, y = 13/5.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact radius of the circumcircle of triangle PQR.

practice.stem: The point P(1, 6) is given, together with the line x − 2y + 2 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the foot F of the perpendicular from P to the line x − 2y + 2 = 0.
parts.working: Let F = (1 + t, 6 − 2t). Substituting into the line: (1 + t) − 2(6 − 2t) + 2 = 0, so 5t − 9 = 0 and t = 9/5. F = (14/5, 12/5).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the image of P after reflection in the line.

practice.stem: Two lines are given by 4x − 3y = 11 and 3x + 4y = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point of intersection of the lines 4x − 3y = 11 and 3x + 4y = 2.
parts.working: Multiply the first by 4 and the second by 3: 16x − 12y = 44 and 9x + 12y = 6. Add: 25x = 50, so x = 2, and then y = −1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the two lines are perpendicular.
parts.working: The first line has gradient 4/3 and the second has gradient −3/4. The product is −1, so the lines are perpendicular.

practice.stem: The points A(2, 1) and B(8, −3) are given.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the locus of points equidistant from A and B, in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: Midpoint (5, −1). Gradient AB = −4/6 = −2/3, so the perpendicular bisector has gradient 3/2. y + 1 = 3/2(x − 5), giving 3x − 2y − 17 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line in part a) meets the x-axis at P. Find the coordinates of P.

parts.label: a
parts.text: ABCD is a rhombus. A is (−1, 2) and C is (7, 6). Find the equation of the diagonal BD.
parts.working: B1 midpoint of AC (3, 4). B1 gradient AC = ½, so BD gradient −2. A1 y = −2x + 10.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B lies on the x-axis. Find the coordinates of B and D.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the rhombus and show that ABCD is in fact a square.
parts.answer: Area 40; AC = BD = √80 (diagonals equal and perpendicular), so it is a square
parts.working: M1 AC = √80, BD = √80. A1 area ½ × √80 × √80 = 40. A1 equal perpendicular bisecting diagonals ⇒ square.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line l has equation y = 2x + 1. Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from P(6, 3) to l.
parts.working: M1 gradient −½ through P: y = −½x + 6. M1 solve 2x + 1 = −½x + 6. A1 (2, 5).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the reflection of P in l, and the exact perpendicular distance from P to l.

practice.stem: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, 0), B(10, 0) and C(4, 6).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of BC.
parts.working: Midpoint of BC is (7, 3). Gradient of BC = 6/(−6) = −1, so the perpendicular gradient is 1. y − 3 = x − 7, giving x − y − 4 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the circumcentre of triangle ABC.
parts.working: The perpendicular bisector of AB is x = 5. Substituting into x − y − 4 = 0 gives y = 1.

parts.label: c

practice.stem: A line passes through (2, 5) with gradient m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining (−1, 2) and (3, 4), in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: Midpoint (1, 3). Gradient of the segment = 2/4 = 1/2, so the perpendicular has gradient −2. y − 3 = −2(x − 1), i.e. 2x + y − 5 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of m for which the line through (2, 5) with gradient m meets this perpendicular bisector on the y-axis.
parts.working: The bisector meets the y-axis at (0, 5). The line y = m(x − 2) + 5 passes through (0, 5) when −2m + 5 = 5, so m = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of m for which the line through (2, 5) with gradient m is perpendicular to the bisector.
parts.working: Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1: m × (−2) = −1, so m = 1/2.

practice.stem: The time, X hours, after the start of an evening shift at which a call is received at a rescue service in Peshawar is modelled by the probability density function f(x) = k(x + 2)(6 − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 6, f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k.
parts.working:
M1 expand: 12 + 4x − x²
M1 k[12x + 2x² − ⅓x³]₀⁶ = 72k
A1 k = 1/72

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X > 4) and P(X < 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student says that f(x) = k(x − 1) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, f(x) = 0 otherwise, is a probability density function when k = ⅔. Show that the total area is 1 for this value of k, but explain why f is still not a valid probability density function.
parts.answer: ∫₀³ (x − 1) dx = 9/2 − 3 = 3/2, so k = ⅔ gives area 1; but f(x) = ⅔(x − 1) < 0 for 0 ≤ x < 1, and a pdf cannot be negative
parts.working:
M1 integrate
A1 area 1 when k = ⅔
B1 f negative for x < 1

parts.label: b
parts.text: The random variable Y has probability density function g(y) = c(y − 1) for 1 ≤ y ≤ 3, g(y) = 0 otherwise. Find c and P(Y < 2).
parts.working:
M1 c[½(y − 1)²]₁³ = 2c
A1 c = ½
B1 ½ × ½ = ¼

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = k(8 − x³) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X > 1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: State, with a reason, whether the median of X is less than or greater than 1.
parts.working: M1 P(X < 1) = 1 − 17/48 = 31/48; A1 31/48 > ½ so the median is less than 1.

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = a + bx for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2,
f(x) = 0 otherwise, where a and b are constants.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that P(X < 1) = 0.4, find the values of a and b.
parts.working: M1 ∫₀² (a + bx) dx = 2a + 2b = 1; M1 ∫₀¹ (a + bx) dx = a + b/2 = 0.4; A1 both equations; M1 solve; A1 a = 0.3, b = 0.2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why your values give a valid probability density function.
parts.answer: f(x) = 0.3 + 0.2x > 0 on [0, 2] and the total area is 1

parts.label: c

parts.label: a
