practice.stem: The random variable X has probability density function given by f(x) = kx for 0 ≤ x ≤ a, where k and a are positive constants, f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that P(X > 1) = 0.64, find the values of k and a.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X > 1 | X < 1.5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = 6x²y, and y = 2 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫(1/y) dy = ∫6x² dx. A1 ln y = 2x³ + c. M1 use x = 0, y = 2: c = ln 2. A1 y = 2e^(2x³).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.5, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = e^(2x − y) and y = 0 when x = 0, show that y = ln(½(e^(2x) + 1)).
parts.answer: eʸ = ½e^(2x) + ½, so y = ln(½(e^(2x) + 1))
parts.working: M1 write as eʸ dy/dx = e^(2x) and separate. A1 eʸ = ½e^(2x) + c. M1 use initial condition. A1 c = ½. A1 given answer correctly obtained.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y are related by 2y dy/dx = 3x² + 2, where y > 0, and y = 4 when x = 0. Find y² in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫2y dy = ∫(3x² + 2) dx. A1 y² = x³ + 2x + c. A1 c = 16.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of x for which y = 2√3, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 x³ + 2x + 16 = 12, i.e. x³ + 2x + 4 = 0, solved numerically. A1 x = −1.18.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a chemical reaction in a laboratory in Karachi, the mass x grams of product formed after t seconds satisfies dx/dt = 0.02(50 − x), and x = 0 when t = 0. Solve the differential equation to show that x = 50(1 − e^(−0.02t)).
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(50 − x) dx = ∫0.02 dt. A1 −ln(50 − x) = 0.02t + c. M1 c = −ln 50. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for 40 grams of product to form, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation (x + 1) dy/dx = 2y, for x > −1 and y > 0, given that y = 5 when x = 0. Give y in terms of x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of x for which y = 45.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After its engine is switched off, a boat on Keenjhar Lake slows so that its speed v m s⁻¹ after t seconds satisfies dv/dt = −0.02v². When t = 0, v = 10. Show that v = 50/(t + 5).
parts.working: M1 ∫v⁻² dv = −∫0.02 dt. A1 −1/v = −0.02t + c. M1 c = −0.1. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed after 15 seconds and the time taken for the speed to fall to 4 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = e^(x + y), and y = 0 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫e^(−y) dy = ∫eˣ dx. A1 −e^(−y) = eˣ + c. M1 c = −2. A1 e^(−y) = 2 − eˣ. A1 y = −ln(2 − eˣ).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y when x = 0.5, correct to 3 significant figures, and state the exact value that x approaches as y tends to infinity.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy cos² x dy/dx = √y, for 0 ≤ x < ½π, with y = 1 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y^(−½) dy = ∫sec² x dx. A1 2√y = tan x + c. M1 c = 2. A1 y = ¼(tan x + 2)².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = π/4.

practice.stem: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = x/y, for y > 0, and y = 3 when x = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y² = x² + 9.
parts.working: Separate: y dy = x dx, so y²/2 = x²/2 + C. With y = 3 at x = 0: 9/2 = C, so y² = x² + 9.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cup of chai at 90 °C is left in a room at 25 °C. Its temperature θ °C after t minutes satisfies dθ/dt = −k(θ − 25), where k is a positive constant. Solve the differential equation to find θ in terms of k and t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: After 5 minutes the temperature is 60 °C. Find the value of k correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the temperature of the chai after 12 minutes, correct to the nearest degree.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = y² sin x, and y = 0.5 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, giving y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y⁻² dy = ∫sin x dx. A1 −1/y = −cos x + c. M1 x = 0, y = 0.5: −2 = −1 + c. A1 c = −1. A1 y = 1/(1 + cos x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = π/3.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what happens to y as x approaches π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = x(1 + y²) and y = 1 when x = 0, show that y = tan(½x² + ¼π).
parts.answer: tan⁻¹ y = ½x² + π/4, so y = tan(½x² + π/4)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(1 + y²) dy = ∫x dx. A1 tan⁻¹ y. A1 ½x² + c. M1 c = tan⁻¹ 1 = π/4. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.8, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact positive value of x at which y becomes infinite for the first time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y dy/dx = x e^(2x), with y = 1 when x = 0 and y > 0. Find y² in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y dy = ∫xe^(2x) dx. M1 integration by parts. A1 ½xe^(2x) − ¼e^(2x). A1 ½y² = ½xe^(2x) − ¼e^(2x) + c, c = ¾. A1 y² = xe^(2x) − ½e^(2x) + 3/2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = y ln x, for x > 0, given that y = 1 when x = 1. Give your answer in the form y = f(x).
parts.answer: y = e^(x ln x − x + 1) = xˣe^(1 − x)
parts.working: M1 ∫(1/y) dy = ∫ln x dx. M1 by parts: ∫ln x dx = x ln x − x. A1 ln y = x ln x − x + c. A1 c = 1. A1 y = e^(x ln x − x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that y = 27e⁻² when x = 3, and evaluate this correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = (y + 2) cos 2x, and y = 1 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(y + 2) dy = ∫cos 2x dx. A1 ln(y + 2). A1 ½ sin 2x + c. M1 c = ln 3. A1 y = 3e^(½ sin 2x) − 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of y, correct to 3 significant figures, and the least positive value of x at which it occurs.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Water drains from a tank so that the depth h metres after t minutes satisfies dh/dt = −k√h, where k is a constant. Initially h = 4, and after 10 minutes h = 1. Show that 2√h = 4 − 0.2t.
parts.answer: 2√h = −kt + 4; using h = 1 at t = 10 gives k = 0.2, so 2√h = 4 − 0.2t
parts.working: M1 ∫h^(−½) dh = −∫k dt. A1 2√h = −kt + c. A1 c = 4. M1 substitute t = 10, h = 1. A1 k = 0.2 and given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the depth after 5 minutes and the time at which the tank becomes empty.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Air is pumped into a weather balloon so that its volume V cm³ at time t seconds satisfies dV/dt = 300/√V. When t = 0, V = 100. Find an expression for V^(3/2) in terms of t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the volume when t = 10, correct to 3 significant figures, and the time at which the volume reaches 400 cm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables θ and y satisfy dy/dθ = y sin² θ, and y = 2 when θ = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining y in terms of θ.
parts.working: M1 ∫(1/y) dy = ∫sin² θ dθ. M1 use sin² θ = ½(1 − cos 2θ). A1 ½θ − ¼ sin 2θ. A1 ln y = ½θ − ¼ sin 2θ + c. M1 c = ln 2. A1 answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when θ = π, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The population P of goats on a farm in Balochistan at time t years is modelled by dP/dt = 0.1P − 20, and P = 300 when t = 0. Show that P = 200 + 100e^(0.1t).
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(0.1P − 20) dP = ∫dt. A1 10 ln(0.1P − 20) = t + c. M1 use t = 0, P = 300. A1 c = 10 ln 10. A1 rearrange to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the population to double, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what would happen to the population if instead P = 200 when t = 0.

practice.stem: Given that dy/dx = 1 + y², and y = 1 when x = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = tan(x + π/4).
parts.working: Separate: dy/(1 + y²) = dx, so arctan y = x + C. With y = 1 at x = 0: arctan 1 = π/4, so C = π/4 and y = tan(x + π/4).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = π/12.

practice.stem: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = 2(x + 1)y, and y = 1 when x = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = e^(x² + 2x).
parts.working: Separate: dy/y = 2(x + 1) dx, so ln y = x² + 2x + C. With y = 1 at x = 0, C = 0, so y = e^(x² + 2x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = 1, in the form e^k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of fish, N, in a pond at time t months is modelled by dN/dt = 0.0005N(800 − N). When t = 0, N = 100. Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation to show that N = 800/(1 + 7e^(−0.4t)).
parts.working: M1 separate. M1 1/(N(800 − N)) = (1/800)(1/N + 1/(800 − N)). A1 (1/800)(ln N − ln(800 − N)) = 0.0005t + c. M1 use t = 0, N = 100. A1 ln(N/(800 − N)) = 0.4t + ln(1/7). A1 rearranged to the given form.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of fish after 5 months.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the number of fish to reach 600, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures, and state what happens to N in the long term.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy x dy/dx = y² − 1, for x > 0, y > 1, and y = 3 when x = 1. Show that y = (2 + x²)/(2 − x²).
parts.answer: ½ ln((y − 1)/(y + 1)) = ln x + ½ ln ½, so (y − 1)/(y + 1) = ½x², giving y = (2 + x²)/(2 − x²)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(y² − 1) dy = ∫1/x dx. M1 partial fractions ½(1/(y − 1) − 1/(y + 1)). A1 ½ ln(y − 1) − ½ ln(y + 1). A1 = ln x + c. M1 c = ½ ln(1/2). M1 remove logs: (y − 1)/(y + 1) = ½x². A1 rearrange to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1.2, correct to 3 significant figures, and explain why the solution is valid only for x < √2.
parts.answer: y = 6.14; at x = √2 the denominator is zero (y → ∞)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = cos² y tan x, for 0 ≤ x < ½π, and y = 0 when x = 0, show that tan y = ln(sec x).
parts.answer: ∫sec² y dy = ∫tan x dx gives tan y = ln(sec x) + c with c = 0
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫sec² y dy = ∫tan x dx. A1 tan y. A1 −ln(cos x) or ln(sec x). M1 use y = 0, x = 0 to find c = 0. A1 given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = π/3, giving your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy x(x + 1) dy/dx = 2y + 1, for x > 0, and y = 1.5 when x = 1. Show that 2y + 1 = 16x²/(x + 1)².
parts.answer: ½ ln(2y + 1) = ln x − ln(x + 1) + ln 4, so 2y + 1 = 16x²/(x + 1)²
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(2y + 1) dy = ∫1/(x(x + 1)) dx. B1 1/(x(x + 1)) = 1/x − 1/(x + 1). A1 ½ ln(2y + 1). A1 ln x − ln(x + 1). M1 use x = 1, y = 1.5: ½ ln 4 = ln ½ + c. A1 c = ln 4. A1 given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y in terms of x and state the limiting value of y as x becomes very large.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = x(y + 1)²e^(−x), and y = 0 when x = 0. Show that 1/(y + 1) = (x + 1)e^(−x).
parts.working: M1 ∫(y + 1)⁻² dy = ∫xe^(−x) dx. A1 −1/(y + 1). M1 integration by parts. A1 −xe^(−x) − e^(−x). M1 use initial condition: c = 0. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 2, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A news item spreads through a town. The number of people, x thousand, who have heard it t days after it was posted satisfies dx/dt = kx(5 − x), where k is a constant. When t = 0, x = 1 and when t = 1, x = 2. Show that ln(4x/(5 − x)) = 5kt and find the value of k correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 separate and use partial fractions 1/(x(5 − x)) = (1/5)(1/x + 1/(5 − x)). A1 (1/5)(ln x − ln(5 − x)). A1 = kt + c. M1 t = 0, x = 1: c = (1/5) ln ¼. A1 given form. M1 t = 1, x = 2: ln(8/3) = 5k. A1 k = 0.196.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of people who have heard the item after 3 days, to the nearest hundred.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (x + 1) dy/dx = y² + 4, for x > −1, and y = 2 when x = 0, show that y = 2 tan(2 ln(x + 1) + ¼π).
parts.answer: ½ tan⁻¹(y/2) = ln(x + 1) + π/8, so y = 2 tan(2 ln(x + 1) + π/4)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(y² + 4) dy = ∫1/(x + 1) dx. A1 ½ tan⁻¹(y/2). A1 ln(x + 1). M1 use y = 2, x = 0. A1 c = π/8. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.2, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = 4 − y², with |y| < 2, and y = 0 when x = 0, show that y = 2(e^(4x) − 1)/(e^(4x) + 1).
parts.answer: (1/4) ln((2 + y)/(2 − y)) = x, so (2 + y)/(2 − y) = e^(4x), giving the result
parts.working: M1 separate. M1 partial fractions 1/(4 − y²) = (1/4)(1/(2 − y) + 1/(2 + y)). A1 (1/4)(ln(2 + y) − ln(2 − y)). A1 = x + c. B1 c = 0. M1 remove logarithms. A1 rearrange to the given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.25, correct to 3 significant figures, and state the limiting value of y as x → ∞.

practice.stem: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = xy², with y = 1 when x = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to show that y = 2/(2 − x²).
parts.working: Separate: dy/y² = x dx, so −1/y = x²/2 + C. With y = 1 at x = 0: −1 = C. So 1/y = 1 − x²/2 and y = 2/(2 − x²).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the range of values of x for which this solution is valid.
parts.working: The solution needs 2 − x² > 0, so |x| < √2. As x approaches √2 from below, y becomes infinitely large.

practice.stem: The population P of a bird colony at time t years satisfies dP/dt = kP, where k is a constant. At t = 0, P = 1000, and at t = 5, P = 1500.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P when t = 10, giving your answer to the nearest whole number.

practice.stem: A sugar cube in a cup of tea loses mass at a rate proportional to its mass, so dm/dt = −0.2m, where m is the mass in grams and t is the time in minutes. Initially m = 50.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to find m in terms of t.
parts.working: dm/m = −0.2 dt, so ln m = −0.2t + C. With m = 50 at t = 0: m = 50e^(−0.2t).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the mass after 3 minutes, correct to 2 decimal places.

practice.stem: A cup of tea cools in a room at 20 °C. Its temperature T °C after t minutes satisfies dT/dt = −k(T − 20), where k is a positive constant. The tea is at 90 °C at t = 0 and at 60 °C at t = 10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the temperature after 30 minutes, correct to 1 decimal place.

practice.stem: Water drains from a cylindrical tank through a hole in its base. The depth of water, h metres, after t minutes satisfies dh/dt = −0.2√h. Initially h = 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 2√h = 4 − 0.2t.
parts.working: dh/dt = −0.2√h, so (1/√h) dh/dt = −0.2, and d(2√h)/dt = −0.2. Integrating: 2√h = −0.2t + C. At t = 0, h = 4, so 2√h = 4: C = 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time when the depth is 1 metre.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the tank to empty.
parts.working: The tank is empty when h = 0: 4 − 0.2t = 0, so t = 20 minutes.

practice.stem: The volume V of a spherical balloon increases at a rate proportional to its surface area S, so dV/dt = kS, where V = (4/3)πr³ and S = 4πr².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dr/dt is constant.
parts.working: dV/dt = kS gives 4πr² dr/dt = k × 4πr², so dr/dt = k, a constant.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that r = 2 at t = 0 and r = 5 at t = 6, find r when t = 10.
parts.working: The rate dr/dt is constant, so r = 2 + 0.5t. Check: at t = 6, r = 5. When t = 10, r = 2 + 5 = 7.

practice.stem: A cylindrical tank leaks water so that the depth h cm after t minutes satisfies dh/dt = −h/200. Initially h = 60.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to find h in terms of t.
parts.working: dh/dt = −h/200, so ln h = −t/200 + C. With h = 60 at t = 0, h = 60e^(−t/200).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the depth after 100 minutes, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the depth to halve, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A curve passes through (0, 2). At each point (x, y) on the curve, dy/dx = (x + 1)/y, for y > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y² = (x + 1)² + 3.
parts.working: y dy/dx = x + 1, so y²/2 = (x + 1)²/2 + C. At (0, 2): 2 = 1/2 + C, so C = 3/2. Multiplying by 2 gives y² = (x + 1)² + 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the y-coordinate of the point on the curve where x = 1, given that y > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of users P of a ride-hailing app in a city increases at a rate proportional to P. At a certain time, when P = 2000, P is increasing at 100 users per day. Write down a differential equation relating P and t (days) and find the constant of proportionality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Taking t = 0 when P = 2000, solve the differential equation and find P when t = 10, to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A metal casting at a foundry in Gujranwala cools so that the rate of decrease of its temperature θ °C is proportional to the difference between θ and the surrounding temperature of 30 °C. Initially θ = 200 and the temperature is falling at 8.5 °C per minute. Form a differential equation and find the constant of proportionality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the differential equation and find the temperature after 20 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the temperature to fall to 50 °C.

practice.stem: A van on a motorway in Punjab has speed v m/s after t seconds, where dv/dt = 1.5 − 0.05v. The van starts from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 30(1 − e^(−0.05t)).
parts.working: dv/dt = 1.5 − 0.05v. Separating and integrating gives v = 30 + Ce^(−0.05t). At t = 0, v = 0, so C = −30 and v = 30(1 − e^(−0.05t)). Check: dv/dt = 1.5e^(−0.05t) = 1.5 − 0.05v.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed after 20 seconds, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: v = 30(1 − e^(−1)) = 18.96..., so 19.0 m/s to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the limiting speed of the van.

practice.stem: A reservoir receives water at a constant rate of 20 million m³ per week. Water leaves at a rate of 0.1 times the current volume V million m³, so dV/dt = 20 − 0.1V. Initially the reservoir is empty.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that V = 200(1 − e^(−0.1t)).
parts.working: dV/dt = 20 − 0.1V. Solving gives V = 200 + Ce^(−0.1t). With V = 0 at t = 0, C = −200, so V = 200(1 − e^(−0.1t)).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for V to reach 150, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the limiting value of V.

practice.stem: A tank holds 200 litres of brine and initially contains 10 kg of salt. Brine containing 0.5 kg of salt per litre flows in at 3 litres per minute. The well-mixed mixture flows out at 3 litres per minute, so the volume stays at 200 litres. Let S kg be the amount of salt at time t minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dS/dt = 1.5 − 0.015S.
parts.working: Salt flows in at 3 × 0.5 = 1.5 kg per minute. Salt flows out at 3 × S/200 = 0.015S kg per minute. The net rate is the difference.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to find S in terms of t.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the amount of salt after 60 minutes, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: The concentration C mg/L of a drug in the blood satisfies dC/dt = 4 − 0.25C, where t is the time in hours. At t = 0, C = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to find C in terms of t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which C = 12, correct to 2 decimal places.

practice.stem: A savings account in Lahore has balance A rupees at time t years. The account earns interest continuously at 5% per year and Ali pays in continuously at 600 rupees per year, so dA/dt = 0.05A + 600. The opening balance is Rs 5000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to show that A = 17000e^(0.05t) − 12000.
parts.working: dA/dt = 0.05A + 600. The general solution is A = Ce^(0.05t) − 12000. With A = 5000 at t = 0, C = 17000.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of A after 10 years, to the nearest rupee.

practice.stem: The population P of a town changes at a rate given by dP/dt = 0.02P + 50, where t is in years, because people move in at a steady rate. At t = 0, P = 1000.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P when t = 10, to the nearest whole number.

practice.stem: The mass m grams of a radioactive isotope satisfies dm/dt = −km, where t is in days. The half-life of the isotope is 8 days and the initial mass is 120 g.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: The half-life is 8 days, so e^(−8k) = 1/2 and k = ln 2/8 = 0.0866.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the mass remaining after 20 days, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A curve passes through (0, 1). At each point (x, y) on the curve, dy/dx = y + 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = 3e^x − 2.
parts.working: dy/dx = y + 2 gives y + 2 = Ce^x. At (0, 1), 3 = C, so y = 3e^x − 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = ln 2.

practice.stem: A bottle of water at 5 °C is taken out of a fridge and placed in a room at 25 °C. Its temperature θ °C after t minutes satisfies dθ/dt = k(25 − θ), where k is a positive constant. The water is at 17 °C after 6 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the water to reach 20 °C, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A reactant has concentration [A] mol dm⁻³ at time t minutes, where d[A]/dt = −0.05[A]². Initially [A] = 2 mol dm⁻³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 1/[A] = 0.5 + 0.05t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find [A] when t = 20, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for [A] to fall to 0.5 mol dm⁻³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A container is filled with water. When the depth of water is h cm, the volume is V = 4h³ cm³. Water leaks out through a small hole at a rate of 2√h cm³ per second. Show that dh/dt = −1/(6h^(3/2)).
parts.working: B1 dV/dh = 12h². M1 chain rule dV/dt = (dV/dh)(dh/dt) with dV/dt = −2√h. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Initially the depth is 16 cm. Solve the differential equation and find the time taken for the container to empty, giving your answer in minutes correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Gas escapes from a spherical balloon so that the rate of decrease of its volume is proportional to its radius r cm. Show that r dr/dt = −c, where c is a positive constant. [The volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³.]
parts.working: B1 dV/dr = 4πr². M1 4πr² dr/dt = −kr. A1 r dr/dt = −c with c = k/(4π).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Initially r = 10, and after 6 seconds r = 8. Solve the differential equation to show that r² = 100 − 6t.
parts.working: M1 ∫r dr = −∫c dt. A1 ½r² = −ct + 50. A1 c = 3 and given answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time at which the balloon has completely deflated, according to this model, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A particle moves in a straight line with velocity v m/s after t seconds. Its acceleration is −0.02v², and v = 30 when t = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 1/v = 1/30 + 0.02t.
parts.working: dv/dt = −0.02v², so dv/v² = −0.02 dt. Integrating: −1/v = −0.02t + C. At t = 0, v = 30, so C = −1/30 and 1/v = 1/30 + 0.02t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the speed to fall from 30 to 10 m/s, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled in this time, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A bacterial culture grows at a rate of 0.1 times the number of bacteria N, but an antibiotic removes 30 bacteria per hour, so dN/dt = 0.1N − 30 with t in hours. Initially N = 1000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that N = 300 + 700e^(0.1t).
parts.working: dN/dt = 0.1N − 30 gives N = 300 + Ce^(0.1t). With N = 1000 at t = 0, C = 700.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find N when t = 5, to the nearest whole number.
parts.working: N = 300 + 700e^(0.5) = 1454.1, so N = 1454 to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time, in hours to 2 decimal places, when N = 3000.

practice.stem: The number x of people who know a rumour in a town of 5000 people satisfies dx/dt = kx(5000 − x), where t is in days and k is a constant. Initially 50 people know the rumour, and after 2 days 400 people know it.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find k, giving its value to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the number of days, to 3 significant figures, for 2500 people to know the rumour.

practice.stem: A fish population P in a lake satisfies dP/dt = 0.04P − 200, where t is in years. Fish are harvested at a constant rate. At t = 0, P = 4000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to show that P = 5000 − 1000e^(0.04t).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find dP/dt at t = 0 and explain what it means.
parts.working: dP/dt = 0.04 × 4000 − 200 = −40, so the population is initially falling by 40 fish per year.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time at which the population becomes zero, to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A curve passes through (1, 2) and (4, 18). At each point (x, y) on the curve, the gradient is ky/x, for a constant k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = ky/x and show that y = 2x^k.
parts.working: Separate: dy/y = k dx/x, so ln y = k ln x + C. With y = 2 at x = 1, C = ln 2, so y = 2x^k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given also that y = 18 at x = 4, find the exact value of k.
parts.working: 2 × 4^k = 18, so 4^k = 9. Then 2^(2k) = 9, so 2k = log₂9 and k = log₂3 ≈ 1.585.

practice.stem: A curve passes through (1, 3). At each point (x, y) on the curve, dy/dx = 2y/x.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = 3x².
parts.working: dy/dx = 2y/x gives dy/y = 2 dx/x, so y = Ax². At (1, 3), A = 3, so y = 3x².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the point where x = 1, in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: dy/dx = 6x, so dy/dx = 6 at (1, 3). The normal has gradient −1/6: y − 3 = −1/6(x − 1), giving x + 6y − 19 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find where this normal meets the x-axis.

practice.stem: The variables v and x satisfy v dv/dx = −0.2v², where v > 0, and v = 10 when x = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 10e^(−0.2x).
parts.working: a = v dv/dx = −0.2v², so dv/dx = −0.2v. Then ln v = −0.2x + C; at x = 0, v = 10, so v = 10e^(−0.2x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of x when v = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A tank initially holds 100 litres of water containing 5 kg of salt. Brine containing 0.2 kg of salt per litre flows in at 3 litres per minute. The well-mixed mixture flows out at 2 litres per minute, so after t minutes the volume is (100 + t) litres. Let S kg be the amount of salt at time t.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dS/dt = 0.6 − 2S/(100 + t).
parts.working: Salt in at 3 × 0.2 = 0.6 kg per minute. Salt out at 2 × S/(100 + t) kg per minute, since the volume is 100 + t litres.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that S = 0.2(100 + t) − 150000/(100 + t)² satisfies the differential equation in part (a) and that S = 5 when t = 0.
parts.answer: Verified: dS/dt = 0.2 + 300000/(100 + t)³, and 0.6 − 2S/(100 + t) = 0.2 + 300000/(100 + t)³, so the equation holds; at t = 0, S = 5.
parts.working: Differentiate: dS/dt = 0.2 + 300000/(100 + t)³ (M1, chain rule on the quotient term). Substitute: 0.6 − 2S/(100 + t) = 0.6 − 0.4 + 300000/(100 + t)³ = 0.2 + 300000/(100 + t)³, which matches (A1). At t = 0: S = 20 − 15 = 5 (B1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the amount of salt after 20 minutes, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A skydiver falls vertically. Her speed v m/s after t seconds satisfies dv/dt = 9.8 − 0.01v², and she starts from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the terminal velocity is √980 m/s, and find it correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Terminal velocity when dv/dt = 0: 9.8 = 0.01v², so v² = 980 and v = √980 = 31.3 m/s.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the speed to reach 20 m/s, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Kxⁿ, where K and n are constants. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line passing through the points (0.5, 2.1) and (2.5, 0.9). Find the values of n and K, giving K correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = A × bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line through (1, 3.2) and (4, 5.0). Find the values of A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 ln y = ln A + x ln b; M1 gradient 1.8/3 = 0.6 = ln b; M1 intercept ln A = 3.2 − 0.6 = 2.6; A1 A = 13.5, b = 1.82.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = axᵇ. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line with gradient 2.5 that crosses the vertical axis at 1.6. Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 3, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: For the relationship y = A bˣ, state which graph should be drawn to give a straight line, and what its gradient represents.
parts.answer: ln y against x; gradient ln b
parts.working: B1 ln y against x; B1 gradient = ln b (intercept ln A).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line obtained has equation ln y = 0.92 + 0.35x. Find A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Kxⁿ, where K and n are constants. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line passing through (0, 1.2) and (2, 6.2). State the value of n and the value of ln K.
parts.working: Gradient = (6.2 − 1.2)/(2 − 0) = 2.5 so n = 2.5 (M1, A1). Intercept on the vertical axis is ln K = 1.2 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of K, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of y when x = 2, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: y = Kxⁿ = e^1.2 × 2^2.5 = 3.3201 × 5.6569 = 18.78, so y = 18.8 (M1 for substituting n and K, A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: For the relationship y = p × qˣ, the graph of log₁₀ y against x is a straight line passing through (0, 1.4) and (5, 2.9). Find the gradient of the line and the value of p, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Gradient = (2.9 − 1.4)/5 = 0.3 (M1, A1). Intercept log₁₀ p = 1.4, so p = 10^1.4 = 25.1 (M1 A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find q, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The table gives values of x and y. x: 1, 2, 3, 4; y: 6, 12, 24, 48. Show that ln y is a linear function of x, and find the gradient and the intercept on the ln y axis, each correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: ln y = 1.792, 2.485, 3.178, 3.871. Equal steps of 0.693 for each unit increase in x, so linear (M1, A1). Gradient = ln 2 = 0.693 (A1). Intercept = ln 6 − ln 2 = ln 3 = 1.10 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the values of A and b in the relation y = A × bˣ.
parts.working: Gradient ln b = ln 2 gives b = 2; intercept ln A = ln 3 gives A = 3 (M1, A1).

practice.stem:
A laboratory culture of bacteria is counted every 2 hours. The number N of bacteria after t hours is modelled by N = N₀e^{kt}.
t (hours): 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
N: 250, 503, 1014, 2042, 4111

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the model N = N₀e^{kt} gives a straight line when ln N is plotted against t, and state what the gradient and intercept represent.
parts.answer: ln N = ln N₀ + kt; gradient k, intercept ln N₀
parts.working: M1 take ln of both sides; A1 gradient k, vertical intercept ln N₀.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the values of ln N for the table, correct to 2 decimal places, and use them to estimate k and N₀.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use the model to estimate the number of bacteria after 10 hours, correct to 2 significant figures, and comment on the reliability of this estimate.
parts.answer: About 8300; it is an extrapolation beyond the data, so less reliable

practice.stem: A student in Lahore times a simple pendulum. The period T seconds and the length L metres are thought to satisfy T = kLⁿ. The graph of ln T against ln L is a straight line passing through the points (−1.20, 0.096) and (0.40, 0.896).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of n and k, giving k correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your values to find the period of a pendulum of length 0.75 m, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A cup of tea cools in a room at 20 °C. Its temperature θ °C after t minutes is modelled by θ − 20 = Ae^{−kt}. Readings: t = 0, θ = 80.0; t = 5, θ = 60.2; t = 10, θ = 47.0; t = 15, θ = 38.07.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the model gives a straight line when ln(θ − 20) is plotted against t, stating the gradient and intercept in terms of A and k.
parts.answer: ln(θ − 20) = ln A − kt; gradient −k, intercept ln A

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the readings at t = 0 and t = 15 to find the values of A and k, correct to 2 significant figures where necessary.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the tea to cool to 30 °C, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: The population P million of a large city is modelled by P = a × bᵗ, where t is the number of years after the start of 2010. The graph of ln P against t is a straight line through (2, 2.65) and (10, 2.97).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of a and b, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the model to find the value of t when the population first reaches 25 million, and state the calendar year in which this happens.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Ae^{−kx²}. Explain why the graph of ln y against x² is a straight line.
parts.answer: ln y = ln A − kx², which is linear in x²

parts.label: b
parts.text: This line passes through (1.0, 2.20) and (4.0, 1.30), where the horizontal axis shows x². Find A and k.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find y when x = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variable V volts satisfies V = 40e^(−0.15t), where t is the time in seconds. The table shows values of V for t = 0, 3, 6, 9: V: 40.0, 25.5, 16.3, 10.4. Complete the table of values of ln V, correct to 3 decimal places, and show that the points lie close to a straight line when ln V is plotted against t.
parts.working: ln V = ln 40 − 0.15t, which is linear in t (M1 for taking logs). Values 3.689, 3.239, 2.791, 2.342 decrease by about 0.45 per 3 seconds (M1, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the first and last points to find the gradient of the line, correct to 2 significant figures, and state the value of V when t = 0.
parts.working: Gradient = (2.342 − 3.689)/9 = −0.1497 ≈ −0.15 (M1, A1). Intercept ln 40 gives V = 40 when t = 0 (A1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the time constant τ, where V = V₀e^(−t/τ), correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A machine part has power P watts at speed v m/s, where P = a × v^b. Two readings are (2, 4) and (4, 32). Show that the graph of ln P against ln v is a straight line, and find its gradient.
parts.working: Taking logs: ln P = ln a + b ln v, a straight line in ln v (M1, A1). Gradient = (ln 32 − ln 4)/(ln 4 − ln 2) = ln 8/ln 2 = 3 (M1, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of a and b.
parts.working: b = 3 (gradient). ln a = ln P − 3 ln v; at v = 2, P = 4: a = 4/8 = 0.5 (M1, A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The relation y = A e^(k/x) is given, where A and k are constants and x > 0. Show that ln y is a linear function of 1/x.
parts.working: ln y = ln A + ln e^(k/x) = ln A + k/x, which is linear in 1/x with gradient k and intercept ln A (M1, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line of ln y against 1/x passes through the points (1/x, ln y) = (2, 3.0) and (4, 1.0). Find k, and A correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Gradient = (1.0 − 3.0)/(4 − 2) = −1, so k = −1 (M1, A1). Intercept: 3.0 = ln A + (−1)(2), so ln A = 5 and A = e⁵ = 148 (M1, A1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find y when x = 0.5, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: 1/x = 2, so ln y = 3 and y = e³ = 20.1 (M1, A1)

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy the equation y² = A bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line passing through (2, 1.45) and (5, 0.70). Find the values of A and b correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 2 ln y = ln A + x ln b, so ln y = ½ ln A + (½ ln b)x; M1 gradient −0.75/3 = −0.25 = ½ ln b; A1 b = e^{−0.5} = 0.607; M1 intercept 1.45 + 0.5 = 1.95 = ½ ln A; A1 A = e^{3.9} = 49.4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Axⁿ. When x = 2, y = 15 and when x = 5, y = 60. By taking natural logarithms, find the values of n and A correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln 15 = ln A + n ln 2 and ln 60 = ln A + n ln 5; M1 subtract: ln 4 = n ln 2.5; A1 n = 1.51; M1 substitute back; A1 A = 15 ÷ 2^{1.513} = 5.26.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence state the gradient and the intercept on the vertical axis of the graph of ln y against ln x.
parts.working: B1 gradient n = 1.51; B1 intercept ln A = 1.66.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = 10 + 3x^1.5 for x > 0. Show that the graph of ln(y − 10) against ln x is a straight line, and state its gradient and its intercept on the ln(y − 10) axis, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: y − 10 = 3x^1.5, so ln(y − 10) = ln 3 + 1.5 ln x, a straight line in ln x (M1, A1). Gradient 1.5 (A1). Intercept ln 3 = 1.10 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence, or otherwise, find y when x = 9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = A x e^(kx), where A and k are constants and x > 0. Show that the graph of ln(y/x) against x is a straight line.
parts.working: y/x = A e^(kx), so ln(y/x) = ln A + kx, which is linear in x with gradient k and intercept ln A (M1, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The straight line of ln(y/x) against x passes through the points (x, ln(y/x)) = (1, 1.5) and (3, 0.1). Find the gradient and the intercept on the vertical axis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find A, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = A xⁿ. The graph of y against x passes through (2, 12) and (8, 36). Find n correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Dividing: 36/12 = (8/2)ⁿ, so 3 = 4ⁿ and n = ln 3/ln 4 = 0.792 (M1 for ratio, M1 for logs, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find A correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of x for which y = 100, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3^{2x} = 20, giving x correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation log₂(x + 5) − log₂(x − 1) = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation ln(3x − 2) = 2, giving x in exact form and correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 5^(x − 1) = 60, giving x correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation log₅(x + 3) + log₅(x − 1) = 1.
parts.working: log₅[(x + 3)(x − 1)] = 1 gives (x + 3)(x − 1) = 5, so x² + 2x − 8 = 0 (M1, A1). (x + 4)(x − 2) = 0 gives x = 2 or x = −4 (M1). x = −4 is rejected since x − 1 < 0 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The population of a town in Sindh is modelled by P = 50 000 × 1.035ᵗ, where t is the number of years after 2025. Find the value of t when P = 80 000, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the first calendar year in which the population is at least 80 000.
parts.working: P(13) = 50 000 × 1.035¹³ ≈ 78 200 < 80 000 and P(14) ≈ 80 900 ≥ 80 000, so the first whole number of years is 14 and the year is 2025 + 14 = 2039 (B1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 2 ln x − ln(x + 6) = ln 2. Give your answer in exact form and correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln(x²/(x + 6)) = ln 2; A1 x² − 2x − 12 = 0; M1 solve: x = 1 ± √13; A1 x = 1 + √13 (4.61) only, since ln x needs x > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation e^{2x} − 5eˣ + 6 = 0, giving your answers in exact form.
parts.working: M1 let u = eˣ: u² − 5u + 6 = 0; A1 u = 2, 3; A1 x = ln 2, ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 5^{x+1} = 3^{2x−1}. Show that x = ln 15 / ln(9/5) and give x correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 (x + 1) ln 5 = (2x − 1) ln 3; M1 collect x terms: x(2 ln 3 − ln 5) = ln 5 + ln 3; A1 x = ln 15/ln(9/5); A1 4.61.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that log₉ x = ½ log₃ x.
parts.working: M1 change of base log₉ x = log₃ x / log₃ 9; A1 log₃ 9 = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve log₃ x + log₉ x = 6.
parts.working: M1 (3/2) log₃ x = 6; A1 log₃ x = 4, x = 81.

practice.stem: A sample of a radioactive substance used in a hospital has mass m grams after t years, where m = 40e^{−0.025t}.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the initial mass.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the mass to fall to 15 g, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the half-life of the substance, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation ln x + ln(x − 3) = ln 10 can be written as x² − 3x − 10 = 0 for x > 3.
parts.working: ln[x(x − 3)] = ln 10 gives x(x − 3) = 10, so x² − 3x − 10 = 0 (M1, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve the equation ln x + ln(x − 3) = ln 10, giving the exact value of x.
parts.working: (x − 5)(x + 2) = 0 gives x = 5 or x = −2 (M1, A1). x = −2 is rejected because ln(x − 3) and ln x need x > 3 (M1, A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 6^(2x) − 35 × 6ˣ + 216 = 0, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation log₄(2x + 1) = 1 + log₄(x − 1), where x > 1.
parts.working: Write 1 = log₄ 4: log₄(2x + 1) = log₄[4(x − 1)], so 2x + 1 = 4x − 4 (M1, M1). 5 = 2x, x = 2.5 (A1). Check: x − 1 > 0 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 2^{2x+1} − 7(2ˣ) + 3 = 0, giving any non-integer answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 2^{2x+1} = 2(2ˣ)²; M1 2u² − 7u + 3 = 0; A1 u = 3 or ½; M1 2ˣ = 3 gives x = ln 3/ln 2; A1 x = 1.58 and x = −1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the simultaneous equations log₂ x + log₂ y = 5 and x + y = 12.
parts.working: M1 log₂(xy) = 5 so xy = 32; M1 substitute y = 12 − x: x² − 12x + 32 = 0; A1 x = 4 or 8; A1 y = 8 or 4; B1 both pairs give positive x, y so both valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3eˣ + 4e^{−x} = 8, giving your answers in exact form.
parts.working: M1 multiply by eˣ: 3u² − 8u + 4 = 0 where u = eˣ; A1 (3u − 2)(u − 2) = 0; A1 u = 2 or 2/3; A1 x = ln 2, ln(2/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3ˣ × 4^(x + 1) = 2^(x + 4), giving x correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation eˣ + e⁻ˣ = 2.5, giving your answers in exact form.
parts.working: Multiply by eˣ: e²ˣ − 2.5eˣ + 1 = 0 (M1). Let y = eˣ: 2y² − 5y + 2 = 0 (M1), so (2y − 1)(y − 2) = 0 (M1). y = 2 gives x = ln 2 and y = ½ gives x = −ln 2 (A1, A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation log₂(x + 1) + log₄ x = 3 can be written as x(x + 1)² = 64, where x > 0.
parts.working: Write log₄ x = ½ log₂ x. Multiply by 2: 2 log₂(x + 1) + log₂ x = 6 (M1, M1). So log₂[x(x + 1)²] = 6 and x(x + 1)² = 64 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of x, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the smallest integer n such that 1.08ⁿ > 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 0.6ˣ < 0.05, giving the boundary value correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 x ln 0.6 < ln 0.05; M1 divide by ln 0.6 (negative) and reverse the inequality; A1 x > 5.86.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of log₂ 40, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least integer n for which 2ⁿ > 40.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the least integer n for which 0.97ⁿ < 0.5.
parts.working: n > ln 0.5/ln 0.97 = 22.76, so the least integer is 23 (M1 for logs, M1 for the division, A1). Check: 0.97²² = 0.5117 and 0.97²³ = 0.4963.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 2 ln x < ln(4x + 5), giving your answer as an interval.
parts.working: 2 ln x = ln x², so x > 0 and x² < 4x + 5 (M1, M1). x² − 4x − 5 < 0 gives (x − 5)(x + 1) < 0 (M1). With x > 0 this gives 0 < x < 5 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality log₂ x + log₂(x − 2) ≤ 3, giving your answer as an interval.
parts.working: log₂[x(x − 2)] ≤ 3 needs x > 2 and x(x − 2) ≤ 8 (M1, M1). x² − 2x − 8 ≤ 0 gives (x − 4)(x + 2) ≤ 0 (M1). With x > 2 this gives 2 < x ≤ 4 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 4ˣ < 3^{x+2}, giving the boundary value correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 x ln 4 < (x + 2) ln 3; M1 x(ln 4 − ln 3) < 2 ln 3; A1 ln 4 − ln 3 > 0 so inequality unchanged; A1 x < 7.64.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |2ˣ − 6| = 3, giving your answers correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: Ayesha invests Rs 200000 in a savings account in Karachi that pays 9% compound interest per year.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the value after n years is 200000 × 1.09ⁿ rupees.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least number of complete years after which the value of the account is more than Rs 500000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality log₁₀ x + log₁₀(x − 3) < 1, giving your answer as an interval.
parts.working: log₁₀[x(x − 3)] < 1 needs x > 3 and x(x − 3) < 10 (M1, M1). x² − 3x − 10 < 0 gives (x − 5)(x + 2) < 0 (M1). With x > 3: 3 < x < 5 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality e²ˣ − 4eˣ < 5, giving the boundary value in exact form.
parts.working: Let y = eˣ (y > 0): y² − 4y − 5 < 0, so (y − 5)(y + 1) < 0 (M1, M1). Since y + 1 > 0, y < 5 (M1). So eˣ < 5 and x < ln 5 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 2 × 7ˣ > 5ˣ⁺¹, giving the boundary value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car bought for Rs 3 200 000 loses 15% of its value each year, so its value after n years is 3 200 000 × 0.85ⁿ rupees. Find the least whole number of years after which the value is less than Rs 1 000 000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |3ˣ − 10| < 5, giving the boundary values correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality ln(2x + 1) > 1 + ln(x − 1), giving the boundary value in exact form and correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 domain x > 1; M1 ln((2x + 1)/(x − 1)) > 1, so 2x + 1 > e(x − 1) (x − 1 > 0); M1 x(2 − e) > −(e + 1); A1 divide by negative 2 − e and reverse: x < (e + 1)/(e − 2); A1 1 < x < 5.18.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 2|eˣ − 3| < eˣ, giving the boundary values in exact form.
parts.working: M1 consider eˣ > 3: 2eˣ − 6 < eˣ, so eˣ < 6; M1 consider eˣ < 3: 6 − 2eˣ < eˣ, so eˣ > 2; A1 2 < eˣ < 6; M1 take ln; A1 ln 2 < x < ln 6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 9ˣ − 3ˣ⁺² + 18 ≥ 0, giving your answer in exact form.
parts.working: Let y = 3ˣ > 0: y² − 9y + 18 ≥ 0 (M1, M1). (y − 3)(y − 6) ≥ 0 (M1). So y ≤ 3 or y ≥ 6 (M1). Hence x ≤ 1 or x ≥ log₃ 6 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality |log₁₀ x − 1| > 0.5, giving your answers in exact form.
parts.working: log₁₀ x − 1 > 0.5 or log₁₀ x − 1 < −0.5 (M1). So log₁₀ x > 1.5 or log₁₀ x < 0.5 (M1). x > 10^1.5 = 10√10 or x < 10^0.5 = √10 (M1, A1). Domain x > 0 (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the inequality 5²ˣ − 6 × 5ˣ + 5 < 0, giving your answer in exact form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The equation e²ˣ − k eˣ + 4 = 0 has two distinct real roots in x, where k is a constant. Find the set of values of k.
parts.working: Let y = eˣ > 0: y² − ky + 4 = 0 must have two distinct positive roots (M1). Product 4 > 0 (always), sum k > 0 (M1). Discriminant k² − 16 > 0 (M1, A1 for k² > 16). So k > 4 (A1).

parts.label: a

parts.text: In a group of 200 students at a school in Lahore, 120 study Physics, 90 study Chemistry and 50 study both. A student is chosen at random. Given that the student studies Physics, find the probability that the student also studies Chemistry.

parts.label: b

parts.working: 11 outcomes contain at least one 5 M1; 2 of them total 8, so 2/11 A1

parts.answer: Not independent: P(X) × P(Y) = 0.175, which is not 0.15
parts.working: Independent events need P(X ∩ Y) = P(X) × P(Y) (M1). 0.7 × 0.25 = 0.175 ≠ 0.15, so they are not independent (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A is the event that a student plays cricket and B is the event that a student plays badminton. In a sports club in Karachi, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A′ ∩ B) = 0.12. Find P(A | B).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(A ∩ B).

parts.text: In a city, 2% of people have a certain infection. A screening test gives a positive result for 95% of people who have the infection and for 4% of people who do not. A person is chosen at random and tested. Find the probability that the result is positive.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the result is positive, find the probability that the person has the infection. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Comment briefly on what your answer to part (b) shows about using this test on its own.
parts.answer: Most people who test positive do not have the infection, so a positive result needs a further test
parts.working: B1 for a sensible comment referring to the answer to (b) being less than 0.5

parts.label: a
parts.text: For events A and B, P(A) = 0.3, P(B | A) = 0.6 and P(B | A′) = 0.2. Find P(B).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(A | B).

parts.text: A cricket team has probability 0.5 of winning the toss before a match. If it wins the toss, the probability that it wins the match is 0.65; if it loses the toss, the probability that it wins the match is 0.45. Find the probability that the team wins the match.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.label: a
parts.text: A card is chosen at random from 20 cards numbered 1 to 20. A is the event 'the number is a multiple of 3', B is the event 'the number is even' and C is the event 'the number is greater than 15'. Find P(A | B) and hence show that A and B are independent.

parts.working: Even numbers greater than 15: 16, 18, 20, so P(C | B) = 3/10 M1; P(C) = 5/20 = 1/4 ≠ 3/10, not independent A1

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: Events A and B satisfy P(A) = 0.45, P(B) = 0.36 and P(A | B) = 0.5. Find P(A ∩ B) and P(B | A).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State, with a calculation, whether A and B are independent.
parts.working: Compare P(A) × P(B) = 0.162 with P(A ∩ B) = 0.18 (M1). They differ, so A and B are not independent (A1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A factory in Sialkot makes footballs on three machines. Machine A makes 50% of the balls, B makes 30% and C makes 20%. The proportions of faulty balls are 2% from A, 3% from B and 5% from C. Find the probability that a randomly chosen ball is faulty.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A ball is found to be faulty. Find the probability that it was made by machine C. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Two balls are chosen at random, independently. Given that at least one of them is faulty, find the probability that both are faulty. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ali travels to college by bus or by bicycle. The probability that it rains on a given morning is 0.3. If it rains, the probability that he takes the bus is 0.8; if it does not rain, the probability that he takes the bus is 0.4. When he takes the bus, the probability that he is late is 0.25. parts.label: c

parts.label: a
parts.text: Events A and B are such that P(B) = 0.4, P(A | B) = 0.25 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.7. Find P(A ∩ B) and P(A).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(A′ | B′).

parts.text: Sara takes a driving test. The probability that she passes at the first attempt is 0.6. If she fails, she takes the test a second time, and the probability that she passes at the second attempt is 0.75. Draw a tree diagram to show this information.
parts.answer: First branch pass 0.6 / fail 0.4; after fail: pass 0.75 / fail 0.25

parts.label: b

parts.text: A biased coin, for which P(head) = 0.3, is tossed and a fair six-sided die is thrown. Find the probability of obtaining a head and a six.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: In Islamabad in spring, the probability that it rains on a Monday is 0.4. If it rains on Monday, the probability that it rains on Tuesday is 0.6; if it does not rain on Monday, the probability that it rains on Tuesday is 0.25. Find the probability that it rains on Tuesday.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that it rains on exactly one of the two days.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A bag contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. A ball is taken at random, its colour is noted and the ball is replaced. This is done twice. Find the probability of getting exactly one red ball.
