parts.working:
M1 total momentum remains zero
A1 48v = 2 × 6
A1 v = 0.25

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle A of mass m kg moving at 5 m s⁻¹ collides with a stationary particle B of mass 0.3 kg. After the collision A moves at 2 m s⁻¹ and B moves at 4.5 m s⁻¹, both in the original direction of A. Find m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two wooden blocks, of masses 0.6 kg and 0.9 kg, lie at rest on a smooth horizontal table with a compressed spring between them. The spring is released and the blocks move apart along the line of the spring. The 0.6 kg block moves off at 1.2 m s⁻¹. (a) Find the speed of the 0.9 kg block. (b) Find the total kinetic energy given to the blocks by the spring.
parts.working: (a) M1 total momentum before = 0; M1 0.6 × 1.2 = 0.9v; A1 v = 0.8 m s⁻¹ (opposite direction). (b) M1 ½ × 0.6 × 1.2² + ½ × 0.9 × 0.8²; A1 0.72 J

parts.label: a
parts.text: A rifle of mass 4 kg lies on a smooth horizontal surface and is free to recoil. A bullet of mass 0.02 kg is fired horizontally at 500 m s⁻¹ from the rifle. The rifle and the bullet were at rest before firing. (a) Find the recoil speed of the rifle. (b) Explain why the rifle moves backwards.
parts.answer: (a) 2.5 m s⁻¹ (in the opposite direction to the bullet); (b) total momentum is zero before firing, so it must be zero after: the bullet's forward momentum is balanced by the rifle's backward momentum.
parts.working: (a) M1 0.02 × 500 = 4v; A1 v = 2.5 m s⁻¹ backwards. (b) B1 total momentum is zero before and after (no external horizontal force); B1 equal and opposite momenta

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle P, of mass 0.4 kg, moves at 5 m s⁻¹ east on a smooth horizontal surface and hits particle Q, of mass 0.6 kg, which is moving towards it (west) with speed w m s⁻¹. After the collision P moves west at 1 m s⁻¹ and Q moves east at 2 m s⁻¹. (a) Find w. (b) Find the kinetic energy lost in the collision.
parts.working: (a) M1 take east as positive: 0.4 × 5 − 0.6w = 0.4(−1) + 0.6 × 2; M1 2 − 0.6w = 0.8; A1 w = 2. (b) M1 KE before = 6.2 J, after = 1.4 J; A1 loss = 4.8 J

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle P, of mass 0.25 kg, moves at 6 m s⁻¹ along a smooth horizontal floor and hits particle Q, of mass 0.5 kg, which is at rest. After the impact P rebounds with speed 2 m s⁻¹ along the same line. (a) Find the speed and direction of Q after the impact. (b) Find the magnitude of the impulse that acts on P.
parts.answer: (a) 4 m s⁻¹ in the direction of P's original motion; (b) 2 N s
parts.working: (a) M1 0.25 × 6 = 0.25(−2) + 0.5v; A1 v = 4 m s⁻¹. (b) M1 impulse = change in momentum of P = 0.25 × (6 − (−2)); A1 2 N s

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle A, of mass 2 kg, moves at 3 m s⁻¹ along a smooth horizontal line. Particle B, of mass 1 kg, is ahead of A and moves in the same direction at 1 m s⁻¹. A catches up with B and they collide directly. After the collision B moves at 4 m s⁻¹ in the same direction. Find the speed of A after the collision.
parts.working: M1 2 × 3 + 1 × 1 = 2v + 1 × 4 (momentum conserved, take the original direction as positive); A1 7 = 2v + 4, so v = 1.5 m s⁻¹

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle P of mass 3m moving with speed 2u collides with particle Q of mass m moving with speed u in the opposite direction. After the collision both particles move in the original direction of P, and the speed of Q is twice the speed of P. Find, in terms of u, the speeds of P and Q after the collision.
parts.working:
M1 6mu − mu = 3mv + m(2v)
A1 5mu = 5mv
A1 v = u for P
A1 2u for Q

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find, in terms of m and u, the loss of kinetic energy in the collision.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particles A, B and C, of masses 4 kg, 2 kg and 6 kg, lie in that order in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface, with B and C at rest. A is projected towards B with speed 3 m s⁻¹. After A collides with B, A moves on in the same direction with speed 1 m s⁻¹. Find the speed of B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B then collides with C and rebounds with speed 0.5 m s⁻¹. Find the speed of C.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A and B then collide and coalesce. Find the velocity of the combined particle and determine whether it will collide with C.
parts.answer: 0.5 m s⁻¹ towards C; no further collision with C
parts.working:
M1 4 × 1 − 2 × 0.5 = 6V
A1 V = 0.5 towards C
A1 0.5 < 1.5 so it never reaches C

parts.label: a
parts.text: A ball of mass 0.2 kg moves at 4 m s⁻¹ and strikes a smooth vertical wall at right angles. It rebounds from the wall at 2.5 m s⁻¹ along the same line. (a) Find the impulse exerted by the wall on the ball. (b) Find the kinetic energy lost by the ball in the impact.
parts.answer: (a) 1.3 N s (directed away from the wall); (b) 0.975 J
parts.working: (a) M1 taking the direction away from the wall as positive: impulse = 0.2 × (2.5 − (−4)) = 0.2 × 6.5; A1 1.3 N s. (b) M1 KE before = ½ × 0.2 × 16 = 1.6 J, after = ½ × 0.2 × 6.25 = 0.625 J; A1 loss = 0.975 J

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle A, of mass 2 kg, moves at 5 m s⁻¹ east along a smooth horizontal surface. Particle B, of mass 3 kg, moves towards A at 1 m s⁻¹ (west). The particles collide head on and coalesce. Find the velocity of the combined particle immediately after the collision, stating its direction.
parts.working: M1 taking east as positive: 2 × 5 + 3 × (−1) = (2 + 3)v; M1 7 = 5v; A1 v = 1.4 m s⁻¹; A1 the direction is east (positive)

parts.answer: (a) 0.6 m s⁻¹; (b) 3.42 J, which is 95% of the clay's initial KE

parts.text: Particle P, of mass 0.5 kg, moves at 4 m s⁻¹ and collides with a particle of mass 1.5 kg which is at rest. They coalesce. Find the percentage of the kinetic energy of P that is lost in the collision.
parts.working: M1 common speed = 0.5 × 4 / 2 = 1 m s⁻¹; M1 KE before = 4 J, KE after = ½ × 2 × 1 = 1 J; A1 loss = 3 J = 75% of the original KE of P

parts.label: a
parts.text: Wagon A, of mass 1500 kg, moves at 5 m s⁻¹ along a straight horizontal track and catches up with wagon B, of mass 500 kg, moving in the same direction at 1 m s⁻¹. The wagons couple together on impact. Find the kinetic energy lost in the collision.
parts.working: M1 momentum: 1500 × 5 + 500 × 1 = 2000V, so V = 4 m s⁻¹; M1 KE before = ½ × 1500 × 5² + ½ × 500 × 1² = 19 000 J, KE after = ½ × 2000 × 4² = 16 000 J; A1 loss = 3000 J

parts.working: (a) M1 2 × 3 + 4 × 1 = 2 × 1 + 4v; A1 v = 2 m s⁻¹. (b) M1 KE before = 9 + 2 = 11 J; M1 KE after = 1 + 8 = 9 J; A1 loss = 2 J

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particles of equal mass m are on a smooth horizontal surface. Particle A moves with speed u and collides with particle B, which is at rest. They coalesce. (a) Show that the common speed after the collision is u/2. (b) Show that the fraction of the original kinetic energy lost in the collision is ½.
parts.answer: (a) m u = 2m V so V = u/2; (b) KE before = ½mu²; KE after = ½ × 2m × (u/2)² = ¼mu²; loss = ¼mu², which is ½ of ½mu².
parts.working: (a) M1 mu = 2mV; A1 V = u/2. (b) M1 KE after = ¼mu²; A1 loss = ¼mu² = ½ × initial KE

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle P, of mass 0.3 kg, moves at 4 m s⁻¹ and hits particle Q, of mass 0.7 kg, which is at rest. The particles coalesce. Find the percentage of the initial kinetic energy of the system that is lost in the collision.
parts.working: M1 common speed = 0.3 × 4 / 1.0 = 1.2 m s⁻¹; M1 KE before = ½ × 0.3 × 4² = 2.4 J, KE after = ½ × 1.0 × 1.2² = 0.72 J; A1 loss = 1.68 J = 70% of 2.4 J

parts.label: a

parts.working:
M1 momentum: 10 = 2w + 3v
M1 energy: 25 − 14.4 = w² + 1.5v²
M1 substitute w = 5 − 1.5v
A1 3.75v² − 15v + 14.4 = 0 → v² − 4v + 3.84 = 0 (AG)

parts.label: b

A1 v = 2.4, w = 1.4

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle A of mass 1 kg moving at 6 m s⁻¹ collides with stationary particle B of mass 2 kg. After the collision A rebounds with speed 2 m s⁻¹ and B moves at 4 m s⁻¹. Show that momentum is conserved and that no kinetic energy is lost.
parts.working:
B1 momentum 6 before, −2 + 8 = 6 after
M1 KE before 18 J, after 2 + 16
A1 equal, so no loss

parts.label: b
parts.text: B then collides with a stationary particle C of mass m kg and they coalesce. The loss of kinetic energy in this collision is 12 J. Find m.

M1 KE after = 32/(2 + m)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle A, of mass 2m, moves at 3u on a smooth horizontal surface and collides directly with particle B, of mass m, which is at rest. They coalesce. Show that the kinetic energy lost in the collision is 3mu².
parts.answer: Common speed V: 2m × 3u = 3mV so V = 2u. KE before = ½ × 2m × 9u² = 9mu²; KE after = ½ × 3m × 4u² = 6mu²; loss = 3mu².
parts.working: M1 momentum: 6mu = 3mV, V = 2u; M1 KE before = 9mu²; M1 KE after = 6mu²; A1 loss = 3mu²

practice.subtopic: Loss of kinetic energy in collisions

parts.label: a
parts.text: A wooden block of mass M is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A bullet of mass m moves horizontally with speed u and becomes embedded in the block. Show that the fraction of the bullet's initial kinetic energy that is lost in the impact is M/(M + m). Hence find this fraction, as a percentage, when m = 0.02 kg and M = 1.98 kg.
parts.answer: Common speed V = mu/(M+m); KE after = ½(M+m)V² = ½m²u²/(M+m); fraction retained = m/(M+m), so fraction lost = M/(M+m). For m = 0.02 and M = 1.98: 1.98/2 = 0.99, i.e. 99%.
parts.working: M1 mu = (M + m)V; M1 KE after = ½ m²u²/(M + m); M1 fraction retained = m/(M + m); A1 fraction lost = M/(M + m); A1 99%

practice.subtopic: Loss of kinetic energy in collisions

parts.label: a
parts.text: Particle A, of mass 2m, moves at speed u on a smooth horizontal surface towards particle B, of mass m, which moves towards A at speed 2u. They collide and coalesce. (a) Show that the combined particle is at rest after the collision. (b) Find, in terms of m and u, the kinetic energy lost in the collision.
parts.answer: (a) Taking A's direction as positive: 2m u − m(2u) = 0 = 3mV, so V = 0. (b) KE before = ½ × 2m × u² + ½ × m × 4u² = 3mu²; KE after = 0; loss = 3mu².
parts.working: (a) M1 momentum before = 2mu − 2mu = 0; A1 combined particle at rest. (b) M1 KE before = mu² + 2mu² = 3mu²; A1 KE after = 0; A1 loss = 3mu²
